He has previously played for Dumbarton, Motherwell, Stenhousemuir, Ayr United, Walsall and Livingston. Devlin made his Scotland debut in 2024. ==Career== ===Motherwell=== Devlin signed for [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] in the summer of 2009, and broke into the first team during the [[2010–11 in Scottish football|2010–11 season]]. Devlin signed a pre-contract agreement with [[Scottish Premier League|SPL]] side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in March 2011. As part of the deal, [[Jordan Halsman]]'s loan deal at Dumbarton was extended until the end of the season,{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/d/dumbarton/9412723.stm |title=Motherwell agree deal for Dumbarton's Nicky Devlin |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 March 2011 |access-date=19 August 2012}} and Motherwell played a pre-season friendly against Dumbarton. Devlin officially joined Motherwell on 1 July 2011. Devlin was injured for most of the [[2011–12 in Scottish football|2011–12 season]], but came back at the start of 2012 and turned in some excellent performances for the [[Motherwell F.C. Reserve and Youth squads#Under 19s Team|Motherwell under-19]] team. On 29 March 2012, Devlin joined [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] on loan until the end of the season where he was awarded the Young Player of the Month award for April, his first full month at the club.{{cite news |url=http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2012/03/29/nicky-devlin-to-join-stenny/ |title=Nicky Devlin to join Stenny |publisher=Motherwell F.C |date=29 March 2012 |access-date=19 August 2012}} On 17 August 2012, Devlin re-joined [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on loan until January 2013,{{cite news |url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=4100 |title=Nicky returns to the rock |publisher=Dumbarton F.C. |date=17 August 2012 |access-date=17 August 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102123553/http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=4100 |archive-date=2 January 2013 }} which was subsequently extended for a further twenty-eight days.{{cite news |url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=4279 |title=Nicky Extends Stay |publisher=Dumbarton F.C. |date=3 January 2013 |access-date=3 January 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130128091645/http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=4279 |archive-date=28 January 2013 }} On 15 March 2013, Devlin was again farmed out on loan, re-joining Stenhousemuir till the end of the season.{{cite news |title=Devlin goes on loan to Stenhousemuir |url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/devlin-goes-on-loan-to-stenhousemuir/ |publisher=Scottish Football League |date=19 March 2013 |access-date=19 March 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411192136/http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/devlin-goes-on-loan-to-stenhousemuir/ |archive-date=11 April 2013 }} On 20 May 2013, after not making a single first-team appearance for Motherwell, Devlin was released by the club.{{cite news |title=Forthcoming squad changes |url=http://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2013/05/20/forthcoming-squad-changes/ |publisher=Motherwell FC |date=20 May 2013 |access-date=20 May 2013}} ===Stenhousemuir=== Upon being released by Motherwell, he was quickly signed on a permanent contract by Stenhousemuir, who he had two previous loan spells with, for the [[2013–14 in Scottish football|2013–14 season]].{{cite web |title=Stenhousemuir take first steps toward new season |url=http://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/local-sport/football/stenhousemuir-take-first-steps-toward-new-season-1-2972106 |publisher=Johnston Publishing Ltd |work=The released players |url=http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2014/05/12/1063/ |publisher=Stenhousemuir FC |last=McMenemy |first=Iain |date=12 May 2014 |access-date=26 July 2014}} ===Ayr United=== In July 2014, Devlin signed for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].{{cite web |title=New signings |url=http://www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk/new-signings-2/ |publisher=Ayr United F.C. |date=24 July 2014 |access-date=26 July 2014 |archive-date=8 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808072544/http://www.ayrunitedfc.co.uk/new-signings-2/ |url-status=dead }} He was made club captain on 19 May |url=https://planetradio.co.uk/west/local/news/nicky-devlin-leave-ayr-united/ |title=Nicky Devlin to leave Ayr United |work=Planet Radio |publisher=Bauer Radio Limited |date=11 May 2017 signed for [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]] in June 2017 on a two-year contract.{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40409515 |title=Nicky Devlin: Walsall sign Scottish right-back following Ayr United exit |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 June 2017 |access-date=26 June 2017}} He was offered a new contract by Walsall at the end of the 2018–19 season, however he opted to move back to Scotland.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48313315|title=Walsall: New Saddlers boss releases 11 players following relegation to League Two|date=17 May 2019|access-date=20 May 2019|publisher=BBC Sport}} ===Livingston=== In June 2019, Devlin signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48569408|title=Nicky Devlin: Livingston sign right-back after he rejects new Walsall deal|work=BBC Sport |date=8 June 2019 |access-date=2019-06-14}} Devlin played four seasons at Livingston, the latter two as team captain. ===Aberdeen=== Devlin confirmed on 22 May 2023 that he had agreed a deal to join fellow Premiership side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].{{Cite news |title=Devlin confirms move from Livingston to Aberdeen |language=en-GB |publisher=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65668932 Livingston defender Nicky Devlin on two-year deal|website=press and journal|date=June 2023 |access-date=2023-06-01}} Devlin won Premiership Player of the Month for October 2024, after the club went on Thelin and Nicky Devlin land monthly awards|first=Sean|last=Wallace|date=8 November 2024|work=The Press and Journal|access-date=25 November 2024}} ==International career== On 1 October 2024, he was '''Stephen Iain Kingsley''' (born 23 July 1994) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

He has previously played for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]], and [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]], as well as appearing for [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] and [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] on loan.

==Club career==

===Falkirk===
Aged 16, Kingsley made his first-team debut for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] on 12 April 2011 in a 2–1 win versus [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in the [[Scottish First Division]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_div_1/9454409.stm | title=Partick Thistle 1–2 Falkirk |publisher=BBC Sport | date=12 April 2011 | access-date=19 August 2011}}</ref> He sustained an injury in a [[2011–12 Scottish League Cup]] tie against [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] that kept him out of action for over three months. He returned to the starting line-up in a League Cup win against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. In March 2013, Kingsley signed a new contract with Falkirk.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=6339&Itemid=320 | title=Pressley Delight at Contract Extensions | publisher=Falkirk FC | date=4 March 2013 | accessdate=4 March 2013}}</ref> Kingsley made his 100th appearance for Falkirk on 5 April 2014, in a 5–0 victory over [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]]. He was also voted in to the SPFL Championship Team of the Year for season 2013–14.

===Swansea City===
On 30 June 2014, Kingsley signed for [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] on a three-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.swanseacity.com/news/article/stephen-kingsley-signs-1707898.aspx | title=Swans sign Falkirk youngster Kingsley | publisher=Swansea City A.F.C. | accessdate=30 June 2014 | archive-date=29 March 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200329025402/http://www.swanseacity.com/news/article/stephen-kingsley-signs-1707898.aspx | url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 18 February 2015, Kingsley joined [[Football League One|English League One]] side [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] on a month's emergency loan which was later extended until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31523397 |title=Stephen Kingsley: Yeovil Town sign Swansea City defender |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 February 2015 |access-date=18 February 2015 }}</ref> Kingsley played in numerous positions in his 12 appearances for the Glovers including [[Defender (association football)|left-back]], [[Defender (association football)|centre-back]] and [[Midfielder|midfield]], and received praise for his versatility from Yeovil boss [[Terry Skiverton]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.westerngazette.co.uk/Stephen-Kingsley-Mr-Versatile-Terry-Skiverton/story-26253430-detail/story.html |title=Stephen Kingsley is Mr Versatile for Terry Skiverton at Yeovil Town |work=westerngazette.co.uk |date=30 March 2015 |accessdate=7 May 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150720083358/http://www.westerngazette.co.uk/Stephen-Kingsley-Mr-Versatile-Terry-Skiverton/story-26253430-detail/story.html |archivedate=20 July 2015}}</ref> Yeovil were subsequently relegated to [[Football League Two|League Two]] at the end of the season and Kingsley returned to Swansea City.

Kingsley joined [[Football League One|English League One]] side [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] on an emergency loan in August 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34062988 |title=Crewe Alexandra: Liverpool winger Wilson & Swansea's Kingsley join |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 August 2015 |accessdate=6 May 2016 }}</ref> He made 12 appearances for them before returning to Swansea after the emergency loan expired in November.

He made his Swansea City debut in their [[FA Cup]] 3–2 defeat away to [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]], on 10 January 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35216450 |title=Oxford United 3–2 Yeovil Town |publisher=BBC Sport |date=10 January 2016 |accessdate=6 May 2016 }}</ref> He made his [[Premier League]] debut on 2 March 2016 in Swansea's 2–1 victory away to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35647629 |title=Arsenal 1–2 Swansea City |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 March 2016 |accessdate=6 May 2016 }}</ref>

===Hull City===
Kingsley moved to [[EFL Championship|Championship]] club [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] in August 2017 for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41029792 |title=Stephen Kingsley: Hull City sign Swansea City defender on three-year deal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 August 2017 |accessdate=23 August 2017}}</ref> He was released by Hull at the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref name = hearts>{{cite web|title=Stephen Kingsley joins Hearts as free agent|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54440582 |publisher=BBC |website=BBC Sport|date=6 October 2020|accessdate=6 October 2020}}</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===
Kingsley signed a one-year contract with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on 6 October 2020.<ref name = hearts/> He played and scored for Hearts in the [[2020 Scottish Cup Final]], which finished 3–3 after extra time, but his effort in the subsequent [[penalty shootout (association football)|penalty shootout]] was saved by [[Conor Hazard]] as Hearts lost 4–3 on penalties.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celtic 3–3 Hearts|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55291058|website=BBC Sport |date=19 December 2020 |accessdate=20 December 2020}}</ref>

On 21 January 2021, Kingsley signed an 18-month contract extension with Hearts, keeping him at the club until the end of the [[2021–22 Scottish Premiership|2021–22 season]]. He further extended his Hearts stay in January 2022, signing a three-and-a-half-year contract and keeping him at the club until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kingsley signs long-term contract {{!}} Heart Of Midlothian Football Club|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/kingsley-signs-long-term-contract|access-date=13 January 2022|website=www.heartsfc.co.uk}}</ref> He then further extended his contract on 6 August 2024 with a new three-year contract until the summer of 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kingsley extends contract to 2027 – Hearts |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/kingsley-extends-contract-to-2027 |access-date=6 August 2024 |website=www.heartsfc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>

Kingsley quickly became known as an efficient taker of the [[direct free kick]], scoring several long-range strikes for Hearts since joining.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stephen Kingsley explains how he has mastered the art of free-kicks for Hearts|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/stephen-kingsley-explains-how-he-has-mastered-the-art-of-free-kicks-for-hearts-3474669|access-date=9 January 2022|website=www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com|date=29 November 2021 |language=en}}</ref> He scored what proved to be the match-winning goal in the semi-final of the [[2021–22 Scottish Cup]] – an [[Edinburgh derby]] against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] – from a 30-yard free kick, albeit assisted with a [[wall pass]] from [[Liam Boyce]].<ref>[https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/stephen-kingsley-admits-hearts-free-23714262 Stephen Kingsley admits Hearts free-kick change of plan that led to stunning Hampden winner vs Hibs], Ross Pilcher, ''Football Scotland'', 17 April 2022. Retrieved 18 April 2022</ref><ref>[https://news.stv.tv/sport/stephen-kingsley-reveals-set-piece-plan-after-netting-hampden-winner Kingsley reveals set-piece plan after netting Hampden winner], Andy Coyle, ''STV News'', 16 April 2022. Retrieved 18 April 2022</ref>

==International career==
In April 2012 Kingsley was called up to the [[Scotland national under-18 football team|Scotland under-18]] squad for two games against Serbia in [[Belgrade]] on the 17th and 19th of the month. He played 90 minutes in the first game, which ended 1–1, and 60 minutes in the second game, where Scotland won 4–1. In season 2012–13 he appeared for [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland under-19]]s against [[Germany national under-19 football team|Germany]] and the [[Netherlands national under-19 football team|Netherlands]]. He was selected for the squad for the [[2014 UEFA European Under-19 Football Championship qualification]] matches in October, playing in the third game against [[Switzerland national under-19 football team|Switzerland]]. This was followed in March with an appearance in the friendly match against [[Sweden men's national under-19 football team|Sweden]]. In May he played in two of the Elite qualifying round games in Belgium against [[Belgium national under-19 football team|Belgium]] and [[Georgia national under-19 football team|Georgia]]. In March 2015, Kingsley made his [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] debut in a 2–1 win against [[Hungary national under-21 football team|Hungary]]. This was followed up with four appearances for the side against [[France national under-21 football team|France]] twice, Northern Ireland and [[Iceland national under-21 football team|Iceland]] in their Euro Championship Qualifying group.

On 20 May 2016, Kingsley received his first call-up to the [[Scotland national football team]] for their friendlies against [[Italy national football team|Italy]] and [[France national football team|France]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36339859 |title=Scotland call up Stephen Kingsley and Jack Hamilton |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 May 2016 |accessdate=23 May 2016}}</ref> He made his Scotland debut as a substitute in a 3–0 defeat against France, on 4 June 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36404268 |title=France 3–0 Scotland |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 June 2016 |accessdate=5 June 2016 }}</ref>

Kingsley was recalled to the national team squad in September 2022 as a replacement for the injured [[Kieran Tierney]] and [[Scott McKenna]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/hearts-duo-barrie-mckay-and-stephen-kingsley-called-up-to-scotland-squad-as-trio-drop-out |title=Hearts duo Barrie McKay and Stephen Kingsley called up to Scotland squad as trio drop out |website=STV News |first=Peter |last=Cassidy |date=25 September 2022 |accessdate=28 September 2022}}</ref> He appeared as a substitute in a goalless draw with [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] that secured a promotion for Scotland in the [[UEFA Nations League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/outstanding-ryan-porteous-debut-helps-scotland-secure-euro-2024-play-off-3858972 |title=Outstanding Ryan Porteous debut helps Scotland secure Euro 2024 play-off |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |first=Phil |last=Johnson |date=27 September 2022 |accessdate=28 September 2022}}</ref>

'''Stuart John Findlay''' (born 14 September 1995) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} club  [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 June 2025 |title=Hearts confirm Stuart Findlay signing: Contract and what Derek McInnes said |url=https://www.heartsstandard.co.uk/news/25231032.hearts-complete-stuart-findlay-signing-derek-mcinnes-said/ |access-date=19 June 2025 |website=Hearts Standard |language=en}}</ref> He has previously represented the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]] at senior level.

==Early life==

Stuart John Findlay was born on September 14, 1995 in the [[Glasgow]] suburb of [[Baillieston]].<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title=Birth registers|url=https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/record-results/102278273969a78c1e801e8 |website=Scotland's People |location=Edinburgh, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=4 March 2026}}</ref> He attended [[Trinity High School, Rutherglen|Trinity High School]]<ref name=intake/> in [[Rutherglen]] and was in the same year group as fellow Celtic youth team player [[Dom Thomas]], who broke through as a professional with [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] and was later a teammate at [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref name=Reformer>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/local-news/trinity-high-school-awards-2631354 |title=Trinity High School awards |date=16 July 2008|accessdate=20 June 2017 |newspaper=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]/[[Rutherglen Reformer]]}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Celtic===
Findlay came through the [[youth system]] at [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], making his first-team debut in a friendly against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]].<ref name=intake>{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/stuart-findlay-celtic-youth-player-and-one-of-original-intake-in-2009-x.17784903|title=Stuart Findlay: Celtic youth player and one of original intake in 2009|newspaper=The Herald|date=4 June 2012|accessdate=6 March 2014}}</ref> He also captained Celtic at under-17 level,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.celticnewsnow.com/news/who-is-stuart-findlay/47890|title=Who is Stuart Findlay|publisher=Celtic News Now|date=23 May 2012|accessdate=6 March 2014}}</ref> and featured regularly for the Development side, taking part in the [[UEFA Youth League]] and the [[Premier League International Cup|English Premier League International Cup]].<ref name="killie" />

====Greenock Morton (loan)====
In January 2014, Findlay signed for [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/morton/articles/2014/01/21/485627-riordan-to-train-with-morton-as-peciar-leaves/|title=Riordan to train with Morton as Peciar leaves|newspaper=Greenock Telegraph|first=Jonathan|last=Mitchell|date=21 January 2014|accessdate=2 February 2014}}</ref> He made his debut on 1 February in a 1–1 draw against league leaders [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], turning in an impressive performance.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://spfl.co.uk/championship/fixture/3635109/|title=Falkirk 1–1 Morton|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=1 February 2014|accessdate=1 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lennon delighted with Findlay's loan move to Morton|url=http://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/morton/articles/2014/02/05/487425-lennon-delighted-with-findlays-loan-move-to-morton/|newspaper=Greenock Telegraph|accessdate=9 July 2015|date=5 February 2014}}</ref> Morton spent most of the season in an unsuccessful struggle against relegation, but Findlay continued to show promise. Morton lost 2–1 away at [[Raith Rovers]] on 15 March, but Findlay's pace and positional sense restricted Raith's goalscoring chances, and his overall performance was described as showing "composure beyond his years".<ref>{{cite web|title=Spence double earns valuable victory|url=http://www.raithrovers.net/13484/raith-rovers-2-1-greenock-morton-3.htm|publisher=Raith Rovers F.C. |accessdate=9 July 2015|date=15 March 2014}}</ref> His spell at Morton ended on an embarrassing note, however, his side losing 10–2 against [[Hamilton Accies]] in their last game of the season, including a Findlay [[own goal]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Crawford|first=Kenny|title=Hamilton 10–2 Morton|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27168757|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=9 July 2015|date=3 May 2014}}</ref>

====Dumbarton (loan)====
On 16 January 2015, Findlay joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on loan until the end of the [[2014–15 in Scottish football|2014–15 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=New face at the rock|url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=1679|publisher=Dumbarton F.C.|last=Findlay|first=Alan|date=16 January 2015|accessdate=16 January 2015}}</ref> He impressed immediately, and was named the club's player of the month for February.<ref name="dbr">{{cite web|title=Stuart hopes to impress Celts with Sons displays|url=http://www.dumbartonreporter.co.uk/sport/football/articles/2015/03/20/527790-stuart-hopes-to-impress-celts-with-sons-displays/|newspaper=Dumbarton Reporter|accessdate=9 July 2015|date=20 March 2015}}</ref> He was noted for his composure with the ball, often carrying the ball out of defence with ease.<ref name="dbr"/> Findlay himself pointed out that "coming through at Celtic it is in their philosophy that they want to play out from the back, they want their defenders to be good on the ball."<ref name="dbr" /> His form also saw him named in the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] squad for a friendly with [[Hungary national under-21 football team|Hungary]] in March.<ref name="dbr" /> He left the club at the end of his loan deal, having made 15 appearances and twice been the recipient of the player of the month award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=1754|title=Baxter Ramsay Player of the Month|publisher=Dumbarton F.C.|date=9 March 2015 |access-date=31 August 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=1838|title=Baxter Ramsay Player of the Month|publisher=Dumbarton F.C.|date=30 April 2015 |access-date=31 August 2022}}</ref>

====Kilmarnock (loan)====
On 9 July 2015, it was confirmed that Findlay was going out on loan to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] for the [[2015–16 Scottish Premiership|2015–16 season]].<ref name="killie">{{cite web|last=Henderson|first=Mark|title=Stuart Findlay heads on loan to Kilmarnock|url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/8586|publisher=Celtic F.C.|accessdate=9 July 2015|date=9 July 2015}}</ref> On 1 August 2015, Findlay made his Kilmarnock debut in a 4–0 defeat against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], in which he featured for the entire 90 minutes.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kilmarnock vs. Dundee |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/08/01/scotland/premier-league/kilmarnock-fc/dundee-fc/2047248/ |publisher=Soccerway |date=1 August 2015 |accessdate=8 July 2016}}</ref>

===Newcastle United===
Findlay joined [[Football League Championship]] side [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] on 8 July 2016, following his release from Celtic.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Magpies Sign Young Duo |url=http://www.nufc.co.uk/articles/20160708/magpies-sign-young-duo_2281670_5705417 |publisher=Newcastle United F.C. |date=8 July 2016 |accessdate=8 July 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for Newcastle in an [[FA Cup]] tie against [[Birmingham City]] on 18 January 2017.<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38579227|title=Newcastle 3-1 Birmingham|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 January 2017|accessdate=18 January 2017}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
In August 2017, Findlay returned to Kilmarnock on loan from Newcastle.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Player Announcement: Stuart Findlay |url=http://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/Article?id=6096 |publisher=Kilmarnock F.C. |date=25 August 2017 |accessdate=25 August 2017}}</ref> He made 36 appearances for the club during the [[2017–18 in Scottish football|2017–18 season]], then signed permanently with the [[Rugby Park]] outfit in July 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44712419 |title=Kilmarnock: Bournemouth's Mikael Ndjoli and Newcastle's Stuart Findlay sign up |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 July 2018 |accessdate=4 July 2018}}</ref> On 23 September 2018, he scored a [[Last-minute goal|last-minute winner]] in a [[2018–19 Scottish Premiership|league fixture]] at home to former club Celtic, giving Killie a 2–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45538080 |title=Kilmarnock 2–1 Celtic |publisher=BBC Sport |first=Jamie |last=Lyall |date=23 September 2018 |accessdate=24 September 2018}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Union===
On 25 February 2021, Findlay moved over to the United States, to join [[Major League Soccer]] club [[Philadelphia Union]] for an undisclosed fee on a two-year deal, with the option to extend a further year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Philadelphia Union Sign Center Back Stuart Findlay |url=https://www.philadelphiaunion.com/post/2021/02/25/philadelphia-union-sign-center-back-stuart-findlay |access-date=25 February 2021 |publisher=Philadelphia Union |date=25 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=Stuart Findlay joins Philadelphia Union
|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/stuart-findlay-joins-philadelphia-union/ |access-date=25 February 2021 |publisher=Kilmarnock F.C. |date=25 February 2021}}</ref>
He made his debut on 15 April 2021, coming off the bench in the side's 4–0 home win against [[Deportivo Saprissa]] in the [[CONCACAF Champions League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phillysoccerpage.net/2021/04/14/match-report-philadelphia-union-4-0-deportivo-saprissa/|title=Match report: Philadelphia Union 4-0 Deportivo Saprissa|publisher=The Philly Soccer Page|first=Nick|last=Fishman|date=14 April 2021|access-date=24 April 2021}}</ref>
27 June 2021, he made his first start for Philadelphia Union away against [[Chicago Fire FC|Chicago Fire]] in a 3–3 draw, also his first appearance in [[Major League Soccer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://phillysoccerpage.net/2021/06/26/match-report-chicago-fire-3-3-philadelphia-union/|title=Match Report: Chicago Fire 3-3 Philadelphia Union|publisher=The Philly Soccer Page|first=Mike|last=Servedio|date=26 June 2021|access-date=9 July 2021}}</ref>

===Oxford United===
On 19 July 2022, Findlay signed for [[EFL League One]] club [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] for an undisclosed fee on a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oufc.co.uk/news/2022/july/stuart-findlay-joins-oxford-united/|title=Stuart Findlay Joins Oxford United |publisher=Oxford United F.C. |first=|last=|date=19 July 2022|access-date=19 July 2022}}</ref>  He made his debut in the first league game of the season, a 1–0 away defeat to [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.oufc.co.uk/matches/fixtures/first-team/202223/july/derby-county-vs-oxford-united-on-30-jul-22/ |title=REPORT Derby County 1 Oxford United 0 |date=30 July 2022 |publisher=Oxford United F.C. |first=Chris |last=Williams |access-date=31 August 2022}}</ref> and scored his first goal for the club in a 5–0  victory over [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]] in the [[EFL Trophy]] group stage on 30 August 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/sport/20860743.oxford-united-player-ratings-win-leyton-orient-papa-johns-trophy |title=Oxford United player ratings for win over Leyton Orient in Papa John's Trophy |first=James |last=Roberts |date=31 August 2022 |newspaper=Oxford Mail |access-date=31 August 2022}}</ref>.

====Kilmarnock (loan)====

Findlay was loaned to Kilmarnock for the beginning of the [[2023-24 Scottish Premiership|2023-24 season]];<ref>{{cite web |last=Delaney |first=James |date=14 July 2023 |title=Kilmarnock secure Stuart Findlay return as Scotland cap agrees loan move from Oxford United |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/kilmarnock-secure-stuart-findlay-return-as-scotland-cap-agrees-loan-move-from-oxford-united |accessdate=14 July 2023 |website=STV News}}</ref> he was then loaned in for a further season the following June.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/sport/24366286.stuart-findlay-rejoins-kilmarnock-loan-oxford-united/ |title=Stuart Findlay rejoins Kilmarnock on loan from Oxford United |first=Liam |last=Rice |date=4 June 2024 |newspaper=Oxford Mail |access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref>

====Heart of Midlothian (loan)====

On 19 June 2025, [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] announced they had signed Findlay on a one-year loan, with a view to making the move permanent at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Findlay joins Jambos on loan – Hearts |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/findlay-joins-jambos-on-loan |access-date=19 June 2025 |publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C. |language=en}}</ref> In joining Hearts, Findlay reunited with his former Kilmarnock manager [[Derek McInnes]]; who himself had just agreed to join the Edinburgh club.

===Heart of Midlothian===

In January 2026, Findlay agreed to join Hearts permanently, on a two-year deal, when his contract with Oxford United expired in July 2026.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date=7 January 2026 |title=Findlay to sign permanent deal |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/findlay-to-sign-permanent-deal|website=Heart of Midlothian F.C. |location=Edinburgh, Scotland |publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C. |access-date=4 March 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Findlay was first called into the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] squad in November 2012 by coach [[Ricky Sbragia]] for a friendly against [[Portugal national under-21 football team|Portugal]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/8231582/|title=Stuart Findlay and Marcus Fraser have been called into the Scotland U21 squad|publisher=Sky Sports|date=7 November 2012|accessdate=1 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fitbastats.com/scotlandu21/player.php?playerid=547 |title=Scotland U21 profile |publisher=Fitbastats.com|accessdate=20 June 2017}}</ref> His 13th and final [[Cap (sports)|cap]] at this age level was in October 2015 against [[France national under-21 football team|France]] at [[Pittodrie Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/international-matches/?mid=150913|title=Scotland 1-2 France|publisher=Scottish FA|accessdate=22 March 2018}}</ref>

Findlay received his first call-up to the senior [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad in March 2019 for games against [[Kazakhstan national football team|Kazakhstan]] and [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47604868 |title=Scotland: Andy Robertson to miss Kazakhstan clash as trio also pull out |date=17 March 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |accessdate=18 March 2019}}</ref> He earned his first full international cap on 13 October 2019 in a 6–0 win over San Marino at [[Hampden Park]], in which he played the full 90 minutes and scored Scotland's 5th goal.<ref name="BBCScotSanMar">{{cite news |last1=Lamont |first1=Alasdair |title=Scotland 6–0 San Marino |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49949350 |accessdate=13 October 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 October 2019}}</ref>

'''Alexander Clark''' (born 26 June 1992) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

After playing youth football with [[Hamilton Academical F.C. Reserves and Academy|Hamilton Academical]] and [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], Clark began his senior career in the 2011–12 season on loan at [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]]. He also had two loan spells at [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] before becoming a St Johnstone regular after making his debut for them in 2015. He was part of the St Johnstone side that won both domestic cups during the [[2020–21 in Scottish football|2020–21]] season. Clark left St Johnstone after the 2021–22 season and signed for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in September 2022.

Clark made his senior international debut for Scotland in October 2023, aged 31.

==Early life==
Alexander Clark was born 26 June 1992 in [[Glasgow]],<ref name="Soccerway">{{cite web |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/alexander-clark/164466/ |title=Z. Clark: Summary |website=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group |access-date=15 November 2023}}</ref> and raised in [[Clydebank]].<ref name="star21">{{cite news |url=https://www.clydebankpost.co.uk/news/19569394.john-paul-mcginn-clydebanks-footballing-heroes-star-austria/ |title=John and Paul McGinn: Clydebank's footballing heroes star against Austria |first=Darren |last=Gibson |newspaper=Clydebank Post |date=9 September 2021 |access-date=15 November 2023}}</ref>

==Club career==
===St Johnstone===
Clark started his career in the youth sides at [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] and then [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Clark delighted to get clearance to play|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/st-johnstones-clark-delighted-to-get-clearance-to-play/|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|last=Stewart|first=Craig|date=1 November 2013|access-date=2 August 2014|archive-date=28 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150928205211/http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/st-johnstones-clark-delighted-to-get-clearance-to-play/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 4 July 2011, Clark joined [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]] on loan ahead of the 2011–12 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Elgin bring in goalkeeper|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/elgin-bring-in-goalkeeper/|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=4 July 2011|access-date=2 August 2014|archive-date=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714114841/http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/elgin-bring-in-goalkeeper/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 17 October 2013, Clark signed for [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] on loan until 1 January 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/permalink.php?id=434160153332839&story_fbid=534885323260321|title=Queens Loyal|website=www.facebook.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Doonhamers call for Clark|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/doonhamers-call-for-clark/|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=18 October 2013|access-date=2 August 2014|archive-date=22 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022221417/http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/doonhamers-call-for-clark/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut on 19 October 2013, in a 2–1 defeat against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Keeper Zander Clark happy with his debut for Queen of the South|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/keeper-zander-clark-happy-debut-2487076|work=Daily Record|last=McNair|first=Andrew|date=24 October 2013|access-date=2 August 2014}}</ref> On 14 January 2014, the loan was extended until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bob McHugh: Motherwell striker joins Queen of the South on loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25725191|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 January 2014|access-date=2 August 2014}}</ref>

On 14 May 2014, Clark signed a new two-year contract with St Johnstone.<ref>{{cite web|title=NEW TWO YEAR DEAL FOR ZANDER|url=http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/newsitemsdetail.php?param=3000|publisher=St Johnstone F.C.|date=14 May 2014|access-date=2 August 2014|archive-date=8 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808043216/http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/newsitemsdetail.php?param=3000|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 25 July 2014, Queen of the South announced that Clark had returned to the club on loan for the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zander Clark Rejoins|url=http://www.qosfc.com/new_newsview.aspx?newsid=2402|publisher=Queen of the South F.C.|date=25 July 2014|access-date=2 August 2014|archive-date=25 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140725194938/http://www.qosfc.com/new_newsview.aspx?newsid=2402|url-status=dead}}</ref> Queens announced on 28 May 2015 that Clark was returning to St Johnstone.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.qosfc.com/new_newsview.aspx?newsid=2821|title=QosFC: Player Update|website=www.qosfc.com|access-date=27 September 2015|archive-date=28 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150528181007/http://www.qosfc.com/new_newsview.aspx?newsid=2821|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Clark made his first appearance for St Johnstone on 26 September 2015, coming on as a substitute in a 2–1 win against Dundee United.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34299442 |title=St Johnstone 2–1 Dundee Utd |publisher=BBC Sport |first=Paul |last=Mitchell |date=26 September 2015 |access-date=27 September 2015}}</ref> It was announced shortly afterwards that Clark had signed a new contract with St Johnstone, due to run until the summer of 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34473153 |title=St Johnstone: Zander Clark extends contract after debut|publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 October 2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref>

In July 2017 he was taken to hospital following a head injury in a friendly match against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40620402 |title=St Johnstone's Zander Clark taken to hospital during win over Sunderland |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 July 2017 |access-date=4 February 2019}}</ref> He was released from hospital after being diagnosed with a concussion.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40623593 |title=St Johnstone's Zander Clark is out of hospital after picking up knock against Sunderland|publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 July 2017 |access-date=4 February 2019}}</ref>

Clark was suggested as a possible candidate for the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] international squad during the 2018–19 season, particularly when he kept five consecutive clean sheets in the autumn<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/international/764591/scotland-coach-peter-grant-defends-decision-to-ignore-st-johnstones-in-form-keeper-zander-clark/ |title=Scotland coach Peter Grant defends decision to ignore St Johnstone's in-form keeper Zander Clark |first=Ian |last=Roache |date=14 November 2018 |access-date=4 February 2019 |work=The Courier |publisher=DC Thomson}}</ref>
and also after a good performance in a 2–0 home defeat against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in early February.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47109888 |title=Zander Clark: St Johnstone goalkeeper earns plaudits in Celtic defeat |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 February 2019 |access-date=4 February 2019}}</ref> Later in February 2019 he suffered a hamstring injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47294793 |title=Zander Clark: St Johnstone goalkeeper expected back sooner from hamstring injury |publisher=BBC Sport |date=19 February 2019 |access-date=19 February 2019}}</ref>

During a [[2020–21 Scottish Cup#Quarter-finals|Scottish Cup quarter-final]] against the Scottish champions [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in April 2021, Clark assisted in St Johnstone's 122nd-minute goal to take the game into a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]]. Having come up the field for a corner, Clark flicked on [[Liam Craig]]'s cross, and the ball was turned into the goal by [[Chris Kane (footballer, born 1994)|Chris Kane]].<ref name="SCQF">{{cite news|first=Andrew|last=Southwick|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56789585|title=Rangers 1-1 St Johnstone (St Johnstone win 4-2 on penalties)|work=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=25 April 2021|accessdate=25 April 2021}}</ref> In the shoot-out itself, Clark saved attempts from [[James Tavernier]] and [[Kemar Roofe]] as St Johnstone won 4–2 to progress to the semi-finals.<ref name="SCQF"/> They went on to win the trophy, with Clark keeping a clean sheet in [[2021 Scottish Cup Final|the final]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/may/22/st-johnstone-hibernian-scottish-cup-final-match-report|title=St Johnstone complete dream double after beating Hibs to win Scottish Cup|author=PA Media|date=22 May 2021|work=The Guardian}}</ref> (as he had in the [[2021 Scottish League Cup Final (February)|League Cup Final]] three months earlier).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/feb/28/livingston-st-johnstone-scottish-league-cup-final-match-report|title=St Johnstone sink Livingston to claim their first Scottish League Cup|last=Murray|first=Ewan|date=28 February 2021|work=The Guardian|accessdate=21 March 2022}}</ref>

Clark left St Johnstone in June 2022,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/20269165.st-johnstone-set-snap-sam-walker-kilmarnock-zander-clark-replacement/|title=St Johnstone set to snap up Sam Walker from Kilmarnock as Zander Clark replacement|website=HeraldScotland |date=11 July 2022 }}</ref> and was linked with transfers to [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and English club [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/zander-clark-handed-transfer-timeline-27369294|title=Zander Clark to Dundee United ramps up as Jack Ross pushes for goalkeeper|first=Scott|last=Burns|date=30 June 2022|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===
On 2 September 2022, Clark joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on a three-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zander Clark joins Hearts {{!}} Heart Of Midlothian Football Club |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/zander-clark-joins-hearts |access-date=2 September 2022 |website=www.heartsfc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62771902|title=Hearts sign former St Johnstone goalkeeper Clark|work=BBC Sport |date=2 September 2022 }}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 24 December 2022, coming on as a substitute after [[Craig Gordon]] broke his leg.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64096288|title=Hearts' Gordon to miss season after leg break|work=BBC Sport |date=26 December 2022 }}</ref>

Clark himself was injured ahead of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-to-assess-zander-clark-injury-after-taking-no-chances-with-goalkeeper-in-dunfermline-friendly-4212557|title=Hearts to assess Zander Clark injury after taking no chances with goalkeeper in Dunfermline friendly|date=9 July 2023|website=The Scotsman}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/23646392.hearts-await-update-zander-clark-pre-season-injury/|title=Hearts await update on Zander Clark pre-season injury|date=10 July 2023|website=The Herald}}</ref> As of 12 October 2023, he had the highest save percentage in the Scottish Premiership during the [[2023–24 Scottish Premiership|2023–24]] season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c2j97ved585o|title=Stopper Clark leads the way|date=12 October 2023|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Clark lost his first-team place in the 2024–25 season,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/zander-clark-why-i-stayed-at-hearts-despite-what-social-media-said-4961101|title=Zander Clark: Why I stayed at Hearts despite what social media said|date=27 January 2025|website=Edinburgh News}}</ref> but in January 2025 signed a new contract with the club until 2027.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/zander-commits-future-to-hearts|title=Zander commits future to Hearts|website=www.heartsfc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c1dg34g9lxzo|title=Hearts: Zander Clark signs new deal|date=15 January 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 10 January 2026, Clark joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk/news/2026/january/10/rovers-land-scotland-international-keeper-zander-clark-on-loan/|title=Rovers land Scotland international keeper Zander Clark on loan|website=www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk|date=10 January 2026|accessdate=11 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c89qg0kj4xqo|title=Zander Clark: Hearts & Scotland goalkeeper joins Doncaster Rovers on loan|date=10 January 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==International career==
Clark received his first call-up to the senior [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad in August 2021 for games against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]], [[Moldova national football team|Moldova]] and [[Austria national football team|Austria]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58317930 |title=Scotland: Zander Clark, Liam Kelly & Lewis Ferguson called up for World Cup qualifiers |date=24 August 2021 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=24 August 2021 |publisher=BBC}}</ref><ref name="star21"/> He earned his second call up in November 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59131721|title=Stoke's Brown 'buzzing' at Scotland call|work=BBC Sport |date=2 November 2021 }}</ref> He pulled out of the Scotland squad in June 2022<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/3382341/st-johnstone-goalkeeper-zander-clark-scotland-squad-ireland/|title=St Johnstone goalkeeper Zander Clark drops out of Scotland squad for Ireland match|first=Eric|last=Nicolson|date=10 June 2022|work=The Courier}}</ref> as he was due to get married.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.leeds-live.co.uk/sport/leeds-united/leeds-united-news-liam-cooper-24194877 |title=Leeds United news as Liam Cooper excused from Scotland squad as Arsenal join race for Whites man |website=Leeds Live |date=10 June 2022 |accessdate=20 July 2022 |first=Danny |last=Bloomer}}</ref>

Clark was recalled to the Scotland squad in March 2023, as he played regularly for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] following an injury to [[Craig Gordon]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64938719 |title=Scotland : Zander Clark & Angus Gunn named in squad for Spain & Cyprus games |website=BBC Sport |date=14 March 2023 |accessdate=14 March 2023}}</ref> He made his international debut in a [[friendly match|friendly]] against [[France national football team|France]] on 17 October 2023, aged 31.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-goalkeeper-zander-clark-ready-to-end-the-prolonged-wait-to-fulfil-a-lifelong-dream-4366813|title=Hearts keeper Zander Clark ready to end the prolonged wait to fulfil a lifelong dream|date=11 October 2023|website=Edinburgh News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=601758&lid=1|title=Zander Clark | Scotland | Scottish FA|website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67061897 |title=France 4-1 Scotland: Star-studded hosts inflict heavy defeat on makeshift Scots |website=BBC Sport |date=17 October 2023 |accessdate=17 October 2023}}</ref>

He was called up to Scotland's provisional squad for [[UEFA Euro 2024]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cyxxlrrlz3vo|title=Euro 2024: Scotland call up Doak, McCrorie and Forrest|date=22 May 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

'''Blair Thomas Spittal''' (born 19 December 1995) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a midfielder for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. He has previously played for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].

==Early life and career==
Blair began playing for Erskine Boys Club and from there moved to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. He spent two years there before joining [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]'s under-17 side.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/spittal-gets-placed-on-queens-park-production-line-of-talent/|title=Spittal the latest to shine at Hampden|last=Stewart|first=Craig|website=SPFL|date=16 August 2013|accessdate=16 August 2014}}</ref> He attended [[Park Mains High School]] in Erskine.

==Club career==

===Queen's Park===
At the age of 16 years old, Blair made his debut for Queen's Park away to [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] on 17 November 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.queensparkfc.co.uk/?page_id=1666|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140816193201/http://www.queensparkfc.co.uk/?page_id=1666|url-status=dead|archivedate=16 August 2014|title=Blair Spittal|website=The Queen's Park Football Club|accessdate=16 August 2014}}</ref> He went on to make a total of 18 appearances that season,<ref name="Soccerway">{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/blair-spittal/268117/|title=B. SPITTAL|website=Soccerway|accessdate=16 August 2014}}</ref> scoring his only goal in a 5–3 win away to [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21680134|title=Elgin City 3–5 Queen's Park|website=BBC Sport|date=5 March 2013|access-date=16 August 2014}}</ref>

The following season, he established himself as a first team regular, making 41 appearances and scoring 12 goals in the process.<ref name="Soccerway"/> This successful form saw him pursued by both of [[Dundee]]'s [[Scottish Premiership]] clubs. Having agreed terms with both sides, he opted to join his ex-Queen's Park teammates [[Aidan Connolly]] and [[Andrew Robertson (footballer)|Andrew Robertson]] at [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], over city rivals [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27815280|title=Dundee United sign Blair Spittal from Queen's Park|website=BBC Sport|date=12 June 2014|access-date=16 August 2014}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
Having spent the first two games of the season as an unused substitute, Blair made his debut for the Terrors from the bench in the club's third game of the season away to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on 16 August 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28716867|title=Celtic 6 1 Dundee Utd|last=Lamont|first=Alasdair|website=BBC Sport|date=16 August 2014|access-date=16 August 2014}}</ref> Blair played in the United squad that faced relegation from the Premiership in 2016. He was part of the side that won the [[2016–17 Scottish Challenge Cup]] as he played in the earlier third and fourth rounds, as well as the quarter-final. However, he missed out on both the semi-finals and the final due to injury.

===Partick Thistle===
Blair joined Scottish Premiership club [[Partick Thistle]] on a two-year contract on 15 June 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Blair Spittal signs two-year deal with Partick Thistle|url=https://stv.tv/sport/football/1391313-blair-spittal-signs-two-year-deal-with-partick-thistle/|publisher=STV News|last=Barrie|first=Douglas|date=15 June 2017|access-date=26 July 2017|archive-date=13 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180813175343/https://stv.tv/sport/football/1391313-blair-spittal-signs-two-year-deal-with-partick-thistle/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He scored three goals in his first three games for the club, scoring a brace against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]], including a free kick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Partick Thistle 5–0 St Mirren|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40691407|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Campbell|first=Andy|date=22 July 2017}}</ref> He then scored in a 2–1 win away to [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] in the same competition.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40723082|title=Livi progress with comfortable victory|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Blair marked his league debut for Partick Thistle with 3 assists against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in a 4–3 defeat. In his second league appearance for the club, he scored his first league goal away to [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in a 1–1 draw. Blair continued his form the week after with a goal direct from a free kick and another assist as ten-man Thistle grabbed a 2–2 draw with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] at [[Firhill Stadium|Firhill]], taking his overall club tally to 7 appearances, 5 goals and 4 assists in all competitions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Partick Thistle 2–2 Rangers|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41196748|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Lewis|first=Jane|date=15 September 2017}}</ref> He then carried his form into the next league game by opening the scoring in a 1–1 draw with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]]. He scored his fourth league goal of the campaign with another freekick, scoring the opener in a 3–2 home win against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Partick Thistle 3–2 Motherwell|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42244873|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 December 2017}}</ref> On 26 February 2019, in the absence of Partick Thistle's regular club captain [[Stuart Bannigan]], Blair donned on the armband as the club travelled to East End Park to take on [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline]]. They ended up losing the game 3–0. Blair again lead the team out in a home game against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] in the Scottish Cup quarter-final which ended in a 1–1 draw, meaning that there would be a replay in Edinburgh. Blair rounded off the season with a total of 8 goals in all competitions, and was awarded the club's Player of the Year award. Blair informed the club that he intended to leave on 31 May 2019. In all competitions, he made 89 appearances for the Jags, scoring 15 goals and registering 13 assists.

===Ross County===
On 4 June 2019, Blair signed for [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]], agreeing a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ross County: Blair Spittal out to 'rebuild reputation' after Partick Thistle exit|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48516739|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Smith|first=Tyrone|date=4 June 2019|accessdate=14 July 2019}}</ref> He made his club debut in the Scottish League cup at home to [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]], providing an assist. Three days later, he scored his first goal for the club in a 4–0 away win to [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]]. Just five days on, he bagged another assist in a 2–1 away win against the group favourites [[St. Johnstone F.C.|St. Johnstone]]. Ross County would finish top of their league cup group with the maximum twelve points and advance to round two. Blair would start his first Premiership game on the bench, but was subbed on after just 11 minutes to help his side defeat [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton]] 3–0.

===Return to Partick Thistle===
On 7 October 2020, Blair made a return to former club [[Partick Thistle]] who, at the time, were in League One, on a loan deal until January.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/loan-news-blair-spittal-joins-on-loan/|title = Loan News: Blair Spittal joins on loan}}</ref> Blair scored on his second debut for Partick Thistle just hours after he rejoined the club, scoring the equaliser in an eventual 4–1 defeat away to [[St. Mirren F.C.|St. Mirren]] in their Scottish League Cup group stage.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54452441|title=St Mirren v Partick Thistle|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Blair scored his first league goal in his second spell for Thistle, scoring the winner in a 2–1 home win over [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] in the second league game of the season, with a fantastic curled shot into the top corner from outside the box.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54580568|title=Partick Thistle v Airdrieonians|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>
On 22 January 2021 Spittal was recalled to County following the suspension of the League one season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/2836459/ross-county-sign-norwegian-defender-leo-hjelde-on-loan-from-celtic/|title = Ross County sign Norwegian defender Leo Hjelde on loan from Celtic}}</ref>

===Return to Ross County===
Following his loan spell at Partick, Blair returned to Dingwall in January. From then and until the end of the season, he only made five appearances. Spittal became a first-team regular for the 2021–22 campaign and was given the number 7 shirt. On 17 May 2022 it was announced Spittal would leave Ross County at the end of his contract after three years having made 72 appearances for the club scoring 12 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/blair-spittal-departs-ross-county|title=Blair Spittal departs Ross County|publisher=Ross County FC|accessdate=17 May 2022|date=17 May 2022}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 27 May 2022, it was announced that Spittal would join [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |date=27 May 2022 |title=Motherwell sign Blair Spittal after Ross County exit |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61609731 |accessdate=3 July 2022 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Spittal scored his first Motherwell goal in a 3–2 away win against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] and would score six times in the [[2022–23 Motherwell F.C. season|2022–23]] season.

In the [[2023–24 Motherwell F.C. season|2023–24]] season Spittal would record a career high 13 goals finishing as [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] 2nd top goalscorer. He won his first Scottish Premiership Player of the Month award in February 2024, after scoring 4 and assisting 2 in 5 games.

===Heart of Midlothian===

On 21 March 2024, he agreed a pre-contract with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Barry |date=21 March 2024 |title=Three new signings for Hearts as Blair Spittal agrees a deal to move from Motherwell |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/three-new-signings-for-hearts-as-blair-spittal-agrees-a-deal-to-move-from-motherwell-4564827 |website=Edinburgh Evening News}}</ref> officially signing for the club on 20 June 2024 on a three-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spittal signs – Hearts |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/spittal-signs |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=www.heartsfc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref> 
On Sunday 26th April 2026, Blair scored the winning goal against Hibs.

'''Kevin Michael Nisbet ''' (born 8 March 1997) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)#Centre-forward|centre-forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]]. He has previously played for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] and [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] as well as [[East Stirlingshire F.C.|East Stirlingshire]], [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] and [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on loan.

==Club career==
===Partick Thistle and loans===
Nisbet was raised in [[Cambuslang]], [[South Lanarkshire]], and attended [[Trinity High School, Rutherglen|Trinity High School]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.pressreader.com/uk/the-courier-advertiser-angus-and-the-mearns-edition/20200111/282376926519803 |title=Dunfermline's loan move for Killie winger as key pair sign contract extensions |date=11 January 2020 |work=The Courier |via=[[PressReader]] |access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/hibs-star-kevin-nisbet-reveals-22946535.amp|title=Hibs star Kevin Nisbet reveals his dad died just days before Hearts semi-final|date=2 November 2020|work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|access-date=4 June 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tes.com/magazine/archived/scotland-players-old-schools-send-good-luck-messages|title=Scotland players' old schools send good luck messages|last=Hepburn|first=Henry|date=11 June 2021|work=[[TES (magazine)|TES]]}}</ref> He played for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]'s under-15 team before joining the [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] youth system.<ref name="call">{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/kevin-nisbet-reveals-covid-19-fears-over-hibs-move-football-wake-call-and-why-he-doesnt-set-personal-targets-2912478 |title=Kevin Nisbet reveals Covid-19 fears over Hibs move, football wake-up call, and why he doesn't set personal targets |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=14 July 2020 |access-date=14 July 2020}}</ref> He joined the club as a full-time apprentice in summer 2014.

Having quickly progressed through the Thistle Weir Academy, he made his breakthrough in the [[Firhill]] side's development squad. He made 18 appearances at that level during the 2014–15 campaign, and scored six goals, including a hat-trick against [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kevin Nisbet|url=http://ptfc.co.uk/teams/senior/seasons/2014-2015/players/kevin_nisbet|website=www.ptfc.co.uk|publisher=Partick Thistle|access-date=19 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160402001006/https://ptfc.co.uk/teams/senior/seasons/2014-2015/players/kevin_nisbet|archive-date=2 April 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Nisbet joined [[Scottish League Two]] side [[East Stirlingshire F.C.|East Stirlingshire]] on loan in February 2015,<ref>{{cite web|title=Kevin Nisbet - March 2015|url=http://ptfc.co.uk/news/2014-2015/march_2015/kevin_nisbet|website=www.ptfc.co.uk|publisher=Partick Thistle F.C.|access-date=19 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006023806/http://ptfc.co.uk/news/2014-2015/march_2015/kevin_nisbet|archive-date=6 October 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> making 11 appearances and scoring six goals in his time at [[Ochilview Park]]. He returned to Partick Thistle and made his first-team debut for the club on 19 September 2015 as a substitute in a 1–0 defeat away to [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Davie|first1=Scott|title=A Liam Boyce header was all Ross County needed to beat a Partick Thistle team that remains winless at the foot of the Scottish Premiership.|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34230270|website=www.bbc.co.uk/sport|date=18 September 2015 |publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=19 September 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/partick-thistle-sign-australian-youth-6507171|title=Partick Thistle sign Australian youth inte rnationalist Ryan Edwards|date=24 September 2015|work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref>

Nisbet joined [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on loan at the start of the 2016–17 season, on a six-month deal running until 14 January 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kevin Nisbet signs|url=https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/kevin-nisbet-signs/|publisher=Ayr United F.C.|date=9 August 2016|access-date=7 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160810031715/https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/kevin-nisbet-signs/ |archive-date=10 August 2016}}</ref> He later joined [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on loan in January 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=3413|title=SIGNING NEWS: STRIKER ARRIVES FROM PARTICK THISTLE|last=Findlay|first=Alan|date=22 January 2018|website=Dumbarton Football Club}}</ref>

Thistle were relegated to the [[Scottish Championship]] via the play-offs at the end of the [[2017–18 Partick Thistle F.C. season|2017–18 season]], following which Nisbet was one of many players released by the club.<ref name="call" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/playing-squad-update/ |title=Playing squad update |date=25 May 2018 |access-date=25 May 2018 |website=www.ptfc.co.uk|publisher=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

===Raith and Dunfermline===
Nisbet signed for [[Scottish League One]] side [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in July 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.raithrovers.net/35808/signing-news-kevin-nisbet-nathan-flanagan.htm|title=Signing News: Kevin Nisbet & Nathan Flanagan|date=11 July 2018|website=Raith Rovers F.C.}}</ref> He finished the season at Raith Rovers with 35 goals in all competitions.

Nisbet then signed for [[Fife derby|local rivals]] [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] in June 2019,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Kevin_Nisbet_signs_for_Dunfermline&ID=11269 |title=Kevin Nisbet signs for Dunfermline |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|date=13 June 2019 |access-date=13 June 2019}}</ref> scoring 20 goals in all competitions before the end of 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/kevin-nisbet/398165/ |title=K. Nisbet profile |publisher=Soccerway |access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref> During the January 2020 transfer window, a number of clubs - including his future employers [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] - were said to be interested in the player's signature, however, Dunfermline opted to reject all bids for Nisbet with the intention of keeping him until at least the summer.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Everyone_happy_with_Nizzy_decision&ID=11727 |title=Everyone happy with Nizzy decision |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=19 February 2020 |access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/1371371/exclusive-portsmouth-dundee-united-rivals-kevin-nisbet-tangerines-table-first-bid/ |title=Exclusive: Portsmouth emerge as serious Dundee United rivals for Kevin Nisbet |first=Eric |last=Nicolson |work=Courier |publisher=DC Thomson Co Ltd |date=12 June 2020 |access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref> Nisbet finished the curtailed 2019–20 season having scored 23 goals in 32 appearances.

===Hibernian===
After attracting interest from several clubs,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-seal-stunning-transfer-move-striker-kevin-nisbet-2909746 |title=Hibs seal stunning transfer move for striker Kevin Nisbet |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |publisher=JPIMedia Publishing Ltd |date=10 July 2020 |access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref> Nisbet signed a four-year contract with [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 10 July 2020 for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53352032 |title=Hibernian sign Kevin Nisbet and Drey Wright |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=10 July 2020 |access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/10669 |title=Hibernian agree Kevin Nisbet signing |publisher=Hibernian F.C. |date=10 July 2020 |access-date=10 July 2020 |archive-date=11 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200711175915/http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/10669 |url-status=dead }}</ref> During the January 2021 transfer window Hibs rejected offers for Nisbet from [[EFL Championship]] club [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/birmingham-city-transfer-news-nisbet-20175061 |title='I wasn't too happy' - Kevin Nisbet breaks silence on failed Birmingham City transfer |first=Shane |last=Ireland |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=15 March 2021 |accessdate=12 April 2021}}</ref> Nisbet finished the [[2020–21 Hibernian F.C. season|2020–21]] season as Hibs' top scorer scoring 18 goals in 45 games in all domestic competitions.<ref name="KN20">{{soccerbase season |105520|2020|access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref>

On 22 July 2021, Nisbet scored his first goal in a European club tournament in Hibs' 3–0 win over Andorran side [[FC Santa Coloma]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57905782|title=Hibernian 3–0 FC Santa Coloma|website=bbcsport.co.uk|first=Colin|last=Moffat|date=22 July 2021|access-date=23 July 2021}}</ref> He suffered a knee injury in February 2022 that required surgery, which prevented him from playing for several months.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60711521 |title=Kevin Nisbet: Shaun Maloney expects striker to make World Cup finals if Scotland qualify |date=11 March 2022 |accessdate=12 March 2022 |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Nisbet returned to first-team training in November 2022, and scored in his first league appearance back, a 3–2 defeat at [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on 15 December.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/rangers-defeat-disappointing-hibs-hero-28747295 |title=Rangers defeat was disappointing, but Hibs hero Kevin Nisbet is glad to be back |first=Andy |last=McGilvray |newspaper=Daily Record |date=16 December 2022 |accessdate=16 December 2022}}</ref> He scored a hat-trick in a 3–2 win at [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 8 January,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64137915 |title=Motherwell 2-3 Hibernian: Kevin Nisbet hat-trick earns vital win |website=BBC Sport |date=8 January 2023 |accessdate=8 January 2023 |first=Thomas |last=Duncan}}</ref> which helped him win a Premiership [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners|player of the month award]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-star-becomes-first-non-celtic-or-rangers-player-to-win-player-of-month-award-this-season-4018962 |title=Hibs star becomes first non-Celtic or Rangers player to win Player of Month award this season |newspaper=The Scotsman |first=Oliver |last=Anderson |date=8 February 2023 |accessdate=8 February 2023}}</ref> Hibs accepted an offer of around £2 million from [[EFL Championship]] club [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] during the January 2023 transfer window, but Nisbet decided against the proposed move.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64400937 |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin|title=Kevin Nisbet: Hibernian consider Millwall's increased offer of £2m for Scotland striker |website=BBC Sport |date=25 January 2023 |accessdate=27 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64428133 |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin|title=Kevin Nisbet: Hibs striker's move to Millwall off despite accepted bid |website=BBC Sport |date=27 January 2023 |accessdate=27 January 2023}}</ref> He finished the season with 12 goals from 20 appearances for Hibs.<ref name = 31may23>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65768139 |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin |title=Kevin Nisbet: Hibernian accept Millwall bid for striker |website=BBC Sport |date=31 May 2023 |accessdate=31 May 2023}}</ref> On 31 May 2023, Hibs were reported as having accepted an offer of £2 million for Nisbet from Millwall.<ref name = 31may23/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-accept-offer-for-kevin-nisbet-from-english-championship-club-4164945 |first=Craig |last=Fowler|title=Hibs accept offer for Kevin Nisbet from English Championship club |website=Edinburgh Evening News |date=31 May 2023 |accessdate=31 May 2023}}</ref>

===Millwall===
Nisbet signed a three-year contract with [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] on 10 June 2023. He made his debut for the club on 5 August 2023 in a 1–0 victory over [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]]. Nisbet scored his first Millwall goal on 26 August 2023 in a 1–0 win against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]]. In May 2024, Nisbet was dropped from the Millwall squad for a match against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] due to a "disciplinary issue".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/kevin-nisbet-axed-millwall-squad-32739336 |title=Kevin Nisbet axed from Millwall squad over 'disciplinary issue' as Scotland Euro 2024 hopeful falls foul of boss |newspaper=Daily Record |date=5 May 2024 |accessdate=24 May 2024}}</ref>

===Aberdeen (loan) ===
On 24 August 2024, Nisbet went on loan to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.afc.co.uk/2024/08/24/nisbet-strengthens-dons-forward-line/ |title=Nisbet strengthens Dons' forward line |date=2024-08-24 |website=Aberdeen F.C. }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Kevin Nisbet Eyes Scotland Squad Return with Aberdeen Loan Move |url=https://en.innews247.com/kevin-nisbet-eyes-scotland-squad-return-with-aberdeen-loan-move/ |website=Innews247 |date=2024-08-25 |access-date=2024-08-25 }}</ref> On 24 May 2025, he won the [[2024–25 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] title.<ref>[https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/mitov-penalty-heroics-see-dons-lift-scottish-cup-for-first-time-since-1990/ Mitov Penalty Heroics see Dons Lift Scottish Cup for first time since 1990]</ref>

===Return to Aberdeen===

On 1 September 2025, Nisbet signed a 3 year deal with Aberdeen for a fee of £300,000<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-01 |title=Kevin Nisbet: Aberdeen buy Scotland striker from Millwall |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cx292x2y5xwo |access-date=2025-09-01 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
On 16 March 2021, Nisbet received his first [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] call-up ahead of [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification|2022 World Cup qualifiers]] against [[Austria national football team|Austria]], [[Israel national football team|Israel]] and [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/scotland-boss-steve-clarke-praises-23737515|title=Scotland boss Steve Clarke praises Kevin Nisbet after receiving first call-up|publisher=Daily Record|date=16 March 2021|access-date=16 March 2021}}</ref> Nisbet made his international debut on 31 March, appearing as a substitute in a 4–0 win against the [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56505762 |title=Scotland 4–0 Faroe Islands |website=BBC Sport |first=Andrew |last=Southwick |date=31 March 2021 |accessdate=31 March 2021}}</ref> He was one of three strikers selected in the Scotland squad for the delayed [[UEFA Euro 2020]] tournament,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57298023 |title=Kevin Nisbet: Hibernian striker says he proved to himself that he is Scotland class |website=BBC Sport |date=30 May 2021 |accessdate=30 May 2021}}</ref> and scored his first international goal in a pre-tournament [[friendly match|friendly]] against the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]].<ref name = intgoal>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/international/kevin-nisbet-on-first-scotland-goal-and-giving-himself-chance-for-shock-czech-republic-start-3259372 |title=Kevin Nisbet on first Scotland goal and giving himself chance for shock Czech Republic start |first=Alan |last=Pattullo |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=2 June 2021 |accessdate=3 June 2021}}</ref> Nisbet appeared as a substitute in each of Scotland's three matches at the Euro 2020 finals.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/kevin-nisbet-this-will-be-catalyst-for-hibs-striker-on-his-international-journey-3282964 |title=Kevin Nisbet: This will be catalyst for Hibs striker on his international journey |first=Moira |last=Gordon |date=22 June 2021 |accessdate=24 June 2021}}</ref>

After two years out of the squad, partly due to a long-term knee injury, Nisbet was recalled for the [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying]] matches in June 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65745470 |title=Scotland: Hibernian's Kevin Nisbet earns recall as Southampton's Che Adams misses out |website=BBC Sport |date=29 May 2023 |accessdate=29 May 2023}}</ref>
