'''Ryan William Fulton''' (born 23 May 1996) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. He has previously played for [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], as well as loan spells at [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] and [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]].

Born in England, he was a youth player for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and a youth international for [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland]].

==Club career==
===Liverpool===
Fulton was born in [[Burnley]], [[Lancashire]]<ref name=SW/> and joined [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in 2007, representing them at under-10 level and upwards.{{citation needed|date=December 2016}} Towards the end of the 2013–14 season, he made progress into the Under-21 squad. He featured sporadically during the 2014–15 campaign but was a regular starter in the [[UEFA Youth League]] for under-19 teams.{{citation needed|date=December 2016}}

He was first called up to the senior squad for their 2015 summer tour of Asia prior to the 2015–16 season.{{citation needed|date=December 2016}} He was made Liverpool's third-choice keeper, behind [[Simon Mignolet]] and [[Ádám Bogdán]], after fellow reserve shot stoppers [[Danny Ward (Welsh footballer)|Danny Ward]] and [[Lawrence Vigouroux]] were sent out on loan.{{citation needed|date=December 2016}}

====Loan to Portsmouth====
In January 2016, Fulton emerged as a loan target for [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] as well as [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].{{citation needed|date=December 2016}}

On 22 January 2016, he was signed by [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] on a one-month youth loan deal.{{citation needed|date=December 2016}} He made his senior debut the following day in a 1–0 defeat to [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]], a game in which he saved a penalty from [[Liam Sercombe]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Portsmouth 0–1 Oxford United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35330873|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 January 2016|accessdate=2 December 2016}}</ref>

====Loan to Chesterfield====
On 9 July 2016, he was signed by [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]] on a season long loan deal for the 2016–17 season, as cover for the injured first-choice goalkeeper [[Tommy Lee (footballer)|Tommy Lee]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Chesterfield complete 'keeper capture|url=http://www.chesterfield-fc.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/chesterfield-complete-keeper-capture-3177327.aspx?|accessdate=10 July 2016|publisher=Chesterfield F.C.|date=10 July 2016}}</ref>

===Hamilton Academical===
On 18 July 2017, Fulton joined [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] initially on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fulton joins Hamilton Academical on permanent deal|url=http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/268516-fulton-joins-hamilton-academical-on-permanent-deal|work=Liverpool FC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stv.tv/sport/football/1393772-hamilton-accies-sign-liverpool-goalkeeper-ryan-fulton/|title=Hamilton Accies sign Liverpool goalkeeper Ryan Fulton|website=STV Sport|language=en|access-date=2017-07-18}}</ref>

=== Heart of Midlothian ===
On 19 June 2024, Fulton joined [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on a two-year deal after his contract with Hamilton expired.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fulton joins the Jambos – Hearts |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/fulton-joins-the-jambos |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=www.heartsfc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
Born in England, Fulton has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]], [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] level.<ref>{{SFA Profile|id=197903|name=Ryan Fulton}}</ref>

'''Craig Peter Halkett''' (born 29 May 1995) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for and captains {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].

Initially a striker in his youth, Halkett joined Rangers at age fourteen before being moved to defensive roles and being loaned out to [[Scottish League Two]] clubs [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] and [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]]. After being released by Rangers, Halkett spent several years at [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], making over 100 appearances, before signing a contract with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in 2019.

==Club career==

=== Rangers ===
Raised in [[Kirkintilloch]] and a boyhood [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] fan,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/14201851.craig-halkett-eyes-livi-bow-against-rangers-at-ibrox/|title=Craig Halkett eyes Livi bow against Rangers at Ibrox|newspaper=[[Glasgow Times]]|access-date=31 October 2021}}</ref><ref name=cliff>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/leaving-rangers-like-stepping-cliff-13909204 |title=Leaving Rangers was like stepping off a cliff but it's the best decision I've ever made insists Craig Halkett|author=Gordon Parks|work=Daily Record|date=26 January 2019|access-date=30 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{ cite news | url=http://www.rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/item/8527-halkett-i-learned-a-lot | title=Halkett: I Learned A Lot | publisher=[[Rangers F.C.]] | date=18 February 2015 }}</ref> Halkett joined the club as a youngster. Initially playing as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]], he was moved into more defensive roles by youth coach [[Alan Kernaghan]].<ref name=cliff/> After winning the [[Scottish Youth Cup]] in [[2013–14 Scottish Youth Cup|2014]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27403333 |title=Rangers break Hearts in Youth Cup penalty shoot-out win|work=BBC Sport|date=13 March 2014|access-date=30 January 2019}}</ref><ref name=cliff/> he was loaned out twice, to [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]]<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29026791| work=BBC| title=Ibrox club loans out seven fringe players | date=2 September 2014| publisher=BBC Sport }}</ref> and [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]],<ref>{{cite news| url=http://rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/halkett-heads-out-on-loan/?| work=Rangers Football Club| title=Halkett Heads Out On Loan| date=30 October 2015| publisher=Rangers F.C.| access-date=1 March 2016| archive-date=4 January 2016| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160104234325/http://rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/halkett-heads-out-on-loan| url-status=dead}}</ref> both playing in the [[Scottish League Two|fourth tier]].

=== Livingston ===
In January 2016, Halkett was informed by Rangers that there was no immediate prospect of him progressing to the first team and he left the [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]] club without having made a senior appearance, joining then [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref name=cliff/><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35307242| work=BBC Sport| title=Andy Halliday & Jason Holt sign new Ibrox deals| date=13 January 2016}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal against Rangers in a 1–0 win for Livingston on 26 April 2016.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36079242| author=Chick Young| author-link=Chick Young| title=Livingston 1-0 Rangers | date=26 April 2016| work=BBC Sport }}</ref>

The ''Lions'' were relegated from the Championship at the end of his first campaign in a [[2015–16 Scottish Championship#Championship play-offs|play-off]], but Halkett became an increasingly important player for the [[West Lothian]] side, helping them to immediately return from [[Scottish League One|League One]] in [[2016–17 Scottish League One|2016–17]],<ref name=livi17/> followed by a second consecutive promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]] after finishing runners-up in the [[2017–18 Scottish Championship|regular season]], once more via [[2017–18 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|the play-offs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/competitions/premiership/partick-thistle-0-1-livingston-agg-1-3-hopkin-s-men-seal-promotion-1-4742233 |title=Partick Thistle 0 - 1 Livingston (agg 1-3): Hopkin's men seal promotion|work=[[The Scotsman]]|date=20 May 2018|access-date=30 January 2019}}</ref>

Halkett was made club captain, and was an important part of Livingston's [[2018–19 Livingston F.C. season|2018–19 season]], with the team's defence gaining much praise with the relatively few number of goals conceded compared to similarly-placed teams in the league.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-01-15|title=Livingston must keep Craig Halkett beyond his current contract|url=https://www.nottheoldfirm.com/analysis/livingston-must-keep-craig-halkett-beyond-his-current-contract/|access-date=2022-01-25|website=Not The Old Firm|language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Hearts ===
In April 2019, Halkett signed a pre-contract agreement with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47775439 |title=Hearts: Livingston's Craig Halkett signs pre-contract to switch on three-year deal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 April 2019 |access-date=1 April 2019}}</ref> He suffered a knee injury in October 2019, and it was announced he would be out for 10 weeks.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49932937|title=Craig Halkett: Hearts defender to miss 10 weeks with knee injury|work=BBC Sport |date=4 October 2019}}</ref>

On 11 January 2022, Halkett signed a new two-and-a-half-year contract with Hearts, keeping him at the club until the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 January 2022 |title=Halkett signs new deal |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/halkett-signs-new-deal |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111123329/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/halkett-signs-new-deal |archive-date=11 January 2022 |access-date=2022-01-11 |publisher=Heart Of Midlothian F.C.}}</ref>

==International career==
Halkett represented Scotland once, at [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19 level]] in 2014.<ref name="SFA"/> He received his first call-up to the senior [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad in March 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60813364 |title=Scotland: Sunderland striker Ross Stewart, Hearts defender Craig Halkett & St Johnstone keeper Zander Clark called up |date=21 March 2022 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=21 March 2022|publisher=BBC}}</ref>

He has previously played for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] and [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. ==Career== ===Partick Thistle=== After progressing through the club's Thistle Weir Academy,{{cite web|title=James Penrice|url=http://ptfc.co.uk/teams/senior/seasons/2015-2016/players/james_penrice|publisher=Partick Thistle F.C.|access-date=13 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160513213106/http://ptfc.co.uk/teams/senior/seasons/2015-2016/players/james_penrice|archive-date=13 May 2016|url-status=dead}} Penrice made his senior debut in a 3–3 draw between [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in which he was credited with an assist.{{cite news|last1=McGarry|first1=Graeme|title=Dundee United 3 Partick Thistle 3: Late fightback from United denies Thistle|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/14483486.Dundee_United_3_Partick_Thistle_3__Late_fightback_from_United_denies_Thistle/|access-date=13 May 2016|work=The Herald|date=11 May 2016|location=Glasgow}} He then made his home debut in a 2–2 draw with [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on the last day of the 2015–16 season, winning the man of the match award. Penrice joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] on loan in December 2016, until the end of the season.{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/penrice-heads-out-on-loan/|title = Penrice heads out on loan}} The following summer Penrice was then loaned to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in August 2017 until '''Liam Patrick Kelly''' (born 23 January 1996) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Rangers}} club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]]. Kelly has previously played for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] and [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]].

==Club career==
===Rangers===
Kelly joined Rangers aged ten and played in the club's youth sides, notably scoring the final penalty during Rangers under-17s [[Glasgow Cup]] win in 2012.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/news/13233159.Goalkeeper_Liam_Kelly_is_the_hero_as_Rangers_colts_triumph_in_Glasgow_Cup_penalty_shoot_out/ |title=Goalkeeper Liam Kelly is the hero as Rangers colts triumph in Glasgow Cup penalty shoot-out |date=17 April 2012 |work=Evening Times |publisher=Herald & Times Group |location=Glasgow}}</ref><ref name="glasgow">{{Cite news |last=Dickson |first=Andrew |url=http://rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/gers-win-glasgow-cup/ |title=Gers Win Glasgow Cup |date=16 April 2012 |work=Rangers.co.uk |access-date=17 April 2012 |publisher=Rangers Football Club}}</ref>

After training with the first-team for the majority of the 2014–15 season and featuring on the bench, Kelly signed a contract extension on 25 February 2015, until the summer of 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/item/8567-kelly-delight-at-new-deal |title=Kelly Delight At New Deal |date=25 February 2015 |work=Rangers.co.uk |access-date=16 July 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712115838/http://www.rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/item/8567-kelly-delight-at-new-deal |archive-date=12 July 2015 |publisher=Rangers Football Club}}</ref>

====Loan moves====
On 8 January 2016, Kelly joined [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] in [[Scottish League Two]] on a six-month loan.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://rangers.co.uk/news/headlines/kelly-joins-east-fife/? |title=Kelly Joins East Fife |date=8 January 2016 |work=Rangers.co.uk |publisher=Rangers Football Club}}</ref> During his time at [[Bayview Stadium]], Kelly played in 16 league matches and was part of the side which won the League Two title.<ref name="East fife">{{Cite news |last=Macgregor |first=Archie |url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/competitions/league-two/clyde-0-0-east-fife-league-2-title-joy-for-fifers-1-4102467 |title=Clyde 0-0 East Fife: League 2 title joy for Fifers |date=16 April 2016 |work=[[The Scotsman]] |publisher=Johnston Press |location=Edinburgh}}</ref> Upon returning to Rangers, Kelly travelled to the United States with the first team for a pre-season training camp.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://rangers.co.uk/news/headlines/gers-head-america/ |title=Gers head to America |date=27 June 2016 |work=Rangers.co.uk |publisher=Rangers Football Club}}</ref> However, on 15 July 2016, he was loaned out to the then [[Scottish League One]] team [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] until January 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thomson |first=Nick |url=http://rangers.co.uk/news/headlines/kelly-moves-loan/? |title=Kelly Moves On Loan |date=15 July 2016 |work=Rangers.co.uk |publisher=Rangers Football Club}}</ref> He made his debut for ''Livi'' the next day in a [[Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] match against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=McLauchlin |first=Brian |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36753147 |title=Livingston 2-3 St Mirren |date=16 July 2016 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC}}</ref>

===Livingston===
Kelly moved to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], where he had previously been on loan, for an undisclosed fee in June 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://rangers.co.uk/news/club/liam-kelly-joins-livingston/ |title=Liam Kelly Joins Livingston |date=8 June 2018 |publisher=Rangers FC |access-date=8 June 2018}}</ref> He played regularly for Livingston in the 2018–19 season, but then invoked a release clause in his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48519001 |title=Liam Kelly triggers Livingston release clause amid English Championship interest |date=4 June 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=5 June 2019}}</ref>

===Queens Park Rangers===
On 14 June 2019, Kelly signed for [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] for an undisclosed fee on a four-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48639859 |title=Liam Kelly: QPR sign goalkeeper from Livingston |date=14 June 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=14 June 2019}}</ref> It was reported that the transfers fee was £50,000 with Livingston retaining a sell on bonus.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/livingston-goalkeeper-liam-kelly-completes-16517652|title=Livingston goalkeeper Liam Kelly completes switch to Queen's Park Rangers|first=Callum|last=Carson|date=14 June 2019|website=Daily Record}}</ref> He made his debut on 13 August 2019, in an [[EFL Cup]] match against [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] saving two penalties in a 5–4 penalty shootout win.

====Motherwell (loan)====
On 6 January 2021, Kelly moved on loan to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Liam Kelly signs on loan|url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2021/01/06/liam-kelly-signs-on-loan/|website=motherwellfc.co.uk|date=6 January 2021|accessdate=6 January 2021}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 5 July 2021, Kelly returned to Motherwell on a permanent transfer from Queens Park Rangers, signing a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=LIAM KELLY RETURNS TO MOTHERWELL |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2021/07/05/liam-kelly-returns-to-motherwell/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk/ |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=5 July 2021 |date=5 July 2021}}</ref> He was ever present in the league during his three seasons at [[Fir Park]], making 133 appearances overall.

===Return to Rangers===
On 27 June 2024, Rangers completed the signing of goalkeeper Liam Kelly on a two-year deal. Kelly, a former Rangers academy player, returned to Ibrox after his contract expired at Motherwell.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/rangers-sign-scotland-international-goalkeeper-liam-kelly/6V1RhVAM3lxTWnYRogJ7bR |title=Rangers Sign Scotland International Goalkeeper Liam Kelly |date=27 June 2024 |publisher=Rangers FC |access-date=27 June 2024}}</ref> Kelly made his first competitive appearance for Rangers on 21 December 2024, in a 1–0 victory against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sports/articles/c05p87r1ny9o |title=Kelly revels in 'unbelievable' Rangers debut |date=22 December 2024 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=3 July 2025}}{{dead link|date=September 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He then started in an [[Old Firm]] game for the first time, as Rangers won 3–0 against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on 2 January 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/fixture/rangers-vs-celtic-scottish-premiership-2025-01-02/2B2XDvamYVuay2C5Ay281w |title=Rangers 3-0 Celtic |date=2 January 2025 |publisher=Rangers FC |access-date=13 January 2025}}</ref> Following a dip of form for regular starter Butland, Kelly was chosen to play in a [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] tie against [[Athletic Bilbao]]. He saved a [[penalty kick]] in the first leg, which ended in a goalless draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ckgeyng3dnlt |first=Martin |last=Dowden |title=Rangers 0-0 Athletic Club - Liam Kelly saves penalty for 10-man hosts |website=BBC Sport |date=10 April 2025 |accessdate=2 July 2025}}</ref> Kelly played in 10 league games during the [[2024–25 Scottish Premiership|2024–25]] season, recording four clean sheets.

==International career==
[[File:Украина U-21 - Шотландия U-21 4-0. 6 сентября 2016 года — 708159.jpg|thumb|Kelly (No 1) with [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21s]] in Ukraine, 2016]]
Kelly has represented Scotland at various age levels, up to an including the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] team.<ref name="SFA" />

Kelly received his first call-up to the senior [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad in March 2019 for games against [[Kazakhstan national football team|Kazakhstan]] and [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47604868 |title=Scotland: Andy Robertson to miss Kazakhstan clash as trio also pull out |date=17 March 2019 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=18 March 2019 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> After many call-ups to the squad without playing, Kelly finally made his full international debut in a [[friendly match|friendly]] against [[France national football team|France]] on 17 October 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67061897 |title=France 4-1 Scotland: Star-studded hosts inflict heavy defeat on makeshift Scots |website=BBC Sport |date=17 October 2023 |accessdate=17 October 2023}}</ref> He was selected in the Scotland squads for [[UEFA Euro 2024]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/clwwdq8dzrno |title=Liam Kelly signs short-term Motherwell deal to secure Euro bonus |website=BBC Sport |date=8 June 2024 |accessdate=8 June 2024}}</ref> and the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/scotland-craig-gordon-2026-fifa-world-cup-roster|title=Scotland Includes 43-year-old Goalkeeper Craig Gordon In World Cup Squad|publisher=Fox Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cvgz2e8g4e8o|title=World Cup: Meet the Scotland squad in their own words|last=Canavan|first=Amy|date=3 June 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==Style of play==
[[Kenny Miller]], who played alongside Kelly at Rangers and was also his player-manager at Livi, said of him in 2018: "He's excellent with the ball at his feet. He's a proper modern-day goalkeeper".<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45741014 |title=Liam Kelly 'could lead next batch of Scotland goalkeepers' - Kenny Miller |date=4 October 2018 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=4 October 2018 |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is the brother of [[Boeung Ket F.C.|Boeung Ket]] defender [[Sean Kelly (Scottish footballer)|Sean Kelly]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Sean Kelly says Liam Kelly 'has the ability and mindset' to play for Rangers|url=https://sportslens.com/sean-kelly-says-liam-kelly-has-the-ability-and-mindset-to-play-for-rangers/251805/|website=Sports Lens|author=Charlie Rhodes |date=25 November 2018}}</ref> and [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] goalkeeper Shay Kelly.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Fraser |date=2025-03-30 |title=My brother is a Rangers ace - now I've made my SPFL debut I want to follow him |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/brother-rangers-ace-now-ive-34960489 |access-date=2026-01-03 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> In October 2023 Liam and Sean faced each other from 12 yards in a Scottish Premiership fixture, with Sean scoring his penalty past Liam.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/motherwell-kid-lennon-miller-wise-31148552|title=Motherwell kid Lennon Miller has wise head on his shoulders, red card won't affect him, says skipper|last=McGilvray|first=Andy|date=10 October 2023|work=Daily Record}}</ref>

'''Calvin Darren Miller'''<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title=Birth registers|url=https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/record-results/102278273969a78c1e801e8 |website=Scotland's People |location=Edinburgh, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref> (born 9 January 1998)<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title=Calvin Miller |url=https://falkirkfc.co.uk/player/c-miller/ |website=Falkirk FC |location=Falkirk, Stirlingshire, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref> is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]] or [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[HMFC|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date=4 June 2026 |title=Calvin Miller becomes a Jambo |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/calvin-miller-becomes-a-jambo |website=Heart of Midlothian FC |location=Edinburgh, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref>

Miller has previously played for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], [[Harrogate Town A.F.C.|Harrogate Town]], [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]], [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]], [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] and [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]. 

==Club career==
===Celtic===
Having attended training sessions at [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.celticquicknews.co.uk/when-celtics-calvin-miller-was-named-best-young-player-in-the-world/|title= When Celtic's Calvin Miller was named best young player in the world|website=Celtic Quick News|date=4 September 2017|accessdate=14 August 2019}}</ref> Miller signed for [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2010, aged 12.<ref name = contract>{{cite web|url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/10588|title=Calvin Miller signs new three-year deal|publisher=Celtic FC|date=24 May 2016|accessdate=21 December 2016|archive-date=21 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161221235921/http://www.celticfc.net/news/10588|url-status=live}}</ref>

In addition to domestic tournaments (he was in the squad which won the [[Scottish Youth Cup]] in [[2014–15 Scottish Youth Cup#Final|2015]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.youthfootballscotland.co.uk/gots/item/17808-nesbitt-the-hat-trick-hero-as-emphatic-celtic-claim-the-little-big-shot-youth-cup.html|title=Nesbitt the hat-trick hero as emphatic 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190711210308/http://www.youthfootballscotland.co.uk/gots/item/17808-nesbitt-the-hat-trick-hero-as-emphatic-celtic-claim-the-little-big-shot-youth-cup.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and started and scored in the competition's [[2016–17 Scottish Youth Cup#Final|2017 final]]),<ref name = "2017 celtic">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39727216 |title=Scottish Miller featured in several international youth tournaments during his Celtic youth career such as the [[NextGen Series]] and the [[UEFA Youth League]].<ref>{{cite Miller made his [[2016–17 Scottish Premiership|league]] and competitive debut against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on 20 December 2016.<ref>{{cite news|first=Richard|last=Wilson|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36994428|title=Celtic 1-0 Partick Thistle: Scott Sinclair strike edges brave visitors|publisher=BBC Sport|date=20 December 2016|accessdate=14 August 2019|archive-date=14 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190814103229/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36994428|url-status=live}}</ref> He received praise for his performance in the match, which Celtic won.<ref>{{cite news|first=Gavin |last=Berry|title=Brendan Rodgers hails Celtic debut boy Calvin Miller and compares him to Ryan Bertrand|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/soccer/scottish-football/celtic-fc/brendan-rodgers-hails-celtic-debut-9494344|publisher=MGN|work=Irish Mirror Online|date=21 December 2016|accessdate=14 August 2019}}</ref> It was at this point that his manager [[Brendan Rodgers]] revealed that Miller, who had previously been considered a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] or [[Forward (association football)|forward]] in his youth career with the club, was retraining in a more defensive position. Rodgers also expressed his hope that Miller could flourish in his new role in a similar manner to his previous trainee [[Ryan Bertrand]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stv.tv/sport/football/1376292-celtic-boss-compares-calvin-miller-to-england-international/|title=Celtic boss compares Calvin Miller to England international|publisher=STV Sport|date=21 December 2016|first=Laura|last=Brannan|accessdate=21 December 2016|archive-date=11 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190711210304/https://stv.tv/sport/football/1376292-celtic-boss-compares-calvin-miller-to-england-international/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He did not feature for the senior team again until 8 August 2017, when he played the full 90 minutes in a 5–0 win over [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in the [[2017–18 Scottish League Cup#Second round|Scottish League Cup]], with regular left-back [[Kieran Tierney]] filling in as a [[Defender (association football)#Central defender|central defender]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Kenny |last=Crawford |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40829930 |title=Celtic 5–0 Kilmarnock |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 August 2017 |accessdate=8 August 2017 |archive-date=5 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180905050605/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40829930 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Miller started at left-back on 19 August 2017 in the [[2017–18 Scottish Premiership|Scottish Premiership]], again against Kilmarnock, and was given [[Player of the match#Association football|man of the match]] by [[Sky Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/sunderland-transfer-gossip-celtic-defender-14802084|title=Sunderland transfer gossip: side won 2–0 with goals from [[James Forrest (footballer, born 1991)|James Forrest]] and [[Callum McGregor]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/kilmarnock-vs-celtic/376412|title=Kilmarnock 0-2 Celtic|publisher=Sky Sports|date=19 August 2017|accessdate=25 September 2017|agency=PA Sport|archive-date=26 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170926041202/http://www.skysports.com/football/kilmarnock-vs-celtic/376412|url-status=live}}</ref> He was selected in further home fixtures against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in February 2018<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43021020|title=Celtic 0–0 St Johnstone|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Andy |last=Campbell |date=18 February 2018|accessdate=10 May 2018}}</ref> and Kilmarnock again in May, being replaced in the second half by Tierney in both matches, which ended in 0–0 draws after Celtic made several other changes which appeared to affect their rhythm as a unit.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43971315|title=Celtic 0–0 Kilmarnock|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180512075126/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43971315|url-status=live}}</ref>

Miller signed a new contract with Celtic in August 2018, tying him to the club until summer 2020 with the possibility of extension. Speaking on his future, he stated that his short-term aim was to secure a loan move to gain further experience.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/14809|title=Delight as Calvin Miller signs new deal with Celtic|first=Mark|last=Henderson|publisher=Celtic FC|date=21 August 2018|accessdate=27 August 2018|archive-date=26 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826015414/http://www.celticfc.net/news/14809|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Ayr United loan====
On 31 January 2019, Miller joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on loan until the end of the [[2018–19 in Scottish football|2018–19 season]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Scott |last=Mullen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47082771|title=Celtic sign Jeremy Toljan from Borussia Dortmund on loan|publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2019|accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref>

====Return, injury and release====
Having returned to Celtic in summer 2019 Miller spoke of his hope of being in the plans of [[Neil Lennon]], Celtic's new manager who had used Miller in friendly matches in his previous spell in charge of the club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/calvin-miller-eager-for-another-chance-at-celtic-under-neil-lennon-rjkc3gjq3|title=Calvin Miller eager for another chance at Celtic under Neil Lennon|work=[[The Times]]|date=4 June 2019|first=Alison|last=McConnell|publisher=Times Newspapers|access-date=1 June 2022}}{{subscription required}}</ref> However, when 2019|first=Danny|last=Owen|publisher=GRV Media|accessdate=1 June 2022}}</ref> Miller then turned down a move to Kilmarnock as part of a deal to bring [[Greg Taylor (Scottish footballer)|Greg Taylor]] (also a left back) to Celtic, a signing which, along with improvement in the form of [[Boli Bolingoli]], another new signing in the same position, further diminished the chances of Miller being selected.<ref name=ruledout>{{cite news|url=https://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/17931737.amp/|title=Celtic's Calvin Miller ruled out for rest of season after op and may have played final Hoops ===Harrogate Town===
English club [[Harrogate Town A.F.C.|Harrogate Town]] signed Miller on 3 October 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54401109 |title=Calvin Miller: Harrogate Town sign versatile former Celtic player |publisher=BBC Sport|date=3 October 2020 |accessdate=25 October 2020}}</ref>

====Notts County (loan)====
On 11 January 2021, Miller joined [[National League (division)|National League]] side [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]] on loan for the remainder of the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.nottscountyfc.co.uk/news/2021/january/effiong-miller-and-boyes-sign-110121/ |title=Two join on loan|accessdate=1 June 2022|publisher=Notts County FC |date=11 January 2021}}</ref>

===Chesterfield===
On 25 June 2021, Miller agreed to return to the National League to join [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]] upon the expiration of his contract with Harrogate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://chesterfield-fc.co.uk/club-news/winger-miller-agrees-contract|title=Winger Miller agrees contract|publisher=Chesterfield FC|date=25 June 2021|accessdate=10 July 2021|archive-date=29 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210629032041/https://chesterfield-fc.co.uk/club-news/winger-miller-agrees-contract|url-status=live}}</ref> On 13 October 2022, Miller had his contract terminated by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://chesterfield-fc.co.uk/club-news/millers-departure-announced|title=Miller's departure announced|website=chesterfield-fc.co.uk|date=13 October 2022|accessdate=14 October 2022|archive-date=14 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014102345/https://chesterfield-fc.co.uk/club-news/millers-departure-announced|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Greenock Morton ===
On 2 January 2023, Miller signed with [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-02 |title=Calvin Miller signs for the Ton |url=https://www.gmfc.net/calvin-miller-signs-for-the-ton/ |access-date=2023-01-02 |website=Greenock Morton FC |language=en-GB |archive-date=2 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230102231504/https://www.gmfc.net/calvin-miller-signs-for-the-ton/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored his first and only goal for the club in a 2–2 draw with [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]],<ref>{{Cite news |title=Inverness CT come back twice to draw with Morton |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64436324 |access-date=2023-06-15 |archive-date=8 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230908072954/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64436324 |url-status=live }}</ref> before leaving in June 2023.

===Falkirk===
After leaving Morton, Miller signed for [[Scottish League One]] club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2023/06/15/calvin-miller-joins-the-bairns/ | title=CALVIN MILLER JOINS THE BAIRNS! | publisher=Falkirk FC | work=falkirkfc.co.uk | date=15 June 2023 | accessdate=15 June 2023}}</ref> In March 2024, Miller won the [[2023–24 Scottish League One|League One title]] with the ''Bairns'' on the same night they defeated [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] 7–1 at [[Links Park]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Falkirk crowned champions prior to rampant victory |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68644141 |access-date=2024-03-31 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Miller would be named to the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#League One 9|PFA Scotland League One Team of the Year]] in April 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kearney |first=Ben |date=19 April 2024 |title=Falkirk dominate PFA Scotland League One team of the year as TEN stars selected |url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-dominate-pfa-scotland-league-one-team-of-the-year-as-ten-stars-selected-4598493 |access-date=21 April 2024 |website=falkirkherald.co.uk |archive-date=20 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420094025/https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-dominate-pfa-scotland-league-one-team-of-the-year-as-ten-stars-selected-4598493 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 2 August 2024, Miller scored in Falkirk's first game back in the [[Scottish Championship]] in a win over [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Winning start for Falkirk {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/winning-start-for-falkirk |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> In April 2025, Miller was among four Falkirk players named to the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Championship 10|PFA Scotland Championship Team of the Year]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2025-04-19 |title=Falkirk quartet included in PFA Scotland Championship team of the year |url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/falkirk-quartet-including-ex-lowland-league-star-named-in-pfa-scotland-championship-team-of-the-year-5090910 |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=Falkirk Herald |language=en |archive-date=20 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250420033823/https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/falkirk-quartet-including-ex-lowland-league-star-named-in-pfa-scotland-championship-team-of-the-year-5090910 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 2 May 2025, Miller started and scored his 10th league goal of the season in a 3-1 home win over [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] to confirm Falkirk as [[Scottish Championship]] winners, winning back-to-back titles and earning the ''Bairns'' promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Falkirk beat Hamilton Academical 3-1 to win Scottish Championship title and promotion |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cj9egnedlgxt |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=2 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250502182412/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cj9egnedlgxt |url-status=live }}</ref> Miller capped off a brilliant season with being awarded the [[SPFL]]'s [[Scottish Professional Football League yearly awards|Scottish Championship Player of the Year]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2025-05-12 |title=Falkirk winger Calvin Miller named Scottish Championship player of the year |url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/falkirk-winger-calvin-miller-named-scottish-championship-player-of-the-year-5125049 |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=Falkirk Herald |language=en |archive-date=12 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250512222117/https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/falkirk-winger-calvin-miller-named-scottish-championship-player-of-the-year-5125049 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===
On 4 June 2026, Miller signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on a three year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cvgzx77z08wo|title=Miller hopes to make a name for himself at Hearts|work=bbc.co.uk|publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=4 June 2026|accessdate=4 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-get-their-third-new-signing-in-a-six-figure-transfer-deal-plus-more-talks-talking-place-8655614|title=Hearts get their third new signing in a six-figure transfer deal - plus more talks talking place|work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com|publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=4 June 2026|accessdate=4 June 2026}}</ref>

He made his debut for the club, starting the whole game, in a 4-0 loss against [[SK Sturm Graz|Sturm Graz]] in the first leg of the [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League qualifying#Second_qualifying_round|UEFA Champions League's second qualifying round]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-sturm-graz-4-0-heart-of-midlothian|title=Match Report: Sturm Graz 4-0 Heart of Midlothian|website=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=21 July 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828071745/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-sturm-graz-4-0-heart-of-midlothian|archive-date=28 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Miller made his league debut for Hearts, starting the whole game, in a 2-1 loss against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in the opening game of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-aberdeen-2-1-hearts-1|title=Match Report: Aberdeen 2-1 Hearts|website=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=1 August 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828080847/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-aberdeen-2-1-hearts-1|archive-date=28 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> A week later on 8 August 2026, he scored his first goal for the club, in a 4-0 win against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-hearts-4-0-dundee-utd|title=Match Report: Hearts 4-0 Dundee Utd|website=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=9 August 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828073223/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-hearts-4-0-dundee-utd|archive-date=28 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> A week later on 16 August 2026, Miller scored once again, in a 4-0 win against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness CT]] in the second round of the Scottish League Cup<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-hearts-6-2-ict|title=Match Report: Hearts 6-2 ICT|website=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=16 August 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828115758/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-hearts-6-2-ict|archive-date=28 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> In the return leg against [[SK Rapid Wien|Rapid Wien]] in the [[2026–27 UEFA_Conference League#Play-off_round|play-off round of UEFA Conference League]], he scored his first European goal and played the whole game to a 2-2 draw and was four out of the Hearts players to successfully converted a penalty shootout, as the club went on to win 4-3.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-sk-rapid-2-2-hearts-3-4p|title=Match Report: SK Rapid 2-2 Hearts (3-4p)|website=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=26 August 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828073436/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-sk-rapid-2-2-hearts-3-4p|archive-date=28 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

==International career==
Miller was selected for Scotland at various youth levels.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1848&playerID=166415 |title=Calvin Miller |publisher=Scottish Football Association |accessdate=22 December 2016 |archive-date=9 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809042204/http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1848&playerID=166415 |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his debut for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21 team]] in March 2019.<ref name=mex19>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/scotland-u21s-0-mexico-u22s-14173946|title=Scotland U21s 0 Mexico U22s 0 as Mikey Johnston misses last-gasp penalty - 3 talking points|work=Daily Record|date=22 March 2019|publisher=Reach Scotland|accessdate=23 March 2019|first=Tony|last=Haggerty|archive-date=23 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190323001800/https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/scotland-u21s-0-mexico-u22s-14173946|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Miller was born in [[Glasgow]] and grew up in the city's [[Castlemilk]] district.<ref name=contract/> He is the father of two daughters, Olivia and Mia, born in 2015 and 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.deadlinenews.co.uk/2017/11/08/doting-dad-calvin-miller-young-family-driving-star-celtic-scotland/|first=Alan|last=Temple|date=8 November 2017|title=Doting dad Calvin Miller on how young family is driving him on to star for Celtic & Scotland|publisher=Capital City Press|accessdate=15 August 2019|work=Deadline News|archive-date=15 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190815112913/http://www.deadlinenews.co.uk/2017/11/08/doting-dad-calvin-miller-young-family-driving-star-celtic-scotland/|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Hicham Mahou''' ({{langx|ar|هشام ماحو}}; born 2 July 1999) is a French professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right winger]] for Scottish Premiership side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref name="SW">{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/hicham-mahou/446668/|title=H. Mahou|website=Soccerway|accessdate=22 October 2017}}</ref>

==Club career==
Mahou made his professional debut for [[OGC Nice|Nice]] in a 3–3 [[Ligue 1]] draw against [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] on 20 May 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/82168|title=LFP.fr - Ligue de Football Professionnel - Ligue 1 - Saison 2016/2017 - 38ème journée - Olympique Lyonnais / OGC Nice|website=www.lfp.fr}}</ref> In January 2020, he was loaned to [[Red Star F.C.|Red Star]] until the end of the [[2019–20 Championnat National|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Nice-prete-hicham-mahou-au-red-star/1103998|title=Nice prête Hicham Mahou au Red Star|publisher=L'Équipe|language=fr|date=29 January 2020}}</ref>

On 9 September 2026, Mahou signed for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c74k1d2p2pjo|title='Technically gifted' French winger Mahou signs for Aberdeen|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 September 2026 |access-date=19 September 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Born in France, Mahou is of Moroccan descent. He is a youth international for France.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mountakhab.net/www/modules/article_une/index.php?storyid=470584|title=Nice : Mahou rejoint le groupe professionnel|first=Achraf|last=Bakkali|website=Mountakhab.net|access-date=30 August 2017|archive-date=30 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170830102853/http://mountakhab.net/www/modules/article_une/index.php?storyid=470584|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Elton Daniël Kabangu''' (born 8 February 1998) is a Belgian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].

==Career==
Kabangu made his [[Eerste Divisie]] debut for [[FC Eindhoven]] on in a game against [[SC Telstar]] and scored twice after coming off the bench late in the first half of the 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2017/08/18/netherlands/eerste-divisie/fc-eindhoven/stormvogels-telstar-combinatie/2463187/|title=Game Report by Soccerway|date=}}</ref>

On 9 June 2023, [[Belgian Pro League]] side [[Royale Union Saint-Gilloise|Union SG]] confirmed the signing of Kabangu until 2026.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Union SG|url=https://rusg.brussels/article/elton-kabangu-premier-transfert-dete-de-lunion-sg|title=Elton Kabangu, premier transfert d'été de l'Union SG (in French)|date=9 June 2023|access-date=10 June 2023|archive-date=10 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230610151506/https://rusg.brussels/article/elton-kabangu-premier-transfert-dete-de-lunion-sg|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 1 January 2025, [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] confirmed the signing of Kabangu on loan until the end of the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/elton-joins-jambos | title=Elton joins Jambos | date=1 January 2025 | access-date=2 January 2025}}</ref> The move was made permanent at the end of the season, with Kabangu signing a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c3v5n00g522o |title=Hearts: Elton Kabangu signs on permanent deal from Union Saint-Gilloise |website=BBC Sport |date=28 May 2025 |accessdate=28 May 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Born in Belgium, Kabangu is of Congolese descent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.willem-ii.nl/artikel/elton-kabangu-tekent-voor-drie-jaar|title=Elton Kabangu tekent voor drie jaar | Willem II|website=www.willem-ii.nl}}</ref>
Kabangu was in a coma for 16 days after contracting COVID-19. He had an infection in his lungs but credits his Christian faith with helping him recover - "It was a battle for me, but I'm a believer in Jesus, so I know it's part of the plan. I accepted it. I survived it. I came back and that's the most important thing for me."<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cr4n3069r5lo|title=How faith helped Hearts' Kabangu defy 16-day Covid coma}}</ref>

'''Nicolas Thierry Yvan Rasking''' ({{IPA|fr|nikɔla ʁaskɛ̃}}; born 23 February 2001) is a Belgian professional footballer who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Rangers}} club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Belgium national football team|Belgium national team]].

Raskin had spells in the youth academies of [[Standard Liège]] and [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] before joining [[KAA Gent|Gent]] in 2017. He made his competitive debut for Gent in February 2018, becoming the first player born in the 21st century to play in the [[Belgian Pro League]]. He re-joined Standard Liège in January 2019, and signed for Rangers four years later.

Raskin earned more than 50 caps for Belgium's youth national teams. He represented the country from under-15 to [[Belgium national under-21 football team|under-21 level]]. He made his senior international debut in March 2025, and was a member of Belgium's squad at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Raskin's first club as a child was Royal Stade Waremmien FC,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.rtbf.be/article/officiel-indesirable-au-standard-nicolas-raskin-sengage-avec-les-glasgow-rangers-11141567 |title=Officiel : Indésirable au Standard, Nicolas Raskin s'engage avec les Glasgow Rangers |website=rtbf.be |date=31 January 2023 |access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref> before playing youth football for [[Standard Liège]] from 2008 to 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lesoir.be/202346/article/2019-01-23/cest-officiel-nicolas-raskin-est-un-joueur-du-standard |title=C'est officiel: Nicolas Raskin est un joueur du Standard |website=lesoir.be |date=23 January 2019 |access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref> He then spent two years in [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]]'s youth academy.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.walfoot.be/news/2019-02-07/nicolas-raskin-standard-revient-sur-ses-departs-a-anderlecht-et-a-la-gantoise |title=Nicolas Raskin revient sur ses départs à Anderlecht et à La Gantoise : "J'aurais déjà pu revenir au Standard" |website=walfoot.be |date=7 February 2019 |access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref> In May 2017, Raskin left Anderlecht to join [[K.A.A. Gent|Gent]], signing a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.kaagent.be/nl/nieuws/26-05-2017/kaa-gent-strikt-toptalent-nicolas-raskin |title=KAA Gent strikt toptalent Nicolas Raskin |website=kaagent.be |date=26 May 2017 |access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref> Raskin made his professional debut for Gent at the age of 16 in a 3–0 [[Belgian Pro League]] win over [[Sint-Truidense V.V.|Sint-Truiden]] in February 2018, becoming the first player born in the 21st century to play in the league.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lesoir.be/139561/article/2018-02-11/avec-nicolas-raskin-gand-lelite-belge-est-entree-dans-le-21e-siecle |title=Avec Nicolas Raskin (Gand), l'élite belge est entrée dans le 21e siècle |website=lesoir.be |date=11 February 2018 |access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref>

===Standard Liège===
On 23 January 2019, Raskin returned to his former youth club Standard Liège.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://standard.be/nl/news/nicolas-raskin-tekent-bij-de-rouches |title=Nicolas Raskin tekent bij de Rouches |website=standard.be |date=23 January 2019 |access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref>

===Rangers===
[[File:Nicolas Raskin 2023.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Raskin playing for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in 2023.]]

On 31 January 2023, Raskin joined Scottish club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on a long-term contract for an undisclosed transfer fee.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64403296 |title=Rangers transfers: Nicolas Raskin signs from Standard Liege |publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2023 |access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref> It was reported that the fee paid was £1.5 million plus additional bonuses, and Raskin signed a four-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://twitter.com/sachatavolieri/status/1620469621852864512|title=As reminder, Nicolas #Raskin to #RangersFC|work=Sacha Tavolieri|publisher=Twitter, Inc|date=31 January 2023}}</ref> He made his debut four days later, in a 2–1 victory over [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64436051 |title=Rangers 2–1 Ross County |publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport |date=4 February 2023 |access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Nicolas Raskin Belgium v USA 6 July 2026-095.jpg|thumb|Raskin playing for [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]]]]
Raskin played youth international football for Belgium at the under-15, under-16, [[Belgium national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[Belgium national under-18 football team|under-18]], [[Belgium national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Belgium national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rbfa.be/en/international/8309/career |title=Nicolas Raskin |website=rbfa.be |access-date=27 June 2023}}</ref>

He represented the Belgium under-17 team at the [[2018 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under17/teams/players/250108589--nicolas-raskin/|title=Under-17 - Nicolas Raskin – UEFA.com|last=uefa.com|website=[[UEFA]]}}</ref> In June 2023, he scored both goals for the Belgium under-21 team in a 2–0 win over [[Israel national under-21 football team|Israel]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c2v83l15el5o |title=Raskin nets double for Euros-bound Belgium U21s |work=BBC Sport |date=16 June 2023}}</ref> The same summer, he was named in the Belgian squad for the [[2023 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]].

On 14 March 2025, Raskin was called up to the senior [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] squad for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |date=15 March 2025 |title=Belgium boss explains Nico Raskin call-up as Rangers star leapfrogs £50m star |url=https://www.rangersnews.uk/news/belgium-boss-explains-nico-raskin-call-up-as-rangers-star-leapfrogs-50m-star/ |access-date=28 November 2025 |website=rangersnews.uk}}</ref> Raskin made his debut on 20 March 2025, replacing [[Koni De Winter]] in the 80th minute of a defeat to [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] in a [[UEFA Nations League]] relegation play-off tie.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-21 |title=Rangers ace Raskin's Belgium debut in preparation for starring role for country |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/25026554.rangers-ace-raskins-belgium-debut-preparation-starring-role/ |access-date=2025-03-21 |website=The Herald |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Raskin was born in [[Liège]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.walfoot.be/news/2019-01-23/raskin-vu-par-son-coach-en-belgique-u17--un-tres-jeune-talent-qui-a-besoin-dun-nouveau-challenge |title=Raskin vu par son coach en Belgique U17 : "Un très jeune talent qui a besoin d'un nouveau challenge" |website=walfoot.be |date=23 January 2019 |access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref> He is the son of [[Thierry Raskin]], who was also a professional footballer in Belgium.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.voetbalnieuws.be/news/278237/16jarig-toptalent-maakt-debuut-bij-aa-gent |title=16-jarig toptalent maakt debuut bij AA Gent |website=www.voetbalnieuws.be |date=11 February 2018 |access-date=25 February 2023}}</ref>

{{cite web|url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/academy/301152-liverpool-fc-u23s-anfield-chelsea-premier-league-2|title=Match report: U23s shine at Anfield to seal second place|website=Liverpool F.C.|date=8 May 2018|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180509000320/http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/academy/301152-liverpool-fc-u23s-anfield-chelsea-premier-league-2|archive-date=9 May 2018|url-status=live}} ==Club career== ===Swansea City=== In May 2018, Dhanda left Liverpool to join [[EFL Championship|Championship]] club [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] where he was originally expected to be with the Under 23s.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44120950|title=Swansea City: Yan Dhanda signs from Liverpool|first=Mandeep|last=Sanghera|website=www.bbc.co.uk|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 May 2018|access-date=13 July 2018|archive-date=25 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181025022856/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44120950|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/academy/302914-liverpool-fc-transfer-yan-dhanda-swansea|title=Yan Dhanda joins Swansea City|website=Liverpool F.C.|date=23 May 2018|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180701004846/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/academy/302914-liverpool-fc-transfer-yan-dhanda-swansea|archive-date=1 July 2018|url-status=live}}{{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/yan-eyes-chance-shine|title=Yan eyes a chance to shine|website=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=23 May 2018|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006181743/https://www.swanseacity.com/news/yan-eyes-chance-shine|archive-date=6 October 2022|url-status=live}} Upon joining the club, Dhanda said: "I am really happy to be here. I was excited from the minute I knew Swansea were interested in signing me. I just wanted to get the deal done. I wasn't really getting a chance at Liverpool and I wanted to come somewhere where I hope I will have a better chance to play in the first team. I want to show what I can do. Once I knew Swansea were interested, I felt the club would suit me. I have watched the football they have played over the years and I hope coming here will bring out the best in me." He was given the number 30 shirt.{{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/squad-numbers-revealed|title=Squad numbers revealed|website=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=3 August 2018|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002185904/https://www.swanseacity.com/news/squad-numbers-revealed|archive-date=2 October 2022|url-status=live}} Dhanda made his debut as a substitute for the club on 4 August 2018 against [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] in a 2–1 win, scoring the winner with his first touch only moments after entering the field.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/44797126|title=Potter's Swansea come from behind to win at Sheff Utd|website=www.bbc.co.uk|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 August 2018|access-date=4 August 2018|archive-date=4 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180804115252/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/44797126|url-status=live}}. However, he found his first team opportunities limited, due to strong competitions in the midfield position.{{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/dhanda-eyes-millwall-chance|title=Dhanda eyes Millwall chance|website=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=30 August 2018|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809015714/https://www.swanseacity.com/news/dhanda-eyes-millwall-chance|archive-date=9 August 2022|url-status=live}}

{{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/matt-grimes-pleased-unbeaten-start-new-partnership|title=Matt Grimes pleased with unbeaten start for new partnership|website=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=13 October 2020|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220807191042/https://www.swanseacity.com/news/matt-grimes-pleased-unbeaten-start-new-partnership|archive-date=7 August 2022|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=Steve Cooper's Yan Dhanda regret and Matt Grimes' telling reaction as Blackburn boss identifies key Swansea City duo|url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/steve-coopers-yan-dhanda-regret-19200611|website=Wales Online|date=1 November 2020|access-date=26 October 2024}} On 27 October 2020, he made his first start for Swansea City and helped the club beat [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] 2–0.{{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/report-swansea-city-2-stoke-city-0|title=Report: Swansea City 2 Stoke City 0|website=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=27 October 2020|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220117210529/https://www.swanseacity.com/news/report-swansea-city-2-stoke-city-0|archive-date=17 January 2022|url-status=live}} Following this, Dhanda received a handful of first team, alternating between the starting eleven and substitute bench.{{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/cooper-delighted-see-yan-dhanda-take-his-chance|title=Cooper delighted to see Yan Dhanda take his chance|website=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=31 October 2020|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007125159/https://www.swanseacity.com/news/cooper-delighted-see-yan-dhanda-take-his-chance|archive-date=7 October 2022|url-status=live}}

{{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/talking-tactics-cardiff-city-v-swansea-city-0|title=Talking Tactics: Cardiff City v Swansea City|website=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=11 December 2020|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220810150709/https://www.swanseacity.com/news/talking-tactics-cardiff-city-v-swansea-city-0|archive-date=10 August 2022|url-status=live}} On 2 December 2020, he scored his first goal of the season, in a 2–1 loss against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]].{{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/report-middlesbrough-2-swansea-city-1|title=Report: Middlesbrough 2 Swansea City 1|website=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=2 December 2020|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005085922/https://www.swanseacity.com/news/report-middlesbrough-2-swansea-city-1|archive-date=5 October 2022|url-status=live}} The following month saw Dhanda set up three goals, including one against [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] in the FA Cup match.{{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/report-stevenage-0-swansea-city-2|title=Report: Stevenage 0 Swansea City 2|website=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=9 January 2021|access-date=26 October 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230104222432/https://www.swanseacity.com/news/report-stevenage-0-swansea-city-2|archive-date=4 January 2023|url-status=live}}

Ahead of the 2021–22 season, Dhanda continued to be linked a move away from Swansea City but he ended up staying at the club.{{cite news|title=Swansea City transfer headlines as Anderlecht eye up Yan Dhanda swoop and Thomas Henry, Liam Walsh and Joel Piroe remain on radar|url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/swansea-city-transfer-headlines-anderlecht-20850596|website=Wales Online|date=18 June 2021|access-date=26 October 2024}} Dhanda appeared in the first three league matches of the season, all of them were substitute.{{cite news|title=The mixed Swansea City player ratings as major learning curve ahead, new man grows into game but star starved of service|url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/mixed-swansea-city-player-ratings-21253203|website=Wales Online|date=7 August 2021|access-date=26 October 2024}}

{{cite news|title=Kilmarnock 3-1 Ross County – The Verdict: Player ratings, talking points and star man as Staggies consigned to relegation play-off|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/5780101/kilmarnock-3-1-ross-county-the-verdict-player-ratings-talking-points-and-star-man-as-staggies-consigned-to-relegation-play-off/|website=Press and Journal|date=28 May 2024|access-date=26 October 2024}} In [[2022–23 Scottish Premiership#Final|the league's promotion play-offs]] against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], Dhanda played a vital role when he scored a penalty, set up a goal for [[George Harmon (footballer)|George Harmon]] to bring the match to eventual [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] and scored the first penalty to help Ross County win on penalties to retain their league status for another season.{{cite news|title=Ross County fan view: Yan Dhanda will be pivotal figure in relegation battle|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/5701219/ross-county-fan-view-yan-dhanda-will-be-pivotal-figure-in-relegation-battle/|website=Press and Jourenal|date=8 May 2023|access-date=26 October 2024}}

'''Brad Joseph Lyons''' (born 26 May 1997) is a Northern Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] and the [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland national team]].

==Club career==
Lyons began his career in the Irish Premiership with [[Coleraine F.C.|Coleraine]]. After helping Coleraine win the Irish Cup, in September 2018 he moved on loan to English club [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], with the deal to become permanent in January 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45406445|title=Brad Lyons: Coleraine midfielder completes Blackburn Rovers move|date=4 September 2018|accessdate=5 September 2018|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In January 2019 he signed a permanent 18-month contract,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.belfastlive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/brad-lyons-signs-permanent-deal-15662677|title=Brad Lyons signs permanent deal with Blackburn Rovers|date=11 January 2019|accessdate=11 January 2019|author=Gareth Fullerton|publisher=Belfast Live}}</ref> his first ever professional contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/irish-league/coleraine/i-will-always-love-coleraine-brad-lyons-blackburn-move-made-permanent-37701901.html|title=I will always love Coleraine: offered a new contract by Blackburn at the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rovers.co.uk/news/2020/june/rovers-confirm-retain-list/|title=Rovers confirm Retain List|website=www.rovers.co.uk|date=24 June 2020 }}</ref>

In December 2020 he appeared in a Blackburn Rovers' first-team match day squad for the first time since he signed for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lancs.live/sport/football/football-news/blackburn-rovers-lyons-butterworth-mowbray-19474650|title=Mowbray explains Lyons decision as Butterworth enters first-team fray|first=Jaquob|last=Crooke|date=17 December 2020|website=LancsLive}}</ref> He moved on loan to [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]] in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/18991679.rovers-youngster-lyons-signs-league-two-side-loan/|title=Debut at Chelsea awaits as Rovers youngster makes loan switch|website=Lancashire Telegraph|date=6 January 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55565723|title=Morecambe sign Rovers midfielder Lyons|work=BBC Sport |date=6 January 2021 }}</ref>

On 14 May 2021 it was announced that he would leave Blackburn at the end of the season, following the expiry of his contract.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Rovers confirm Retain List |url=https://www.rovers.co.uk/news/2021/may/rovers-confirm-retain-list/ |publisher=Blackburn Rovers F.C.|date=14 May 2021}}</ref>

On 17 June 2021, it was announced that Lyons would join [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on a two-year deal following the expiry of his Blackburn contract.<ref>{{Cite web|date=17 June 2021|title=Brad Lyons joins Tommy Wright's Killie rebuild|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/brad-lyons-joins-tommy-wrights-killie-rebuild/|url-status=live|access-date=17 June 2021|website=kilmarnockfc.co.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210617205911/https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/brad-lyons-joins-tommy-wrights-killie-rebuild/ |archive-date=17 June 2021 }}</ref> On 7 June 2023, he signed a new two-year contract,<ref>{{cite web| url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/brad-will-be-back/| title=Brad will be back!| work=Kilmarnock FC| date=7 June 2023| access-date=21 February 2025}}</ref> and on 5 April 2024 signed a further new contract to keep him at the club until 2026.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/brad-lyons-extends-contract-with-new-deal/| title=Brad Lyons extends contract with new deal| work=Kilmarnock FC| date=5 April 2024| access-date=21 February 2025}}</ref>

On 28 May 2026, Lyons agreed to join [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on a two-year deal from 1 July.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/en/news/lyons-agrees-move-to-pittodrie|title=Lyons Agrees Move to Pittodrie|website=www.afc.co.uk|date=28 May 2026|accessdate=28 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cdjpkjl9p30o|title=Aberdeen sign Alexander Briedl, Brad Lyons & Lewis Mayo|date=28 May 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==International career==
In August 2023, Lyons received his first call-up to the [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland senior national team]] by head coach [[Michael O'Neill (footballer)|Michael O'Neill]], for two [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying Group H|UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying]] matches against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]] and [[Kazakhstan national football team|Kazakhstan]].<ref>{{cite news |date=29 August 2023 |title=Michael O'Neill reveals Northern Ireland squad for Euro qualifiers |url=https://www.irishfa.com/news/2023/august/michael-o-neill-reveals-squad-for-euro-qualifiers |accessdate=29 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=29 August 2023 |title=Lyons earns first Northern Ireland call-up |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66631382 |access-date=29 August 2023 |website=BBC Sport }}</ref> He made his debut on 17 October 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/international/brad-lyons-playing-for-northern-ireland-is-the-pinnacle-now-ive-got-a-taste-of-it-i-want-more/a58653445.html|title=Brad Lyons: Playing for Northern Ireland is the pinnacle… now I've got a taste of it, I want more|date=18 October 2023|via=www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67143692|title='I'm trying to pinch myself' – Lyons on NI debut|work=BBC Sport |date=18 October 2023 }}</ref>

'''Lewis Smith''' (born 16 March 2000) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

==Club career==
===Hamilton Academical===
Smith attended [[St Ninian's High School, Giffnock]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Lewis Smith selected for Scotland|url=https://blogs.glowscotland.org.uk/er/StNinians/2016/08/31/lewis-smith-selected-for-scotland/|publisher=[[St Ninian's High School, Giffnock]]|date=31 August 2016|accessdate=8 November 2018|archive-date=20 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420031946/https://blogs.glowscotland.org.uk/er/StNinians/2016/08/31/lewis-smith-selected-for-scotland/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was involved with the [[youth system]] at [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], the club his family supported,<ref name=new/><ref name=myson>{{cite news|title=Dani Garavelli: My son the Hamilton Accies baller and what it's like bringing up an aspiring young player|author=Dani Garavelli |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/dani-garavelli-my-son-the-hamilton-accies-baller-and-what-it-s-like-bringing-up-an-aspiring-young-player-1-4999755/|newspaper=The Scotsman|date=8 September 2019|accessdate=10 September 2019}}</ref> from the age of 9.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/lewis-smith-selected-for-scotland-u21s-squad/|title=Lewis Smith Selected for Scotland U21s Squad|date=19 August 2019|website=Hamilton Academical Website|access-date=19 August 2019|archive-date=30 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191130185052/https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/lewis-smith-selected-for-scotland-u21s-squad/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

After signing a professional contract in summer 2016,<ref name=new>{{cite web|title=New full time Academy players|work=Hamilton Academical Website |url=https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/new-full-time-academy-players/|publisher=[[Hamilton Academical F.C.]]|date=26 August 2016|accessdate=8 November 2018}}{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> he appeared for the club's age-restricted teams in three editions of the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]]<ref name=soccerway>{{cite web|title=L. Smith|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/lewis-smith/451117/|website=Soccerway|accessdate=8 November 2018 }}</ref> and in the [[2018–19 UEFA Youth League]],<ref name=soccerway/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bzbasel.ch/sport/basel/mit-dem-ruecken-zur-wand-der-fc-basel-u19-kommt-gegen-hamilton-academical-nicht-ueber-ein-22-hinaus-133539670|title=Mit dem Rücken zur Wand – Der FC Basel U19 kommt gegen Hamilton Academical nicht über ein 2:2 hinaus|trans-title=With backs to the wall - FC Basel U19 did not beat Hamilton Academical, 2–2|language=German|work=[[Basellandschaftliche Zeitung]]|date=4 October 2018|accessdate=8 November 2018}}</ref><ref name=fcb22>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/hamilton-accies-uefa-youth-league-13475206|title=Hamilton Accies UEFA Youth League adventure continues after dramatic penalty victory over Basel|work=Daily Record|date=24 October 2018|accessdate=8 November 2018 }}</ref> before making his debut for the ''Accies'' senior team on 31 October 2018, appearing [[Substitute (association football)|from the bench]] for the last ten minutes of a 3–0 away defeat to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in the [[2018–19 Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Aberdeen 3 – 0 Hamilton Academical |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45961227|work=[[BBC Sport]]|author=Clive Lindsay|date=31 October 2018|accessdate=8 November 2018 }}</ref>

Smith made his first league start for the club on 10 August 2019 against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] at [[New Douglas Park]]; he scored the opening goal and created the second in a 2–0 victory, receiving praise for his performance.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49214574 Hamilton Academical 2–0 Kilmarnock], BBC Sport, 10 August 2019</ref> In November 2019 he signed a new contract with Hamilton, running until summer 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/done-deal-for-lewis-hamilton/|title=Done Deal for Lewis/Hamilton|date=24 November 2019|website=Hamilton Academical Website}}</ref>

A hamstring injury disrupted his season in [[2020–21 Scottish Premiership|2020–21]] as Hamilton were relegated from the Premiership.<ref>[https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/19308680.hamiltons-lewis-smith-determined-use-relegation-pain-accies-promotion-bid-next-season/ Hamilton's Lewis Smith determined to use relegation pain in Accies' promotion bid next season], James Cairney, ''The Herald'', 17 May 2021</ref> He signed a further contract extension, until summer 2024, in November 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/lewis-smith-commits-new-hamilton-25442711|title=Hamilton hand Lewis Smith new deal until 2024|first=Scott|last=Burns|date=12 November 2021|website=Daily Record}}</ref> The club were relegated from the [[Scottish Championship]] in 2023, but Smith had an important role as they returned via the [[2023–24 Scottish Championship#Championship play-offs|promotion play-offs]] a year later, scoring in wins over [[Alloa Athletic]] and [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>[https://news.stv.tv/sport/hamilton-claim-play-off-glory-to-replace-inverness-in-scottish-championship Hamilton claim play-off glory to replace Inverness in Championship], ''STV News'', 18 May 2024</ref>

===Livingston===
In May 2024, Smith signed a pre-contract with [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], effective from 1 June, on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/lewis-smith-is-a-lion/|title=Lewis Smith is a Lion!|website=livingstonfc.co.uk|date=24 May 2024}}</ref>

===Aberdeen===
In July 2026 he transferred to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cx23x14n2z5o|title=Aberdeen buy winger Lewis Smith from Livingston|date=13 July 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==International career==
Smith has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] youth level;<ref>{{SFA player|201209}}</ref> he sat four of his [[Higher (Scottish)|Higher]] school exams while on international duty at the [[2017 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]] in Croatia.<ref name=myson/> In August 2019 he was called-up by the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] squad,<ref name="auto"/> making his debut in September 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/lewis-smith-makes-scotland-u21-debut/|title=Lewis Smith Makes Scotland U21 Debut|date=5 September 2019|website=Hamilton Academical Website}}</ref>
