He previously appeared at the semi-professional level for [[Birmingham Hammers]], [[Reading United AC|Reading United]], and [[Dayton Dutch Lions]] and as a professional with [[Columbus Crew]], [[Atlanta United FC|Atlanta United]], [[Atlanta United 2]], [[Birmingham Legion FC|Birmingham Legion]], [[FC Tulsa]], [[Phoenix Rising FC|Phoenix Rising]], [[Tampa Bay Rowdies]] and [[Rhode Island FC|Rhode Island]]. Although he was born in [[Clovis, New Mexico]], Williams grew up in [[Montgomery, Alabama]], and attended [[Alabama Christian Academy]]. After scoring 122 goals while in high school, he spent three years playing at the [[University of Kentucky]]. Williams was a first team all-American and the C-USA Men's Soccer Player of the Year in 2018. He also spent time during the collegiate offseason with Birmingham Hammers, Reading United, and Dayton Dutch Lions. Williams signed a [[Generation Adidas]] contract with Major League Soccer ahead of the [[2019 MLS SuperDraft]] and was selected in the first round by Columbus Crew. He spent most of his rookie year on loan to Birmingham Legion before being waived by the Crew ahead of the [[2020 Major League Soccer season|2020 season]], eventually finding his way to Atlanta United. ==Early life== Born in [[Clovis, New Mexico]], Williams moved to Alabama as a child and grew up in [[Montgomery, Alabama|Montgomery]].{{cite news|last=Hall|first=Erik|url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/high-school/soccer/2020/07/10/jj-williams-facts-atlanta-united-alabama-christian-academy-soccer-mls/5414464002/|title=4 things to know about Atlanta United, former Alabama Christian soccer forward JJ Williams|website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]]|publisher=[[Gannett]]|access-date=January 29, 2021|date=July 10, 2020|url-access=limited}} He began playing soccer at the age of nine, joining the Capital City Streaks youth club and playing for regional Olympic Development Program teams.{{cite news|last=Dunn|first=Graham|url=http://riverregionsports.com/wordpress/?p=18068|title=Former ACA soccer star Williams makes history as first local player taken in MLS draft|website=River Region Sports|access-date=February 14, 2019|date=January 12, 2019}}{{dead link|date=January 2021}}{{cite news|last=Bernal|first=Ethan|url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/high-school/soccer/2015/03/22/acas-jj-williams-plays-soccer-overseas/25174427/|title=ACA's J.J. Williams plays soccer overseas|website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]]|publisher=[[Gannett]]|access-date=February 14, 2019|date=March 21, 2015|url-access=limited}} Williams attended [[Alabama Christian Academy]], playing three years on [[Varsity team|varsity]] for the Eagles. He combined for 57 goals across his sophomore and junior seasons before breaking out as a senior with 65 goals and 20 assists.{{cite news|last=Long|first=A. Stacy|url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/2019/01/15/for-alabama-christian-j-j-williams-making-mls-columbus-crew-first-round-queue-a-dream-come-true/2577515002/|title=For ACA's Williams, making Crew's first-round queue 'a dream come true'|website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]]|publisher=[[Gannett]]|access-date=February 14, 2019|date=January 15, 2019|url-access=limited}} Williams was a two-time All-Metro player of the year in Montgomery and was named as the 2016 [[Alabama High School Athletic Association|AHSAA]] Boys Soccer Player of the Year.{{cite news|last=Bean|first=Josh|url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/alabama-christians-jj-williams-named-states-best-boys-high-school-soccer-by-gatorade/|title=Alabama Christian's J.J. Williams named state's best boys high school soccer by Gatorade|website=[[AL.com]]|publisher=[[Advance Publications]]|access-date=February 14, 2019|date=May 10, 2016}} At club level, Williams appeared for Vestavia Hills Soccer Club, winning three State Cup championships.{{cite web|url=https://ukathletics.com/sports/mens-soccer/roster/jj-williams/6591|title=JJ Williams – Kentucky profile|website=[[Kentucky Wildcats]]|date=August 10, 2017 |publisher=[[University of Kentucky]]|access-date=February 15, 2019}} He committed to play [[College soccer in the United States|college soccer]] at the [[University of Kentucky]], one of seven members of the 2016 class for the Wildcats.{{cite news|last=Bernal|first=Ethan|url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/high-school/prepsports/2016/02/10/alabama-christians-jj-williams-signs-kentucky/80201156/|title=Alabama Christian's J.J. He was not initially on the roster, but was added midway through the [[2016 NPSL season|2016 season]] and made his debut on June 12 against [[Nashville FC]].{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BGkdzrEtLst/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/BGkdzrEtLst |archive-date=2021-12-24 |url-access=limited|title=Tonight's starting XI for tonight's match against Nashville FC! #hammerdown #lovemyhammers|website=[[Instagram]]|access-date=February 11, 2019|date=June 12, 2016}}{{cbignore}} In his second match for the Hammers, Williams was [[Red card (association football)|sent off]] in the 72nd minute of a 2–0 defeat against [[Chattanooga FC]] after a collision with Chattanooga goalkeeper Greg Hartley.{{cite news|url=https://www.npsl.com/6734/|title=NPSL Game of the Week: Chattanooga defeats Birmingham 2–0 in front of 4,293|website=[[National Premier Soccer League]]|access-date=February 11, 2019|date=June 19, 2016}} He finished the season with five appearances for Birmingham. ==College and amateur== On August 26, 2016, Williams came off the bench to make his [[Kentucky Wildcats men's soccer|Kentucky]] debut in a 4–0 victory against [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's soccer|Marquette]].{{cite web|url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/ukathletics.com/documents/2016/8/27/082716%20Marquette.pdf|title=Marquette 0–4 Kentucky|website=[[Kentucky Wildcats]]|publisher=[[University of Kentucky]]|access-date=February 15, 2019|date=August 26, 2016}}

In the [[Eastern Conference (USL Championship)|Eastern Conference]] play-in match against [[North Carolina FC]], Williams provided the winning goal: his strike three minutes into [[stoppage time]] handed Birmingham a 3–2 victory in their first-ever playoff game.{{cite news|last=Wray|first=Cheryl|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2019/10/birmingham-legion-fc-earns-road-win-in-usl-playoffs.html|title=Birmingham Legion FC earns road win in USL playoffs|website=[[AL.com]]|publisher=[[Advance Publications]]|access-date=November 21, 2019|date=October 23, 2019}} On the season, Williams made nine appearances in Columbus and tallied eight goals from 23 matches with Birmingham.{{Soccerway|jerome-williams/484027|accessdate=February 7, 2019}} He was waived by the Crew on February 20, 2020. A lack of potential playing time, with Williams sitting fourth on the depth chart at the forward position, was cited by the club as the reason behind the move.{{cite news|last=Myers|first=Jacob|url=https://www.dispatch.com/sports/20200220/columbus-crew-waives-forward-jj-williams-2019-first-round-draft-pick|title=Columbus Crew waives forward JJ Williams, 2019 first-round draft pick|website=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]|publisher=[[Gannett]]|access-date=February 20, 2020|date=February 20, 2020|archive-date=February 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200221053039/https://www.dispatch.com/sports/20200220/columbus-crew-waives-forward-jj-williams-2019-first-round-draft-pick|url-status=dead}} ===Atlanta United and loan spells=== Although Williams had been waived by the Crew, his rights were still owned by [[Major League Soccer]] for another year, owing to his Generation Adidas contract. After passing through the league's waiver system on February 27, it was announced that he would return to Birmingham Legion for the 2020 season, officially on a loan from MLS.{{cite news|last=Humphries|first=Clayton|url=https://www.bhmlegion.com/news_article/show/1090741|title=Forward JJ Williams rejoins Legion FC on loan from Major League Soccer|website=[[Birmingham Legion FC]]|publisher=[[United Soccer League]]|access-date=February 27, 2020|date=February 27, 2020}}{{Dead link|date=June 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} The league retained the ability to recall Williams at any time if an MLS club had committed to signing him, and they exercised that right exactly one week later. On March 5, he instead joined [[Atlanta United FC|Atlanta United]], arriving as a replacement for the injured [[Josef Martínez]].{{cite news|last=Humphries|first=Clayton|url=https://www.bhmlegion.com/news_article/show/1092830|title=JJ Williams signed by Atlanta United FC|website=[[Birmingham Legion FC]]|publisher=[[United Soccer League]]|access-date=March 5, 2020|date=March 5, 2020|archive-date=April 8, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210408113315/https://www.bhmlegion.com/news_article/show/1092830|url-status=dead}}
{{cite news|last=Goodman|first=Joseph|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2020/03/alabama-soccer-star-signs-with-mls-giant-atlanta-united.html|title=Alabama soccer star signs with MLS giant Atlanta United|website=[[AL.com]]|publisher=[[Advance Publications]]|access-date=March 5, 2020|date=March 5, 2020}} Williams made his lone appearance for the club on July 16 in the [[MLS is Back Tournament]], receiving a [[Red card (association football)|red card]] in second-half stoppage time in a 1–0 loss against [[FC Cincinnati]].{{cite news|url=https://www.gwinnettdailypost.com/sports/atlanta-united-in-deep-hole-in-mls-is-back-tournament-after-1-0-loss-to/article_22d11c08-c798-11ea-919b-3f4df3123366.html|title=Atlanta United in deep hole in MLS is Back Tournament after 1–0 loss to FC Cincinnati|website=[[Gwinnett Daily Post]]|publisher=Southern Community Newspapers Inc.|access-date=July 16, 2020|date=July 16, 2020}} After playing news|last=Soto|first=Kyle|url=https://www.dirtysouthsoccer.com/2020/9/3/21419202/jj-williams-leaves-first-team-joins-atl-utd-2|title=JJ Williams leaves first team, joins ATL UTD 2|website=Dirty South Soccer|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|access-date=September 14, 2020|date=September 3, 2020}} Williams returned on loan to Birmingham Legion for the remainder of the 2020 season.{{cite news|last=Humphries|first=Clayton|url=https://www.bhmlegion.com/news_article/show/1122022|title=Forward JJ Williams rejoins Legion FC on loan for remainder of season|website=[[Birmingham Legion the bench in a 3–1 defeat against [[Charlotte Independence]].{{cite news|last=Humphries|first=Clayton|url=https://www.bhmlegion.com/news_article/show/1122338|title=Match Recap: Legion FC knocked off He was left out of Atlanta's preliminary squad for the resumption of the [[2020 CONCACAF Champions League]] and subsequently had his contract option declined on November 24.{{cite news|author=Atlanta United Communications|url=https://www.atlutd.com/post/2020/11/20/atlanta-united-announces-provisional-roster-scotiabank-concacaf-champions-league|title=Atlanta United announces provisional roster for Scotiabank Concacaf Champions League|website=[[Atlanta United FC]]|publisher=[[Major League Soccer]]|accessdate=February 3, 2021|date=November 20, 2020}}{{cite news|last=Roberson|first=Doug|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-united/atlanta-united-lets-go-of-carleton-several-other-players/HUKZAK4JXRDJXIOZ4VGB6HN3BM/|title=Atlanta United lets Carleton go, keeps Bello|website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|publisher=[[Cox Enterprises]]|accessdate=February 3, 2021|date=November 24, 2020}} ===Birmingham Legion=== After two previous loan spells in Birmingham, Williams signed permanently for the Legion on January 19, 2021. In the announcement press release, he expressed his excitement "to give [his] full focus to one team."{{cite news|last=Sadowey|first=Gunnar|url=https://mybhmsports.com/legion-fc-sign-jj-williams/|title=Legion FC sign JJ Williams|website=Birmingham Sports|access-date=January 19, 2021}} On his third debut for the club, Williams picked up a red card in the [[2021 Birmingham Legion FC season|season]] opener against [[Indy Eleven]].{{cite news|last=Fuller|first=John|url=https://www.thefootballforge.com/2021/05/04/did-jj-williams-deserve-the-red-card/|title=Did JJ Williams deserve the red card?|website=The Football Forge|access-date=July 14, 2022|date=May 4, 2021}} He tallied five goals and four assists from 28 appearances in all competitions, helping Birmingham qualify for the [[2021 USL Championship Playoffs]]. Those stats featured a pair of goal-and-assist games, including as part of a 3–1 victory against Atlanta United 2, his former club, on August 4.{{cite news|url=https://www.dirtysouthsoccer.com/atlanta-united-2-usl-reserves-news/2021/8/5/22610431/a-tale-of-two-halves-as-atlanta-united-2-falls-3-1-to-birmingham-legion|title=A tale of two halves as Atlanta United 2 falls 3–1 to Birmingham Legion|website=Dirty South Soccer|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|access-date=July 14, 2022|date=August 5, 2021}} Following the season, Williams had his contract option declined by Birmingham.{{cite press release|url=https://www.bhmlegion.com/news/2021/12/01/legion-fc-announces-year-end-roster-updates/|title=Legion FC Announces Year-End Roster Updates|publisher=[[Birmingham Legion FC]]|location=[[Birmingham, Alabama]]|access-date=December 10, 2021|date=December 1, 2021}} ===FC Tulsa=== On January 27, 2022, Williams signed elsewhere in the Championship with [[FC Tulsa]].{{cite press release|url=https://www.fctulsa.com/news/2022/01/27/fc-tulsa-signs-dynamic-former-mls-first-round-pick-jj-williams/|title=FC Tulsa Signs Former MLS First Round Pick JJ Williams|publisher=[[FC Tulsa]]|location=[[Tulsa, Oklahoma]]|access-date=January 27, 2022|date=January 27, 2022}} ===Phoenix Rising=== On July 27, 2022, Williams was traded to fellow Championship club [[Phoenix Rising FC]] in exchange for [[Marcus Epps (soccer)|Marcus Epps]]. Petersburg, Florida]]|access-date=January 11, 2023|date=January 11, 2023}} ===Rhode Island FC=== Williams was unveiled as the first forward on [[Rhode Island FC]]'s inaugural squad on December 4, 2023.{{cite press release|author=Rowdies Communications|url=https://www.rowdiessoccer.com/news/2023/12/04/rowdies-transfer-jj-williams-to-rhode-island/|title= Rowdies Transfer JJ Williams to Rhode Republic FC]].{{Cite web |title=The Long Path to a Joyous Moment |url=https://www.rhodeislandfc.com/news/the-long-path-to-a-joyous-moment/ |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Rhode Island FC |language=en-US}} Williams' importance to the team increased over the course of the season, and he finished with 6 regular-season goals and 6 assists.{{Cite web |date=2026-08-18 |title=Rhode Island FC Agree to Transfer JJ Williams to Heart of Midlothian F.C. |url=https://tidetalkri.com/rhode-island-fc-reportedly-agree-to-transfer-jj-williams-to-heart-of-midlothian-f-c/ |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Tide Talk |language=en}} Williams scored a first-half hat trick in Rhode Island's 8–1 season finale win against [[Miami FC]],{{Cite web |title=Sellout Crowd Sees Rhode Island FC Conclude Inaugural Regular Season With Largest Win in Club History |url=https://www.rhodeislandfc.com/news/sellout-crowd-sees-rhode-island-fc-conclude-inaugural-regular-season-with-largest-win-in-club-history/ |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Rhode Island FC |language=en-US}} and followed up by scoring all three team goals in their first playoff game at [[Indy Eleven]].{{Cite web |title=Rhode Island FC Defeats Indy Eleven in First-Ever Playoff Match |url=https://www.rhodeislandfc.com/news/rhode-island-fc-defeats-indy-eleven-in-first-ever-playoff-match/ |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Rhode Island FC |language=en-US}} With two additional playoff goals, Williams tied for the team lead with eleven goals across all competitions, and helped lead the team to the 2024 USL Eastern Conference Championship.{{Cite web |title=Rhode Island FC Wins USL Championship Eastern Conference Title |url=https://www.rhodeislandfc.com/news/rhode-island-fc-wins-usl-championship-eastern-conference-title/ |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Rhode Island FC |language=en-US}} He was named USL Championship Player of the Month for October 2024.{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=USLChampionship com |date=2024-10-31 in goals scored in all competitions in 2025, with a team-lead 6 in the regular season and 8 overall. Had his goal against Miami FC not been wiped out due to a Miami forfeit,{{Cite web |title=Rhode Island FC Jumps Above Playoff Line with Come-From-Behind 3-1 Win vs. Las Vegas Lights FC |url=https://www.rhodeislandfc.com/news/rhode-island-fc-jumps-above-playoff-line-with-come-from-behind-3-1-win-vs-las-vegas-lights-fc/ |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Rhode Island FC |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |title=USL Championship issues forfeit to Las Vegas Lights FC for use of ineligible player |url=https://www.rhodeislandfc.com/news/usl-championship-issues-forfeit-to-las-vegas-lights-fc-for-use-of-ineligible-player/ |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Rhode Island FC |language=en-US}} he would have led the team in total goals scored in all competitions. Williams appeared in 18 regular-season games including the forfeit, missing time in the mid-season due to injury. Williams ranked first in Rhode Island FC history with 30 goals and two hat tricks across all competitions, and second with 13 assists. He also led the club with 11 selections to the USL Championship Team of the Week. === Heart of Midlothian === Williams' transfer was announced by [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on August 25, 2026,{{Cite web |title=JJ Joins Jambos – Hearts |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/jj-joins-jambos |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=www.heartsfc.co.uk |language=en}} and he made his team debut in the 71st minute in Hearts' derby game with Hibernian FC on September 3, 2026.{{Cite news |last=Martin |first=Robert |date=September 3, 2026 |title=DERBY DOMINATION Hibs 1 Hearts 3: Jambos make it THREE derby wins in a row as bragging rights head for Gorgie |url=https://www.thescottishsun.co.uk/sport/16775956/hibs-hearts-three-derby-wins-in-a-row-edinburgh-derby/ |access-date=September 6, 2026 |work=The Scottish Sun}} He scored his first goal for Hearts against Stenhousemuir in the League Cup. ==Personal life== Williams is the youngest of four siblings. '''Mats Knoester''' (born 19 November 1998) is a Dutch professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref name = "WF">{{Worldfootball.net|mats-knoester|new_id=pe351863}}</ref>

==Club career==
Knoester joined the [[Feyenoord]] youth academy and developed there for 14 years, before transferring to [[Heracles Almelo|Heracles]] on 17 January 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.voetbalzone.nl/doc.asp?uid=344911|title=Heracles pikt 'talentvolle verdediger' op bij Feyenoord: 'Veel zin in'|date=17 January 2019|website=Voetbalzone}}</ref> Knoester made his professional debut with Heracles in a 1–0 [[Eredivisie]] win over [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] on 9 February 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://intsoccerway.com/matches/2019/02/09/netherlands/eredivisie/stichting-heracles-almelo/afc-ajax/2794108/|title=Heracles vs. Ajax - 9 February 2019|website=Soccerway}}</ref>

On 26 May 2022, Knoester signed with [[Ferencvárosi TC|Ferencváros]] in Hungary.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Ferencváros|url=https://www.fradi.hu/en/football/men-s/news/we-have-signed-a-dutch-youth-national-team-defender|title=WE HAVE SIGNED A DUTCH YOUTH NATIONAL TEAM DEFENDER|date=26 May 2022|access-date=21 July 2022}}</ref> On 5 May 2023, he won the [[2022–23 Nemzeti Bajnokság I]] with Ferencváros, after [[Kecskeméti TE|Kecskemét]] lost 1–0 to [[Budapest Honvéd FC|Honvéd]] at the [[Bozsik Aréna]] on the 30th matchday.<ref>{{Cite web |last=nemzetisport.hu |date=2023-05-05 |title=NB I: a Ferencváros megszerezte 34. bajnoki címét - NSO |url=https://www.nemzetisport.hu/labdarugo_nb_i/nb-i-a-ferencvaros-megszerezte-34-bajnoki-cimet-2955187 |access-date=2023-05-06 |website=NSO.hu |language=hu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Summary - NB I - Hungary - Results, fixtures, tables and news - Soccerway |url=https://int.soccerway.com/national/hungary/nb-i/20222023/regular-season/r69309/ |access-date=2023-05-06 |website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref>

On 1 September 2023, Knoester joined [[Aarhus Gymnastikforening|AGF]] in Denmark on a one-year loan deal with a purchase option.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Ferencváros|url=https://agf.dk/nyheder/2023/september/ny-mand-mats-pa-plads|title=NY MAND: MATS PÅ PLADS|date=1 September 2023|access-date=1 September 2023}}</ref>

On 3 February 2025, Knoester joined Scottish Premiership side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] after his contract expired with Ferencváros.<ref>https://www.afc.co.uk/2025/02/03/dutch-defender-joins-on-deadline-day/</ref> In May, he won the Scottish Cup and was given the Man of the Match award, stating it was the best moment of his career to date.<ref>pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/6764958/mats-knoester-scottish-cup-win-career-highlight/</ref> In June, he signed a long-term contract lasting until at least 2029.<ref>https://www.afc.co.uk/2025/06/03/defender-signs-contract-extension-with-the-dons/</ref>

'''Kristers Tobers''' (born 13 December 2000) is a Latvian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] or [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] and [[Captain (association football)|captains]] the [[Latvia national football team|Latvia national team]].<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|kristers-tobers}}</ref>

==Career==
===Club career===
In January 2020, he joined [[Lechia Gdańsk]] on a loan with an option of permanent transfer after the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://lechia.pl/aktualnosci/kristers-tobers-nowym-pilkarzem-lechii-16617 |title=Kristers Tobers nowym piłkarzem Lechii! |access-date=14 February 2020 |archive-date=4 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200204033350/http://lechia.pl/aktualnosci/kristers-tobers-nowym-pilkarzem-lechii-16617 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 7 February 2020 he made his [[Ekstraklasa]] debut against [[Śląsk Wrocław]] playing as a midfielder. After only seven games, Lechia triggered the option and Tobers signed a permanent deal until June 2023.<ref>[https://sportowefakty.wp.pl/pilka-nozna/883172/pko-ekstraklasa-kristers-tobers-zostal-wykupiony-lechia-gdansk-zwiazala-sie-na-d PKO Ekstraklasa. Kristers Tobers został wykupiony. Lechia Gdańsk związała się na dłużej z Łotyszem], sportowefakty.wp.pl, 22 May 2020</ref>

On 2 July 2023, he signed with [[Switzerland|Swiss]] record champion [[Grasshopper Club Zürich|Grasshoppers]], who play in the [[Swiss Super League]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[Grasshopper Club Zürich]]|url=https://www.gcz.ch/en/news/article/17/gc-zurich-signs-kristers-tobers/|title=GC Zurich signs Kristers Tobers|date=3 July 2023|accessdate=3 July 2023}}</ref> He signed a two-year contract with an option to extend. He quickly established himself as the lead in Grasshopper's defense, as he started in 32 games for the club.<ref name="Soccerway">{{soccerway}}</ref>

On 24 August 2024, he finally scored his first goal for Grasshoppers, a skillful volley into the upper right corner of the goal, in a 3–1 victory over [[FC Sion]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.srf.ch/sport/fussball/super-league/1-super-league-sieg-tatsache-tor-premieren-fuer-lee-und-tobers-gc-schlaegt-sion-mit-3-1|title=Tor-Premieren für Lee und Tobers: GC schlägt Sion mit 3:1|publisher=[[Schweizer Radio und Fernsehen|SRF]]|date=24 August 2024|access-date=24 August 2024}}</ref>

On 8 January 2025, he transferred to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in the [[Scottish Premiership]],<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[Grasshopper Club Zurich]]|url=https://www.gcz.ch/en/news/article/1/kristers-tobers-leaves-gc-zuerich/|title=Kristers Tobers leaves GC Zurich|date=9 January 2025|access-date=9 January 2025}}</ref> for a reported £700,000.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Aberdeen Live|first=Ruaraidh|last=Britton|url=https://www.aberdeenlive.news/sport/football/kristers-tobers-fee-agreed-latvia-9845294|title=Kristers Tobers fee agreed as Latvia captain due to arrive in Aberdeen today|date=8 January 2025|access-date=9 January 2025}}</ref> He signed a three-and-a-half-year deal with "The Dons".<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[Aberdeen F.C.]]|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2025/01/08/latvia-captain-makes-move-to-the-dons/|title= Latvia Captain Makes Move to the Dons |date=9 January 2025|access-date=9 January 2025}}</ref>

===International career===
Tobers made his international debut for [[Latvia national football team|Latvia]] on 21 March 2019, coming on as a substitute for [[Artūrs Karašausks]] in the 68th minute of the [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying]] match against [[North Macedonia national football team|North Macedonia]], which finished as a 1–3 away loss.<ref name="EUF">{{cite web |url=https://eu-football.info/_player.php?id=30601 |title=Kristers Tobers |website=EU-Football.info |access-date=29 January 2019}}</ref>

Ahead of their [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying Group D|UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying]] games in June 2023, he was chosen to captain the national team, by coach [[Dainis Kazakevičs]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[Grasshopper Club Zürich]]|url=https://sportacentrs.com/futbols/legionari/03072023-izlases_kapteinis_tobers_karjeru_turpinas|title=National team captain Tober will continue his career in the Swiss club "Grasshopper".|date=3 July 2023|accessdate=3 July 2023}}</ref> In his first match as captain, he scored his first international goal, the 2–2 equalizer, against [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]].

'''Joshua McPake''' (born 31 August 2001) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[winger (association football)|winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

McPake started his career at Rangers and has had several loans spells with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]], [[Harrogate Town A.F.C.|Harrogate Town]], [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]], [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] and [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] respectively. After departing Rangers, he played for [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]] on a short-term deal, before joining St Johnstone the following season.

==Club career==
===Rangers===
====Early career====
A youth product of [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] who was their Academy Player of the Year for 2018–19<ref name=poty>[https://rangers.co.uk/news/headlines/mcpake-is-academy-poty/ McPake Is Academy POTY], Rangers FC, 7 April 2019</ref> having won the [[SPFL Reserve League]], the Under-18 League and the [[Scottish Youth Cup]] in that season<ref name=ext/> plus the [[Glasgow Cup]] in the prior campaign,<ref name=poty/> McPake signed a new contract on 10 July 2019, which will keep him at the club until the summer of 2022.<ref name=ext>{{ Cite news | url=https://rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/mcpake-signs-contract-extension/| work=Rangers.co.uk | publisher=Rangers Football Club| date=10 July 2019| title=McPake Signs Contract Extension }}</ref> A week later he made his debut in a qualifying match against Gibraltese [[St Joseph's F.C.|St Joseph's]] at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]], coming on as a 67th minute substitute for [[Greg Docherty]].<ref name=":0">{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48970483 | title=Rangers 6-0 St Joseph's | first=Jamie | last=Lyall | work=BBC Sport | date=18 July 2019 }}</ref>

====Loan spells====
On 20 August 2019, McPake joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a loan until the following January.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/josh-joins-on-loan/|title=Josh joins on loan|last=|first=|date=20 August 2019|website=dundeefc.co.uk|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=20 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49389042 |title=Josh McPake: Rangers winger joins Dundee on loan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 August 2019 |accessdate=20 August 2019}}</ref> After an ankle injury hindered his progress with the Dark Blues, McPake spent the last few weeks of his loan spell back at Rangers, and officially returned in January.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/josh-returns-to-rangers/|title=Josh returns to Rangers|last=|first=|date=13 January 2020|website=dundeefc.co.uk|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=13 January 2020}}</ref>

In September 2020, McPake joined [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] on loan until January with an option to extend.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=25 September 2020|title=Josh McPake signs on-loan deal with 'Ton|url=https://www.gmfc.net/josh-mcpake-signs-on-loan-deal-with-ton/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=25 September 2020|website=gmfc.net}}</ref> On 8 January 2021, McPake joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Harrogate Town A.F.C.|Harrogate Town]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2020–21 Harrogate Town A.F.C. season|2020–21 season]].<ref>{{Cite news |url= https://www.harrogatetownafc.com/news-media/exciting-winger-josh-mcpake-joins-from-rangers/ |title=Exciting winger Josh McPake joins from Rangers |publisher=Harrogate Town FC |date=8 January 2021}}</ref> McPake impressed during his loan spell with Harrogate, making 21 appearances for the club.<ref name=newdeal />

On 1 July 2021, McPake signed a new contract with Rangers until summer 2024 and immediately joined newly-promoted [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]], with a recall option in January 2022.<ref name=newdeal>{{cite web|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/josh-mcpake-signs-new-deal/373DneEBOoGLuGfMJr9BAW|title=Josh McPake Signs New Deal|website=Rangers F.C.|date=1 July 2021|accessdate=1 July 2021}}</ref>

On 5 January 2022, McPake joined [[EFL League Two]] side [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] on loan for the remainder of [[2021-22 EFL League Two|2021–22]] season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.tranmererovers.co.uk/news/2022/january/josh-mcpake-joins-on-loan-from-rangers/ |title=Josh McPake joins on loan from Rangers |publisher=Tranmere Rovers FC |date=5 January 2022 |accessdate=5 January 2022}}</ref>

On 23 July 2022, McPake joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cairns |first=Ian |date=2022-07-23 |title=Josh McPake signs on Season Long loan |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/josh-mcpake-signs-on-season-long-loan/ |access-date=2022-07-23 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref> He would make his debut for the club the same day in a [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage game against [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hamilton Academical v Queen's Park |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62210582 |access-date=2022-07-23}}</ref> McPake would net his first and second goals for the ''Spiders'' in a thrashing away victory over [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in October.<ref>{{Cite news |title=McPake brace helps Queen's Park hammer Thistle |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63267373 |access-date=2022-10-22}}</ref>

On 1 September 2023, McPake left Rangers by mutual consent.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-01 |title=Rangers confirm Josh McPake contract decision as winger exits Ibrox |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/23763131.rangers-confirm-josh-mcpake-transfer-exit-winger-pens-message/ |access-date=2023-09-03 |website=HeraldScotland |language=en}}</ref>

=== Stirling Albion ===
After training with clubs such as [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] after being released by Rangers,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Collin |first=Iain |date=2024-01-30 |title=Dunfermline boss James McPake delighted to snap up Blackpool striker as he runs rule over ex-Rangers winger |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/4882167/dunfermline-fc-brad-holmes-blackpool-rangers-mcpake/ |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> McPake signed a deal on 23 February 2024 with [[Scottish League One]] club [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gallacher |first=Scott |title=Stirling Albion Sign Josh McPake - SAFC |url=https://www.stirlingalbionfc.co.uk/stirling-albion-sign-josh-mcpake/ |access-date=2024-02-23 |language=en-GB}}</ref> McPake made his debut the following day against [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]], and marked his first game as a ''Bino'' with a free kick goal in a 4–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Stirling Albion v Edinburgh City |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68324525 |access-date=2024-02-24 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== St Johnstone ===
On 20 June 2024 following a successful trial period, McPake joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Josh McPake signs for Saints |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/ |access-date=2024-06-20 |website=St Johnstone Football Club |language=en}}</ref> He made his debut for the ''Saints'' in a victory over [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brechin City vs St. Johnstone: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/czd9kz3nv0wt |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 5 January 2025, McPake scored his first St Johnstone goal in a losing effort at home to his former loan club Dundee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=St Johnstone vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership report, reaction & stats |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4gpy30j1y9t |access-date=2025-01-05 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 2 August 2025, McPake scored a hat-trick in a 5–1 home win over Partick Thistle.<ref name=":0" /> After scoring 4 goals in as many games to start the season, McPake was awarded the [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners|SPFL Championship Player of the Month]] award for August 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=McPake named Player of the Month {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/mcpake-named-player-of-the-month |access-date=2025-09-14 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> McPake would score 19 goals in all competitions for the ''Saints'', finishing as the Championship's top scorer and winning the [[Scottish Championship]] with St Johnstone.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saints secure Championship title {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/saints-secure-championship-title |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> Individually, McPake won both the [[SPFL]] and [[PFA Scotland]] Championship player of the year awards and was named in PFA Scotland's [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year|PFA Scotland's Championship Team of the Year]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Championship award for McPake {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/championship-award-for-mcpake |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref><ref name="PFA POTY">{{Cite web |title=Josh McPake wins PFA Scotland Championship Player of the Year award {{!}} ST JOHNSTONE FC |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/josh-mcpake-wins-pfa-scotland-championship-player-of-the-year/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Luke |date=2026-04-17 |title=Championship Team of the Year |url=https://pfascotland.co.uk/championship-team-of-the-year/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=PFA Scotland |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===

McPake agreed to join [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[HMFC|Heart of Midlothian]] on a three-year deal at the beginning of the 2026–27 season, when his contract with St Johnstone was due to expire.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date=15 January 2026 |title=Josh McPake to join Hearts next season |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/josh-mcpake-to-join-hearts-next-season |website=Heart of Midlothian F.C. |location=Edinburgh, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=12 March 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
McPake has played for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] at youth level, representing the under 17s, under 18s and under 19s.<ref>[https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=233835&lid=13 Joshua McPake], [[Scottish Football Association]]</ref> He received his first-ever senior call-up in September 2026 when he was named in the squad for the [[2026–27 UEFA Nations League B|UEFA Nations League]] qualifiers against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]], [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] and [[North Macedonia national football team|North Macedonia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/ckjrxzg9wg77o|title=Hearts winger Josh McPake has 'more to give' after Scotland call|date=16 September 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cmx2z1jldpnzo|title=Josh McPake's 'colourful' journey from club-less to Scotland call-up in three years|last=Canavan|first=Amy|date=22 September 2026|website=BBC Sport|access-date=22 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-star-backed-to-reach-top-level-soaring-confidence-rising-through-roof-9131328|title=Hearts ace backed to reach 'top level' amid confidence that's rising through the roof|date=22 September 2026|website=Edinburgh News}}</ref> He made his international debut on 6 October in their home match against Slovenia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Scotland 1–2 Slovenia {{!}} UEFA Nations League |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cm4gkgyz44rzt |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=6 October 2026 |date=6 October 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Tochi Phil Chukwuani''' (born 24 March 2003) is a Danish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].

==Club career==
===Nordsjælland===
Born in [[Herlev]] to [[Igbo people|Igbo]] Nigerian parents,<ref name="euroman" /> Chukwuani started playing football in the youth at B1973 Herlev and later [[Boldklubben af 1893|B.93]] before moving to the youth academy of [[Danish Superliga|Superliga]] club [[FC Nordsjælland]]. He practiced with the first team at age 14, and head coach [[Flemming Pedersen (football manager)|Flemming Pedersen]] stated that he was "one of the top players of the future".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Blond |first1=Mikael |title=FCN-træner teaser: 16-årig stortalent er på vej |url=https://www.bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/fcn-traener-teaser-16-aarig-stortalent-er-paa-vej/ |accessdate=29 October 2020 |work=bold.dk |date=4 August 2018 |language=Danish}}</ref> In July 2019, Chukwuani signed a three-year contract, keeping him in Nordsjælland until 2022.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schmidt |first1=Martin |title=FC Nordsjælland forlænger med 16-årig midt |url=https://www.bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/fc-nordsjaelland-forlaenger-med-16-aarig-midt/ |accessdate=29 October 2020 |work=bold.dk |date=25 July 2019 |language=Danish}}</ref>

On 22 September 2019, Chukwuani made his professional debut in the Superliga in a 2–1 home win over [[AaB Fodbold|AaB]], thereby becoming the sixth youngest player to appear in a game in the league.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schmidt |first1=Martin |title=FCN-boss roser 16-årig: AGF slipper for ham |url=https://www.bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/fcn-boss-roser-16-aarig-agf-slipper-for-ham/ |accessdate=29 October 2020 |work=bold.dk |date=23 September 2019 |language=Danish}}</ref> He came on as a substitute in the 82nd minute for [[Magnus Kofod Andersen]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hebo |first1=Benjamin Alexander |title=Chanceorgie da FC Nordsjælland slog AaB |url=https://www.bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/chanceorgie-da-fc-nordsjaelland-slog-aab/ |accessdate=29 October 2020 |work=bold.dk |date=22 September 2019 |language=Danish}}</ref> On 17 July 2020, Chukwuani scored his first senior goal in a 6–3 away loss to eventual champions [[FC Midtjylland|Midtjylland]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Frigaard |first1=Anders |title=MINUT FOR MINUT Midtjylland tager sejren i målfest mod Nordsjælland |url=https://www.dr.dk/sporten/fodbold/superliga/minut-minut-midtjylland-tager-sejren-i-maalfest-mod-nordsjaelland |accessdate=29 October 2020 |work=DR |date=17 July 2020 |language=Danish |quote=Stik mod spil og chancer lykkedes det den indskiftede Tochi Chukwuani at udligne med 20 minutter igen.}}</ref> With the goal, he became the club's youngest scorer in league history, a record that was broken the following season by teammate [[Andreas Schjelderup]] at 16 years and 284 days.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fcn.dk/2021/03/andreas-schjelderup-er-yngste-fcn-maalscorer-i-superligaen-nogensinde/|title=ANDREAS SCHJELDERUP ER YNGSTE FCN-MÅLSCORER I SUPERLIGAEN NOGENSINDE|website=FCN|date=12 March 2021|accessdate=21 March 2021|language=Danish}}</ref> He finished the season with 9 total appearances his which he scored one goal.<ref name="SW">{{cite web |title=T. Chukwuani - Soccerway |url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/tochi-phil-chukwuani/602880/ |website=int.soccerway.com |publisher=Perform Group |accessdate=29 October 2020}}</ref>

On 5 April 2022, it was reported that Chukwuani had signed with Italian [[Serie A]] club [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]]. Among others, the well-known transfer journalist [[Fabrizio Romano]] posted a picture of Chukwuani back in April, wearing a Verona jersey.<ref>[https://www.tipsbladet.dk/nyhed/superliga/se-billedet-superliga-spiller-rykker-til-serie Se billedet: Superliga-spiller rykker til Serie A], tipsbladet.dk, 5 April 2022</ref> However, according to an Italian newspaper on 14 July 2022, Chukwuani failed the medical check in Verona because the medical staff had found a minor heart defect and as there were strict rules in Italy regarding heart problems, the transfer was no longer possible.<ref>[https://www.bt.dk/fodbold/medie-tochi-chukwuani-glipper-serie-a-skifte-grundet-hjerteproblemer Medie: Tochi Chukwuani glipper Serie A-skifte grundet hjerteproblemer], bt.dk, 16 July 2022</ref>

===Lyngby===
After training with [[Lyngby Boldklub]] for several weeks, the club confirmed on 31 August 2022, that Chukwuani had signed a two-year deal with the newly promoted [[Danish Superliga]] team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Talentfulde Tochi skifter til De Kongeblå |trans-title=Talented Tochi moves to the Royal Blues |url=https://lyngby-boldklub.dk/2022/08/31/talentfulde-tochi-skifter-til-de-kongeblaa/ |website=Lyngby Boldklub |access-date=30 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220831155909/https://lyngby-boldklub.dk/2022/08/31/talentfulde-tochi-skifter-til-de-kongeblaa/ |archive-date=31 August 2022 |language=da-DK |date=31 August 2022}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 4 September, starting in a 2–0 home loss to [[Randers FC|Randers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lyngby vs. Randers 0–2: Summary |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/09/04/denmark/superliga/lyngby-boldklub/randers-fc/3795505/ |website=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group |access-date=30 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231130205059/https://us.soccerway.com/matches/2022/09/04/denmark/superliga/lyngby-boldklub/randers-fc/3795505/ |archive-date=30 November 2023}}</ref> On 7 May 2023, he scored his first goal for ''De Kongeblå'', opening the score in the second minute of a 2–1 league victory against [[FC Midtjylland|Midtjylland]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bitsch |first1=Ole |title=FCM smeltede i forårssolen: Tabte til bundholdet |url=https://www.herningfolkeblad.dk/artikel/8de5902b-8225-4a28-8846-f10b461fbf94/ |website=Herning Folkeblad |access-date=30 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230507122922/https://www.herningfolkeblad.dk/artikel/8de5902b-8225-4a28-8846-f10b461fbf94/ |archive-date=7 May 2023 |language=da |date=7 May 2023}}</ref>

===Sturm Graz===
On 20 March 2024, it was announced that Chukwuani would be joining [[Austria]]n club [[SK Sturm Graz|Sturm Graz]] from the summer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/lyngby-saelger-tochi-til-danskerklub|title=Lyngby sælger Tochi til danskerklub|trans-title=Lyngby sells Tochi to "Danish club"|language=da|website=bold.dk|date=20 March 2024|access-date=29 May 2024}}</ref>

===Rangers===

On 11 January 2026, Chukwuani was announced by [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on an initial three-and-a-half-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/rangers-announce-signing-of-tochi-chukwuani/6AJZNGPM3gzyusTAMWEkV1|title=Rangers Announce Signing of Tochi Chukwuani|language=en|website=Rangers.co.uk|date=11 January 2026|access-date=11 January 2026}}</ref>

'''Kieran Wright''' (born 1 April 1999) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. Wright has also played for Scotland at [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland national under-21 team]] levels.

==Club career==
Wright started his career at [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], he signed a professional contract with the club in March 2016, lasting until 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 March 2016 |title=Rangers move to secure seven young prospects on new deals including Liam Burt |work=Daily Record |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/rangers-move-secure-seven-young-7489277 |access-date=17 October 2020 |archive-date=22 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201122190152/https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/rangers-move-secure-seven-young-7489277 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In August 2016, he joined [[Gala Fairydean Rovers F.C.|Gala Fairydean Rovers]] on loan until the end of the year.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Knox |first=David |date=22 August 2016 |title=Dean delight as Rangers keeper arrives at Netherdale |work=Border Telegraph |url=https://www.bordertelegraph.com/sport/14696516.dean-delight-as-rangers-keeper-arrives-at-netherdale/ |access-date=17 October 2020 |archive-date=22 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201122190143/https://www.bordertelegraph.com/sport/14696516.dean-delight-as-rangers-keeper-arrives-at-netherdale/ |url-status=live }}</ref> His loan was later extended until the end of the season,<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=819276690723663872 |user=RangersFC |title=@RFC_Youth players Sam Jamieson and Kieran Wright have also extended their development loans at Stirling University and Gala Fairydean. |author=[[Rangers F.C.]] |date=11 January 2017 |access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref> with him winning the club's Player's Player of the Year and Young Player of the Year awards for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=5 June 2017 |title=Star-studded evening celebrates the greats of Gala |work=Border Telegraph |url=https://www.bordertelegraph.com/sport/15328257.star-studded-evening-celebrates-the-greats-of-gala/ |access-date=17 October 2020 |archive-date=22 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201122190132/https://www.bordertelegraph.com/sport/15328257.star-studded-evening-celebrates-the-greats-of-gala/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

He joined [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]] on loan until the end of the month on 4 January 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 January 2018 |title=Kieran Wright joins from Rangers |url=https://albionroversfc.com/kieran-wright-joins-from-rangers/ |access-date=17 October 2020 |website=albionroversfc.com |publisher=Albion Rovers F.C. |archive-date=22 November 2020 3–1 defeat to [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mackenzie |first=Alasdair |date=30 January 2018 |title=Rangers loan watch: Hardie strikes on Livingston debut as Wright makes senior }}</ref> He played four times for Alloa in the Scottish Championship during the [[2019–20 Alloa Athletic F.C. season|2019–20 season]].<ref name="soccerway" />

On 27 August 2020, he joined Scottish League One side [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 August 2020 |title=Loan News: Breen & Wright join on season-long loans |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/loan-news-breen-wright-join-on-season-long-loans/ |access-date=17 October 2020 |website=ptfc.co.uk |publisher=Partick Thistle F.C. |archive-date=22 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201122190142/https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/loan-news-breen-wright-join-on-season-long-loans/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He made 15 appearances on loan at the club.<ref name="soccerway" /> After a one game emergency loan spell at [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] in November 2021, Wright joined fellow [[Scottish League One]] side [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on loan until the end of the season in January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dumbarton Football Club - KIERAN WRIGHT JOINS ON LOAN FROM RANGERS|url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=5204|access-date=2022-01-13|website=www.dumbartonfootballclub.com}}</ref> On 29 May 2023, Wright signed a contract extension with Rangers until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{ Cite news | url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/kieran-wright-signs-new-rangers-contract-1/2FLuTpHG6AYhmW74VWjHix| work=Rangers.co.uk | publisher=Rangers Football Club| date=29 May 2023| title=KIERAN WRIGHT SIGNS NEW RANGERS CONTRACT}}</ref>

Wright joined [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on an emergency loan on 3 May 2024.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c72pen8214yo|title=Livi sign Rangers keeper Wright on emergency loan | work=BBC Sport | publisher=BBC | date=3 May 2024}}</ref> He made his first and only appearance for Livingston on 19 May 2024, in the [[Scottish Premiership]], coming on as a substitute for [[Shamal George]], in a 1-1 draw at home against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{ Cite news | url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/701962/hibernian-livingston| publisher=ESPN| date=29 May 2023| title=Livingston 1-1 Hibernian}}</ref>

On 5 July 2024, Wright joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Keeper Kieran joins on loan |url=https://www.airdriefc.com/2425-news/240705/keeper-kieran-joins-on-loan |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=airdrie |language=en}}</ref> On 3 July 2025, Wright signed a further extension to his Rangers contract by agreeing a deal until the summer of 2026 and assuming the role of third choice goalkeeper.<ref>{{ Cite news | url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/kieran-wright-signs-contract-extension/5n5O5dRZbpus95ttXPQWvM| work=Rangers.co.uk | publisher=Rangers Football Club| date=3 July 2025| title=Kieran Wright Signs Contract Extension}}</ref> On 30 April 2026, Wright joined [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on a seven-day emergency loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c4g454xe537o|title=Killie sign Rangers keeper Wright on emergency loan|publisher=BBC|date=30 April 2026|accessdate=17 August 2026}}</ref> The loan was later extended.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/st-mirren-a-team-news/|title=St Mirren (A) team news|publisher=[[Kilmarnock F.C.]]|date=9 May 2026|accessdate=17 August 2026}}</ref>

After leaving Rangers at the end of his contract, he featured as a trialist for [[Scottish League One]] side [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] during their [[Scottish League Cup]] match on 11 July 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/26274239.former-rangers-goalkeeper-trial-queen-south/|title=Former Rangers goalkeeper on trial at Queen of the South|website=thenational.scot|date=13 July 2026|accessdate=17 August 2026}}</ref> The following month, he again appeared as a trialist, this time playing for [[East Kilbride F.C.|East Kilbride]] in their [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cmx25lk35068|title=East Kilbride vs Kilmarnock II|publisher=BBC|date=11 August 2026|accessdate=17 August 2026}}</ref>

On 14 August 2026, he joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.| Heart of Midlothian]] on a short term deal until January 2027.<ref name="ClarkINJ">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cx253lwez27o|title=Goalkeeper Wright joins Hearts on short-term deal|work=bbc.co.uk|publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=14 August 2026 |accessdate=14 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/26467065.hearts-sign-released-rangers-player-short-term-deal/|title=Hearts sign released Rangers player on short-term deal|work=.heraldscotland.com|publisher=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]|date=14 August 2026 |accessdate=14 August 2026}}</ref>

==International career==

'''Emmanuel Oluwasegun Opeyemi Fernandez''' (born 17 July 2001) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. Born in England, he plays for the [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria national team]] at international level.

==Club career==
===Early career===
Fernandez began his career with [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] and [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.peterboroughtoday.co.uk/sport/football/peterborough-united/new-peterborough-united-signings-contract-is-a-reward-for-persistence-over-heartbreak-3305107|title=New Peterborough United signing's contract is a reward for persistence over heartbreak|website=www.peterboroughtoday.co.uk |date=12 July 2021 }}</ref> and whilst at Gillingham spent time on loan at [[Sheppey United F.C.|Sheppey United]] and [[Margate F.C.|Margate]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gillinghamfootballclub.com/news/2019/february/scholars-loan-deals/|date=4 February 2019|title=Scholars agree work experience deals|publisher=Gillingham F.C.}}</ref><ref name = "SUFC">{{Cite web|url=https://fulltime.thefa.com/statsForPlayer.html?selectedOrgStatRecordingTypeID_ForSort=&teamID=&selectedStatisticDisplayMode=3&personID=383483807&selectedSeasonID=32285694|title=Emmanuel Oluwasegun Opeyemi Fernandez player stats | Southern Counties East Football League|website=fulltime.thefa.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.margate-fc.co.uk/news/19-sep-2019/Two-Additions-To-Margate-Squad|title=PLAYER NEWS | Two Additions To Margate Squad|publisher=Margate F.C.}}</ref> After being released by Gillingham he played for [[Ramsgate F.C.|Ramsgate]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.kentonline.co.uk/medway/sport/posh-swoop-for-former-gills-youngster-250449/|title=Posh swoop for former Gills youngster|date=10 July 2021|website=Kent Online}}</ref>

===Peterborough United===
Fernandez signed a two-year contract with [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] in July 2021.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theposh.com/news/2021/july/fernandez-agrees-two-year-deal/|title=Fernandez Agrees Two-Year Deal|website=www.theposh.com}}</ref> He made his debut on 2 April 2022 in a "surprise" selection in a 4–0 home defeat against Middlesbrough.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.peterboroughtoday.co.uk/sport/football/peterborough-united/report-peterborough-united-0-middlesbrough-4-the-end-is-nigh-for-posh-after-a-spanking-from-boro-3638235|title=REPORT: PETERBOROUGH UNITED 0, MIDDLESBROUGH 4: The end is nigh for Posh after a spanking from Boro|website=www.peterboroughtoday.co.uk |date=2 April 2022 }}</ref> In November 2021, Fernandez joined [[Spalding United F.C.|Spalding United]] on loan,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://the72.co.uk/2021/11/13/peterborough-united-summer-signings-ethan-bojang-emmanuel-fernandez-join-club-legend-at-spalding-united/|website=The72|title=Peterborough United summer signings Ethan Bojang, Emmanuel Fernandez join club legend at Spalding United|first=James|last=Ray|date=13 November 2021}}</ref> making one appearance.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.peterboroughtoday.co.uk/sport/football/peterborough-united/peterborough-united-teenagers-join-gaby-zakuanis-spalding-on-loan-3456782|title=Peterborough United teenagers join Gaby Zakuani's Spalding on loan|date=13 November 2021|website=Peterborough Telegraph}}</ref> In March 2023, he joined [[Barnet F.C.|Barnet]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://barnetfc.com/fernandez-is-a-bee|title=Fernandez is a Bee!|publisher=Barnet F.C.}}</ref>

===Rangers===
In July 2025, Fernandez joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c3enz4l8qepo|title=Rangers sign Bournemouth's Joe Rothwell and Peterborough United's Emmanuel Fernandez|date=2 July 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 22 November 2025, Fernandez scored his first league goal for Rangers in a 2–1 win over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cy7erk3kl6vt|title=Ragged Rangers edge out Livingston for controversial win|date=22 November 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In February 2026, Fernandez suffered [[Racism in association football|racist abuse online following a match]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/ce823456kmmo|title=Rangers: Police Scotland investigates online abuse of Fernandez & Gassama|date=23 February 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In October 2026 he was defended by Rangers manager [[Derek McInnes]] following criticism aimed at Fernandez.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c6e3x50p3v1eo|title=Rangers manager Derek McInnes defends Emmanuel Fernandez|date=29 October 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==International career==
In March 2026, Fernandez received his first call-up to the [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria national team]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c9v0wv7yywdo|title=Rangers defender Emmanuel Fernandez receives first Nigeria call-up|date=18 March 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made his international debut on 27 March, coming off the bench in a 2–1 victory against [[Iran national football team|Iran]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c5yw2ekznp0o|title=Rangers: Fernandez makes Nigeria debut in win over Iran|date=27 March 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Four days later, he scored his first international goal in a 2–2 friendly draw with [[Jordan national football team|Jordan]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Meikle |first=Blair |url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/25985882.rangers-star-scores-classy-goal-second-international-cap/ |title=Rangers star scores classy goal on second international cap |publisher=The National Scot |date=31 March 2026 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Fernandez was born in London, and is eligible to represent Nigeria.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenigerianvoice.com/sports/353292/rangers-sign-nigerian-eligible-defender-emmanuel-fernandez-o.html|title=Transfer: Rangers sign Nigerian eligible defender Fernandez|date=3 July 2025|website=The Nigerian Voice}}</ref> He wears number 37 to honour his brother who died at 37 years old.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y2_nbmByfv4|title='To honour my brother I wear the number 37 on my back' Getting To Know Emmanuel Fernandez|date=4 July 2025|website=YouTube}}</ref> He is the youngest of 8 children.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/emmanuel-fernandez-rangers-ready-thanks-35551450|title=Emmanuel Fernandez is Rangers ready thanks to relentless family|first=Andrew|last=Newport|date=14 July 2025|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

He became an important player for the club the following season, leading them to the promotion playoffs before coming short with a loss to [[Entebbe UPPC|Gaddafi]]. In September 2021 it was announced that the player had signed a four-year contract with 13-time [[Uganda Premier League]] champions [[Kampala Capital City Authority FC|KCCA]] for an undisclosed fee.{{cite web |title=KCCA FC completes the signing of Proline FC forward Rogers Mato for an undisclosed fee. | date=4 September 2021 |url=http://nilepost.co.ug/2021/09/04/kcca-fc-completes-the-signing-of-proline-fc-forward-rogers-mato-for-an-undisclosed-fee/#:~:text=By%20Shafik%20Kiyaga-,Rogers%20Mato%2C%20a%20product%20of%20the%20FUFA%20Juniors%20League%20has,club%20with%20a%20big%20vision. |publisher=The Nile Post |access-date=19 January 2022}} After a year with [[Şanlıurfaspor]] of the [[TFF First League|Turkish First League]], Mato moved to [[FC AP Brera Strumica|AP Brera]] of [[North Macedonia]]'s [[Macedonian First Football League|First Football League]] in February 2024. He made his competitive debut for the club on 18 February in a league fixture against [[FK Sileks|Sileks]].{{cite web |last1=Damba |first1=Allan |title=Rogers Mato makes winning debut at his new European outfit |url=https://www.pulsesports.ug/football/story/rogers-mato-makes-winning-debut-at-his-new-european-outfit-2024021910314820357 |publisher=Pulse Sports |access-date=6 September 2024}} On 13 January 2026, he signed a pre-contract with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], initially joining on loan for the remainder of the [[2025–26 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2025–26 season]] before permanently joining on a three-year deal.{{Cite web |title=Rogers Mato agrees to join Hearts in summer |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/rogers-mato-agrees-to-join-hearts-in-summer |access-date=13 January 2026 |website=www.heartsfc.co.uk |language=en}} ==International career== In September 2021 Mato was called up to the senior national team for its [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – CAF second round#Group E|2022 FIFA World Cup qualification]] match against [[Rwanda national football team|Rwanda]].{{cite web |last1=Sang |first1=Kiplagat |title=2022 World Cup Qualifiers: Sredojevic trims Uganda squad ahead of Rwanda duel |url=https://www.goal.com/en-au/news/2022-world-cup-qualifiers-sredojevic-trims-uganda-squad-ahead-of-/1raca5233x28d16pcprqnm6h4b/match/6i657ey6a9g5lkeegel1vnms4 |publisher=Goal |access-date=19 January 2022}} Two months later he featured for the national side in a practice match against a representative team from the [[Northern Region, Uganda|Northern Region]]. Mato opened the scoring as the national side went on to win 3–1.{{cite web |title=Cranes put up impressive friendly performance ahead of clash WC clash with Kenya |url=https://the-cleansheet.com/2021/11/05/cranes-put-up-impressive-friendly-performance-ahead-of-clash-wc-clash-with-kenya/?fbclid=IwAR3XjY-ermG5LgZ9Ofq5Ty90a39INPb-KPZIgQxqUA-PgOlhAIrDdvnGOj0 |publisher=the-cleansheet.com |access-date=19 January 2022}} In January 2022 he was called up again for five friendlies with national sides from [[Europe]] and [[Asia]] as the Cranes traveled to [[Turkey]], [[Iraq]], and [[Bahrain]].{{cite web |last1=Abdusalam |first1=Kigozi |title=Micho Summons 45-man squad for Friendlies in Europe, Asia |date=3 January 2022 |url=https://chimpreports.com/uganda-cranes-micho-summons-45-man-squad-for-friendlies-in-europe-asia/ |publisher=chimpreports.com |access-date=18 January 2022}} He went on to make his senior debut in the first match against Iceland on 12 January 2022. '''Ross McCausland''' (born 12 May 2003) is a Northern Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Rangers}} club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland national team]].<ref name="soccerway"/>

==Club career==
===Rangers===
McCausland joined the [[Rangers F.C. B Team and Academy|Rangers Academy]] from Northern Irish side [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]] in the summer of 2019 for £60,000.<ref name="Four Players Join Academy">{{cite news | url=https://rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/four-players-join-academy/ | title=Four Players Join Academy | publisher=Rangers Football Club | work=Rangers.co.uk | date=31 August 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/ross-mccausland-set-rangers-contract-28049344  | title=Ross McCausland set for Rangers contract talks in bid to fend off transfer interest  | publisher=Football Scotland  |date =5 November 2023 | accessdate=9 November 2023}}</ref> In 2021, he signed a contract extension with the club running until 2024.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/ross-mccausland-signs-contract-extension/RecFmlZXqdq0ynVx60ALw| work=Rangers.co.uk | publisher=Rangers Football Club| date=27 September 2021| title=ROSS MCCAUSLAND SIGNS CONTRACT EXTENSION }}</ref>

Having been selected regularly for the club's B-team in the 2021–22 season (featuring in the [[UEFA Youth League]] as well as the [[Lowland Football League|Lowland League]] and [[Scottish Challenge Cup|Challenge Cup]]),<ref name="soccerway"/> McCausland made his first team debut for Rangers on 14 May 2022, replacing [[Amad (footballer)|Amad]] as a 61st-minute substitute during a 3–1 win over [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]; he set up fellow debutant [[Cole McKinnon]] for his first goal.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61360062 | title=Heart of Midlothian 1-3 Rangers | work=BBC Sport | publisher=BBC | date=14 May 2022 | access-date=14 May 2022 }}</ref> He continued to be a B-team player during the 2022–23 season<ref name="soccerway"/> and made only one senior appearance, being used as a late substitute by manager [[Michael Beale (football coach)|Michael Beale]] in a league match away to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 21 May 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65586920 | title=Hibernian 1-3 Rangers | work=BBC Sport | date=21 May 2023 }}</ref>

After the sacking of Beale during the 2023–24 season, McCausland started to get a run of games under interim manager [[Steven Davis]] and then the new permanent manager [[Philippe Clement]]. On 5 October 2023, he made his first appearance against Cypriot side [[Aris Limassol FC|Aris Limassol]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]], coming on as an 84th minute substitute for [[Scott Wright (footballer)|Scott Wright]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66929464 | title=Aris Limassol 2-1 Rangers | work=BBC Sport | date=5 October 2023 }}</ref>

McCausland impressed supporters with his performance off the bench against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] in October 2023; he was denied a first Rangers goal in a victory over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in a [[Scottish Premiership]] fixture, with the strike ruled out for a foul by [[Abdallah Sima]] in the build-up.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67324985 | title=Livingston 0-2 Rangers | work=BBC Sport | first=George  | last=O'Neill | date=12 November 2023 }}</ref>

McCausland signed a new four-year contract with Rangers on 28 November 2023 and was promoted to the first-team squad permanently.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/ross-mccausland-signs-new-rangers-contract/7hWvAOaKT0cCAlv9gbYzy7|title=Ross McCausland signs new Rangers contract|work=Rangers FC|publisher=rangers.co.uk|date=28 November 2023}}</ref> Two days later he celebrated with a first goal for the club against Aris Limassol, after coming in as a first half substitute for [[Todd Cantwell]].<ref name="Aris">{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67515252 | title=Rangers 1-1 Aris Limassol | work=BBC Sport | first=Andy | last=Campbell| date=30 November 2023 }}</ref> On 17 December, McCausland started in the [[Scottish League Cup]] final against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], and won his first trophy when Rangers captain [[James Tavernier]] scored the only goal of the match.<ref name="SCL2324">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67684521|title=Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen|website=BBC|date=17 December 2023|accessdate=17 December 2023}}</ref>

McCausland scored his first Premiership goal against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on 2 January 2024, but a run of starting appearances ended when he was injured by a tackle from [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] defender [[Dan Casey (footballer)|Dan Casey]] on 2 March, causing him to miss several fixtures; when he returned to fitness he was again among the substitutes. He was nominated for the [[PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year]] award,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/pfa-scotland-wonderkids-can-be-2034-world-cup-stars-as-young-player-award-marks-10-years-since-andy-robertson-4616451 |title=PFA Scotland wonderkids can be 2034 World Cup stars as young player award marks 10 years since Andy Robertson |publisher=The Scotsman|author =Alan Pattullo|date=4 May 2024 |access-date=12 May 2024}}</ref> but lost out to [[David Watson (footballer, born 2005)|David Watson]] of Kilmarnock.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c1vw9w7rpn0o |title=Lawrence Shankland, David Watson & Rangers trio win PFA awards |website=BBC Sport |date=5 May 2024 |access-date=12 May 2024}}</ref>

McCausland scored his first goal of the season 2024-25 against St Johnstone in the Scottish League Cup, with the assist coming from teammate [[Cyriel Dessers]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Rangers vs St Johnstone |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cgjv57g9nndt |access-date= |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Aris Limassol===
On 1 August 2025, McCausland joined [[Aris Limassol FC|Aris Limassol]] on a season long loan which included a conditional obligation to buy at the end of the loan deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ross McCausland Joins Aris Limassol On Loan |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/ross-mccausland-joins-aris-limassol-on-loan/UtISc8OKyA0JzTpcAJmGc |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=www.rangers.co.uk}}</ref>

==International career==
McCausland played regularly for Northern Ireland as a youth internationalist. On 14 November 2023, he received his first call-up to the [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland senior team]] for a round of [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying]] matches.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/international/ross-mccausland-receives-first-northern-ireland-call-up-for-euro-double-header/a1622153782.html | title=Ross McCausland receives first Northern Ireland call-up for Euro double-header | work=Belfast Telegraph | date=14 November 2023 }}</ref> Three days later he made his debut against [[Finland national football team|Finland]], starting in a 4–0 defeat.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67376194 | title=Finland 4-0 Northern Ireland | work=BBC Sport | date=17 November 2023 }}</ref>

'''Oisin Michael McEntee''' (born 5 January 2001) is an Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].

==Early and personal life==
Born in [[New York City]],<ref name = "SW"/> McEntee grew up in [[County Cavan]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/2026/04/03/oisin-mcentee-and-the-hearts-surge-shaking-scottish-football/|title=Oisín McEntee and the Hearts surge shaking Scottish football|website=The Irish Times}}</ref> and attended Patrician High School in [[Carrickmacross]] in neighbouring [[County Monaghan]].<ref name="auto1"/> His father Mickey was a [[Gaelic football|Gaelic footballer]] who played for [[Cavan GAA]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/hearts-and-soul-with-injury-woes-behind-him-cavans-oisin-mcentee-has-old-firm-in-his-sights-now/a2019140718.html|title=Hearts and soul: With injury woes behind him, Cavan’s Oisín McEntee has Old Firm in his sights now|date=26 September 2025|website=Irish Independent}}</ref> and McEntee played at youth level for [[Shercock]] GAA before concentrating on association football.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/oisin-mcentee-interview-4712640-Jul2019/|title=The son of an ex-inter-county GAA player aiming to realise a Premier League dream|first=Paul|last=Fennessy|website=The42|date=6 July 2019 }}</ref>

==Club career==
McEntee spent his early career with Cootehill, Carrick Rovers, [[Belvedere F.C.|Belvedere]] and [[Malahide United F.C.|Malahide United]].<ref name="auto1"/> McEntee joined [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] at the age of 16, captaining their under-18 team.<ref name="auto1"/> He spent time on loan at [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] before signing for [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]] in May 2022.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61608865|title=Walsall sign Newcastle centre-back McEntee|work=BBC Sport }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/oisin-mcentee-newcastle-5775852-May2022/|title=McEntee falls on his feet at Walsall after he's released by Newcastle|first=The42|last=Team|website=The42|date=27 May 2022 }}</ref> He underwent shoulder surgery in June 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.expressandstar.com/sport/football/walsall-fc/2022/06/24/walsalls-oisin-mcentee-undergoes-shoulder-surgery/|title=Walsall's Oisin McEntee undergoes shoulder surgery|first=Joe|last=Edwards|website=www.expressandstar.com|date=24 June 2022 }}</ref>

On 21 November 2023, Walsall announced McEntee had extended his contract to 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Walsall midfielder McEntee signs new contract |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67486350 |access-date=23 November 2023}}</ref>

McEntee left Walsall at the end of his contract on 30 June 2025, and signed for Scottish club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on 1 July 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Walsall midfielder McEntee joins Hearts |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cy4eg1dd2jzo |access-date=31 May 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
McEntee was an Irish youth international.<ref name = "SW"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/20011539.morton-defender-oisin-mcentee-aims-euro-qualification-ireland-u21s/|title=Morton defender aims for Euro qualification with Ireland U21s|website=Greenock Telegraph|date=24 March 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://punditarena.com/football/andrew-dempsey/oisin-mcentee-no-brainer-first-team-football-ireland-u21-walsall/|title=Exclusive: Oisin McEntee on his Newcastle exit & Ireland underage journey|first=Andrew|last=Dempsey|date=1 August 2022}}</ref> He appeared at the [[2018 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]].<ref name="auto1"/> 

He made various appearances at underage level, including seven appearances for the [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|Republic of Ireland under-21s]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statistics: Under 21 [Powered by tplSoccerStats] |url=http://www.soccerscene.ie/ss_gen/player.php?id=713&level=ss21 |access-date=26 August 2025 |website=www.soccerscene.ie}}</ref>
