'''Harry Jordon Milne''' (born 29 October 1996) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left-back]] or [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. He has previously played for [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]], [[Culter F.C.|Culter]] and [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].

== Early life ==

Harry Jordon Milne was born on 29 October 1996<ref>{{Cite web |title=Harry Milne |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-team/harry-milne-23-24-2/ |access-date=13 December 2024 |website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>  in the town of [[Banchory]] in [[Aberdeenshire]], Scotland.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title=Birth registers |url=https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/record-results/191392730069a78f5d192f9 |website=Scotland's People |location=Edinburgh, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=9 March 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==

===Cove Rangers===
Milne began his career at [[Aberdeen]]-based [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]]. During eight years at the club he won three league titles: the [[Highland Football League|Highland League]], [[Scottish League Two]] and [[Scottish League One]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/cove-rangers/5109511/harry-milne-partick-thistle-cove-rangers/|title=Harry Milne back to where it all started as Cove Rangers favourite makes return with Partick Thistle|first=Jamie|last=Durent|date=3 December 2022|work=The Press and Journal}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
In April 2022, Milne signed a pre-contract agreement for a two-year deal with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/harry-milne-signs-a-pre-contract-agreement-with-the-club/|title=Harry Milne signs a pre-contract agreement with the Club|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/20091142.partick-thistle-seal-second-pre-contract-deal-harry-milne-signs/|title=Partick Thistle seal second pre-contract deal as Harry Milne signs up|date=April 25, 2022|website=Glasgow Times}}</ref> Milne made his Partick Thistle debut in a cup game against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], in which Thistle won on penalties.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62123408 | title=Kilmarnock v Partick Thistle | work=BBC Sport }}</ref> Milne scored his first and second goal for Partick Thistle in a 3–2 home defeat to [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63436297|title=Dundee comeback floors 10-man Partick Thistle|work=BBC Sport }}</ref>

In July 2023 Milne added an extra year to his deal with Thistle, signing a new one-year contract taking his deal to the end of the 2024–25 season.<ref>https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/harry-milne-signs-one-year-contract-extension/</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===
After two and a half years with Thistle, Milne joined Scottish Premiership club Heart of Midlothian in February 2025 for an undisclosed fee on an 18 month deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c75ze4nr141o|title=Full-back Milne joins Hearts from Partick Thistlework=bbc.co.uk|publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 February 2025|accessdate=3 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/milne-from-jags-to-jambos|title=Milne: From Jags to Jambos|work=heartsfc.co.uk |publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] |date=3 February 2025|accessdate=3 February 2025}}</ref>

Milne became first-choice left back for the [[2025-26 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2025-26 season]] after [[James Penrice]] departed the club, but began playing as a makeshift [[right midfielder]] in a 0-2 away win against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and a 3-0 home win against [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in September 2025, receiving praise for both performances.<ref>{{cite news |last=Herrall |first=Jack |date=27 September 2025 |title=Milne's rise from deputy left-back to Hearts' dynamic attacker |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/crrjx089e04o |work=BBC Sport Scotland |location=Glasgow, Scotland |publisher=BBC |access-date=29 September 2025}}</ref> He then signed a contract extension with Hearts in October 2025, adding an extra year to his deal until summer 2027.<ref>https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/harry-signs-new-contract</ref> 

After an impressive season with the club, Milne was named in the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Premiership 12|2025-26 PFA Scotland Team of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news |author=<!-- not stated --> |date=17 April 2026 |title=Motherwell & Hearts dominate PFA Scotland Team of the Year |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cd0rmz1vg3mo |work=BBC Sport Scotland |location=Glasgow, Scotland |publisher=BBC |access-date=19 April 2026}}</ref>

'''Amadou Ba-Sy'''  (born 8 June 2001) is a French professional [[Association football|football]]er who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. 

Born in [[Nice]], Ba-Sy began his career as a youth at local side [[OGC Nice]]. He has subsequently played for [[Gazélec Ajaccio]], [[USL Dunkerque|Dunkerque]], [[F.C. Vizela|Vizela]], [[Académica de Coimbra (football)|Académica de Coimbra]] and [[FC Rouen|Rouen]]. He is of Senegalese descent.

==Career==
A youth product of [[OGC Nice|Nice]] since 2011, Ba-Sy began his senior career with their reserves in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ogcnice.com/fr/fiche/966/amadou-ba-sy.html|title=La fiche de Amadou Ba-Sy|website=OGC Nice}}</ref> He moved to [[Gazélec Ajaccio]] for the 2021–22 season, and ended up scoring 10 goals in 24 games.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.corsematin.com/articles/national-3-le-gazelec-football-club-ajaccio-veut-confirmer-a-nice-120230|title=National 3. Le Gazélec Football Club Ajaccio veut confirmer à Nice|date=11 September 2021|website=CorseMatin.com}}</ref> On 30 June 2022, he transferred to [[USL Dunkerque|Dunkerque]] in the [[Championnat National]] signing his first professional contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.foot-national.com/national/dunkerque--un-buteur-de-n3-s-engage-off-784102|title=Dunkerque : un buteur de N3 s'engage (off)|date=30 June 2022|website=Foot National}}</ref> He helped the team come in second on his debut season and earn promotion to the [[Ligue 2]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usldunkerque.com/amadou-ba-sy-mon-but-est-de-mimposer-afin-de-devenir-un-titulaire-indiscutable/|title=Amadou Ba-Sy : "Mon but est de m'imposer afin de devenir un titulaire indiscutable !"|date=6 November 2022}}</ref>

In January 2024, Ba-Sy joined [[Primeira Liga]] club [[F.C. Vizela|Vizela]] on a two-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |date=18 January 2024 |title=Amadou Ba-Sy reforça o ataque |trans-title=Amadou Ba-Sy reinforces the attack |url=https://fcvizela.pt/2024/01/18/amadou-ba-sy-reforca-o-ataque/ |accessdate=18 January 2024 |publisher=F.C. Vizela |language=Portuguese}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Born in France, Ba-Sy is of Senegalese descent and has [[dual nationality]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unfp.org/joueur/amadou-ba-sy-23500/|title=Amadou BA SY -|website=www.unfp.org}}</ref>

'''Mitchel Frame''' (born 25 January 2006) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left-back]] for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

==Club career==
Frame is a youth product of [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], having joined at the age of 9.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.67hailhail.com/celtic-youth/celtic-announce-great-mitchel-frame-news-after-premier-league-interest/|title=Celtic announce great Mitchel Frame news after Premier League interest|first=Hamish|last=Carton|date=29 September 2023|website=67 Hail Hail}}</ref> On 1 July 2022, he signed his first developmental contract with the club and joined their B-team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2022/july/01/new-celtic-academy-intake-sign-on-with-the-hoops/|title=New Celtic Academy intake sign on with the Hoops|first= |last= |date=1 July 2022|website=Celtic FC}}</ref>

Frame earned an opportunity to join the senior team for the preseason of the summer of 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.67hailhail.com/celtic-youth/brendan-rodgers-gives-17-year-old-celtic-chance-after-interest-from-newcastle-and-spurs/ |title=Brendan Rodgers gives 17-year-old Celtic chance after interest from Newcastle and Spurs |first=John |last=McGinley |date=13 July 2023 |website=67 Hail Hail}}</ref> He impressed further as on 29 September 2023, he extended his contract with the club until 2026 and signed professionally.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/23822522.mitchel-frame-agrees-new-celtic-contract-2026/|title=Mitchel Frame 'agrees' new Celtic contract until 2026|date=29 September 2023|website=Glasgow Times}}</ref> 

He made his senior and professional debut with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] as a substitute in a 2–1 [[UEFA Champions League]] win over [[Feyenoord]] on 13 December 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/67682857|title=Champions League: Reaction as Celtic snatch late win over Feyenoord|work=BBC Sport |date=13 December 2023}}</ref> 

In August 2025, Frame joined [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on a four-year deal.<ref>{{cite web | title=Aberdeen agree deal to sign Celtic left-back on four-year contract | date=26 August 2025 | url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/6837201/aberdeenfc-celtic-left-back-transfer-deal/ }}</ref>

After months of hard work, Frame made his competitive debut for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on 18 January 2026, coming on as a substitute in a 1–0 [[Scottish Cup]] victory over [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] at [[Pittodrie Stadium|Pittodrie]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AFC Heritage Trust - Mitchel Frame |url=https://afcheritage.org/football/players/mitchel-frame |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=afcheritage.org}}</ref>

==International career==
Frame is a youth international for Scotland, having played for the [[Scotland national under-17 football team|Scotland U17]]s at the [[2022 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]]. 

He was also part of the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland U19]]s that played for [[2024 UEFA European Under-19 Championship qualification]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thecelticstar.com/who-is-mitchell-frame-and-why-he-deserves-an-opportunity/|title=Who is Mitchell Frame and why he deserves an opportunity|date=13 December 2023|website=thecelticstar.com}}</ref>

'''Tony Lauren Yogane''' (born 24 September 2005) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

Yogane is a product of the [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C. Academy|Sheffield Wednesday Academy]] and began his professional career with [[Brentford F.C. Reserves and Academy#Relaunch (2016–present)|Brentford B]] in 2022. After gaining his first senior experience away on [[Loan (sports)|loan]], he transferred to Aberdeen in 2026.

== Career ==

=== Sheffield Wednesday ===
A right-footed [[Winger (association football)|winger]], with a preference for playing on the left,<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 June 2025 |title=Dundee seal deal for Tony Yogane – who is Brentford winger with 'amazing one-v-one skills'? |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5280164/dundee-tony-yogane-brentford-winger-amazing/ |access-date=30 June 2025 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> Yogane began his career in the [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C. Academy|Sheffield Wednesday Academy]].<ref name="SignsBrentford">{{Cite web |title=Tony Yogane signs for Brentford B |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/tony-yogane-signs-for-brentford-b |access-date=10 August 2022 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> He progressed through the youth ranks and was offered a scholarship at the end of the [[2021–22 Sheffield Wednesday F.C. season|2021–22]] season,<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 August 2022 |title=Promising Sheffield Wednesday duo Yogane and Holland snapped up by Brentford |url=https://www.examinerlive.co.uk/sport/football/news/promising-sheffield-wednesday-youngsters-brentford-24724499 |access-date=10 August 2022 |website=YorkshireLive |language=en}}</ref> but he declined the offer and departed the club in August 2022.<ref name="SignsBrentford" />

=== Brentford ===

==== 2022–2024 ====
On 10 August 2022, Yogane signed a pre-contract to become a professional with the [[Brentford F.C. Reserves and Academy#Relaunch (2016–present)|B team]] at [[Premier League]] club [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]],<ref name="SignsBrentford" /> for an undisclosed compensation fee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 August 2023 |title=Sheffield Wednesday’s attacker negotiations still ongoing with Owls future in question |url=https://uk.style.yahoo.com/sheffield-wednesday-attacker-negotiations-still-105725460.html |access-date=8 August 2023 |website=uk.style.yahoo.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> He began his time with the club as a scholar and a three-year professional contract was triggered on 24 September 2022, his 17th birthday.<ref name="SignsBrentford" /> He made concurrent appearances for the [[Brentford F.C. Reserves and Academy#U18|U18]] team during the 2022–23 and 2023–24 seasons.<ref name="Soccerway">{{Soccerway|id=806785|access-date=21 April 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Brentford Under-18s exit FA Youth Cup |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-under-18s-exit-fa-youth-cup |access-date=9 December 2022 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Brentford Under-18s Merit League update |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/club-news-brentford-under-18s-merit-league-update |access-date=4 April 2023 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> Yogane made two first team friendly appearances during the [[2023–24 Brentford F.C. season|2023–24]] [[pre-season]] and ended a "breakthrough" B team season with 29 appearances.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Highlights, report and reaction: Boreham Wood 1 Brentford 1 |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/match-reports-boreham-wood-1-brentford-1-pre-season-friendly |access-date=5 August 2023 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Highlights, report and reaction: Brentford 0 Lille 0 |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/match-reports-brentford-lille-pre-season-friendly |access-date=5 August 2023 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref name="Debut">{{Cite web |title=Ji-soo Kim and Tony Yogane make Brentford debuts |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-ji-soo-kim-tony-yogane-brentford-v-leyton-orient-carabao-cup |access-date=19 September 2024 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref>

==== 2024–25 and loan to Exeter City ====
Yogane was included in the first team squad for its [[2024–25 Brentford F.C. season|2024–25]] pre-season [[training camp]] in [[Portugal]] and he made five pre and early-season [[Friendly match|friendly]] appearances.<ref name="2024Contract">{{Cite web |title=Yogane extends Brentford stay |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-tony-yogane-contract-extension |access-date=2 December 2024 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Brentford 0 QPR 0: Minutes for first-team players in Jersey Road friendly |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/first-team-brentford-0-queens-park-rangers-0-friendly |access-date=5 September 2024 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> Yogane won his maiden competitive first team call-up for an [[EFL Cup]] third round match versus [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]] on 17 September 2024 and he made his debut as a substitute late in the 3–1 victory.<ref name="Debut" /> On 2 December 2024, Yogane signed a new {{frac|2|1|2}}-year contract.<ref name="2024Contract" /> After featuring as an unused substitute in seven further senior matches and making 14 B team appearances so far during the 2024–25 season,<ref name="Soccerway" /> Yogane joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]] on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] for the remainder of the season on 23 January 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yogane completes Exeter loan move |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-tony-yogane-brentford-exeter-city-loan |access-date=23 January 2025 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> He made 19 appearances during his spell.<ref name="DundeeLoan">{{Cite web |title=Yogane joins Dundee on loan |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-tony-yogane-dundee-loan-scottish-premiership |access-date=30 June 2025 |website=www.brentfordfc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> After the League One season ended, Yogane resumed match play for Brentford B and scored the winner in the 3–2 [[2024–25 Professional U21 Development League#Professional Development League|Professional Development League]] Final victory over [[AFC Bournemouth Under-21s and Academy|Bournemouth]].<ref name="DundeeLoan" />

==== 2025–26 and loan to Dundee ====
On 30 June 2025, Yogane joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a season-long loan.<ref name="DundeeLoan" /> He made 42 appearances during a mid-table [[2025–26 Dundee F.C. season|2025–26]] season and scored his first professional goal,<ref name="Soccerbase2526" /><ref>{{Fchd|id=DUNDEE|name=Dundee F.C.}}</ref> in a 2–1 victory over [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 7 March 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 March 2026 |title=Dundee's Tony Yogane delighted to net first senior goal against Motherwell |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c80j953r0p9o |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> The loan saw Yogane undertake extra fitness work and adjust his diet.<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 January 2026 |title='Two packets of digestives a day' – Dundee wing wonder Tony Yogane reveals curbing sweet tooth is helping unlock potential |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5418745/two-packets-digestives-dundee-tony-yogane-unlock-potential/ |access-date=17 May 2026 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> Yogane transferred out of Brentford in June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tony Yogane joins Aberdeen in permanent deal |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/news/article/brentford-b-team-tony-yogane-aberdeen-transfer |access-date=19 June 2026 |website=Brentford FC |language=en-gb}}</ref>

=== Aberdeen ===
On 19 June 2026, Yogane transferred to Scottish Premiership club [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] and signed a four-year contract for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Highly Rated Youngster Yogane Commits to the Dons |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/en/news/highly-rated-youngster-yogane-commits-to-the-dons |access-date=19 June 2026 |website=Aberdeen FC |language=en}}</ref>

'''James Thomas Wilson''' (born 6 March 2007) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. Wilson has represented the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]],<ref>{{cite web |url= https://int.soccerway.com/players/james-wilson/894996/| website= Soccerway|accessdate=27 October 2024|title=James Wilson}}</ref> and represented [[Northern Ireland]] at [[Northern Ireland national under-17 football team|under-17]] level.

==Early life==
Wilson grew up in [[Linlithgow]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-24 |title=Linlithgow Kid Wilson Signs New Hearts Deal|url=https://www.pressreader.com/uk/west-lothian-courier/20250424/282089167626772|access-date=2025-08-01 |website=West Lothian Courier}}</ref> and attended [[Balerno Community High School|Balerno High School]] in Edinburgh.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/czrl3jx2nkdo|title='I'm getting stopped at school for selfies'|date=16 January 2025|accessdate=26 February 2025|work=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref> His twin brothers Alfie and Stanley also developed at the Hearts academy,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-produce-two-more-wilsons-the-twins-following-older-brother-james-with-club-and-country-5007107|title=Hearts produce two more Wilsons: The twins following older brother James with club and country|date=25 February 2025|access-date=26 February 2025
|work=Edinburgh Evening News}}</ref> and have appeared for the club's B-team in the [[Lowland League]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-16 |title=Hearts B suffer Tranent defeat: Wilson twins debut, new captain, deserving loss |url=https://www.heartsstandard.co.uk/news/25011967.wilson-twins-make-hearts-b-debut-loss-tranent/ |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=Hearts Standard}}</ref>

==Club career==
Wilson signed a first professional contract with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in the summer of 2023.<ref name="contract"/> He broke through into first team during the [[2023–24 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2023–24 season]], making three appearances as a substitute, whilst also playing for the Hearts B-team in the Lowland League.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/exclusive-hearts-forward-james-wilson-talks-fifa-feeling-bloated-and-gaining-weight-4711993|website=Edinburgh Evening News|access-date=27 October 2024|title= Exclusive: Hearts forward James Wilson talks FIFA, feeling bloated and gaining weight|first=Barry|last=Anderson|date=23 July 2024}}</ref> He made his professional debut as a 16-year-old in the [[Scottish Cup]] on 20 January 2024 in a 2–1 away win against [[The Spartans F.C.|The Spartans]].<ref name="contract"/><ref>{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Mcdonald|access-date=27 October 2024|date=9 July 2024|url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/james-wilson-targets-hearts-breakthrough-29503475|title= James Wilson targets Hearts breakthrough season after snubbing Manchester United interest|website=Football Scotland}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=20 January 2024|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2024/01/20/scotland/scottish-cup/spartans-edinburgh-fc/heart-of-midlothian-fc/4272975/|website=Soccerway|title= SPARTANS VS. HEARTS 1 - 2|accessdate=27 October 2024}}</ref> He then made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] in May 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c1d4vj2dmr1o|title=Naismith tips Wilson for bright future at Hearts|date=12 May 2024|access-date=27 October 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

He scored his first league goal for Hearts in October 2024 in a 4–0 win over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]];<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/24664534.hearts-4-st-mirren-0-neil-critchley-enjoys-dream-start/ |website=Herald Scotland|access-date=27 October 2024|title= Hearts 4 St Mirren 0: Neil Critchley enjoys dream start|date=19 October 2024}}</ref> the following week he made headlines with a late equaliser in the [[Edinburgh derby]] against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 27 October 2024, which finished 1–1.<ref>{{cite web|first=Barry|last=Anderson|url= https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-report-and-player-ratings-v-hibs-teenage-wonder-wilson-critchleys-run-quality-questions-at-er-4841522|website=Edinburgh Evening News|access-date=27 October 2024|title= Hearts report and player ratings v Hibs: Teenage wonder Wilson, Critchley's run, quality questions at ER|date=27 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|website=Sky Sports|access-date=27 October 2024|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/video/19508/13242655/james-wilson-scrambles-home-for-heart-with-equaliser-vs-hibs|title=He saves the derby for Hearts {{!}} James Wilson scrambles home dramatic late equaliser|date=27 October 2024}}</ref>

On 19 December 2024, in a [[UEFA Conference League]] game against [[FC Petrocub Hîncești|Petrocub Hîncești]], Wilson became the youngest goalscorer in the competition's four-year history, and the all-time youngest scorer for Hearts in any European fixture,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/james-wilsons-hearts-rise-hints-at-epl-talent-at-liverpool-and-man-utd-level-4920272|website=Edinburgh Evening News|title=James Wilson's Hearts rise hints at EPL talent at Liverpool and Man Utd level|date=23 December 2024|accessdate=27 December 2024}}</ref> at the age of 17 years and 288 days.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsstandard.co.uk/news/24808916.hearts-conference-league-history-made-hearts-star/ |website=Hearts Standard|accessdate=27 December 2024|title=The Hearts and Conference League history made by Hearts star|date=20 December 2024}}</ref> He subsequently signed a contract extension until the summer of 2026.<ref name="Contracts">{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/wilson-extends-contract|title=Wilson Extends Contract|work=heartsfc.co.uk|publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] |date=21 December 2024|accessdate=27 December 2024}}</ref> He was [[Red card (association football)|sent off]] for the first time on 6 April 2025, for a late sliding tackle on [[Luca Stephenson]] of [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c2kvdlvz095t#Report|title=Dundee United took a significant step towards a top-five Scottish Premiership finish and reignited their hopes of finishing third with victory over 10-man Hearts.|date=6 April 2025|accessdate=7 April 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/the-scottish-fa-rule-on-james-wilsons-hearts-red-card-and-the-games-he-will-miss-after-dundee-united-loss-5070019|website=[[Edinburgh Evening News]]|title=The Scottish FA rule on James Wilson's Hearts red card - and the games he will miss after Dundee United loss|date=7 April 2025|accessdate=7 April 2025}}</ref>

On 2 February 2026, Wilson joined English [[Premier League]] side [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] on a six-month loan deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/wilsons-spurs-loan|title=Wilson's Spurs Loan |work=heartsfc.co.uk|publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] |date=2 February 2026|accessdate=2 February 2026}}</ref> Initially joining up with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C. Under-21s and Academy|their under-21 side]], the deal included an option to buy at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2026/february/james-wilson-joins-from-hearts/|title=Wilson Joins From Hearts |work=tottenhamhotspur.com|publisher=[[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.]] |date=2 February 2026|accessdate=2 February 2026}}</ref>

Having returned from his loan spell at Tottenham Hotspur, Wilson scored his first goal in a year for Hearts in a 6–2 win over [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in August 2026.<ref>{{cite web|date=17 August 2026|title= Where does Wilson fit in at Hearts after starring role?|website=BBC Sport|accessdate=22 August 2026|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cx25515j2r4o}}</ref> Later in the week, he scored a long-range goal against [[Rapid Vienna]], helping Hearts to draw 2–2 with the Austrian club in the [[2026–27 UEFA Conference League]]; Hearts ultimately qualified for the competition.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stunning James Wilson strike helps Hearts secure draw with Rapid Vienna|date=20 August 2026|accessdate=22 August 2026|url= https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/sport/national/26483165.stunning-james-wilson-strike-helps-hearts-secure-draw-rapid-vienna/?callback=in&code=YTC5MJK4NTYTNJI4ZC0ZNGZKLTHJYZKTZTNINTC0NZYYY2YW&state=25f8636a0037435fa838de7ab352efab|website=Enfield Independent}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Campbell |first=Andy |date=26 August 2026 |title=Vrancken's side come of age as Hearts bid goodnight Vienna |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c7v468zj6r5o |work=BBC Sport |location=Vienna, Austria |publisher=BBC Sport Scotland |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Having come on as a substitute against the Faroe Islands for the [[Northern Ireland national under-17 football team|Northern Ireland under-17s]] in 2022<ref>[https://www.irishfa.com/news/2022/august/ni-u17s-defeated-at-nordic-cup NI U17s defeated at Nordic Cup], [[Irish Football Association]], 8 August 2022</ref> (being eligible at that stage, as well as for England and the Republic of Ireland, through his parents),<ref name="ireland">{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/james-wilson-reveals-northern-ireland-cap-call-his-scotland-future-and-hearts-european-aim-5065312|title=James Wilson reveals Northern Ireland cap call, his Scotland future and Hearts' European aim|first=Barry|last=Anderson|website=[[Edinburgh Evening News]]|date=3 April 2025}}</ref> Wilson went on to captain Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] and [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17 levels]].<ref name="contract">{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/exclusive-james-wilsons-hearts-debut-fires-ambition-after-rangers-celtic-manchester-united-and-leeds-interest-4442238|website=Edinburgh Evening News|access-date=27 October 2024|title= Exclusive: James Wilson's Hearts debut fires ambition after Rangers, Celtic, Man Utd and Leeds interest|first=Barry|last=Anderson|date=22 January 2024}}</ref>

In March 2025 he received his first call up for the [[Scotland national football team|senior Scotland squad]] for the [[2024–25 UEFA Nations League|UEFA Nations League]] play-off against [[Greece national football team|Greece]];<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scotland squad named for Greece double-header |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-squad-named-for-greece-double-header/?rid=13925 |access-date=2025-03-11 |website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref> He made his full international debut in the second leg of the tie, becoming the youngest man to play for Scotland at the age of 18 years, 17 days (surpassing the record set by [[John Lambie (footballer, born 1868)|John Lambie]] which had stood for 138 years).<ref>{{cite web |title=Scotland 0-3 Greece (agg 1-3): Key stats |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c7780p8lp0do |date=24 March 2025 |accessdate=24 March 2025 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Wilson becomes youngest Scotland men's international|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cyvezv43qj6o |date=24 March 2025 |access-date=28 March 2025 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref name="ireland"/> Wilson was one of four young players invited to train with the Scotland squad ahead of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026 World Cup]] finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cgepznz1xe8o |title=Scotland call up James Wilson, Liam McFarlane, Luke Graham and Tyler Fletcher for pre-World Cup training |website=BBC Sport |date=20 May 2026 |accessdate=21 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Findlay Kenneth Curtis''' (born 9 June 2006)<!--Do not change without reason. In this source, a Rangers official states that the often cited birthdate of 1 October is not true. This is backed by friends and family who can confirm his birthday as the 9th of June. https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/rangers/latest-rangers-news/findlay-curtis-fake-news-confession-as-rangers-teenager-comes-of-age-literally-after-ibrox-heroics-5239438 --> is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

He joined Rangers at age 6 and made his professional debut in January 2025. Twelve months later he moved on loan to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], and helped the team avoid relegation. He made his senior international debut for Scotland in March 2026 and was chosen for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], where he became the country's youngest player in tournament history.

==Club career==
Curtis joined [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]' academy at age 6, having impressed at a football school run by the club.<ref name=academy/> In July 2022, he signed his first professional contract and was promoted to Rangers' under-18 team.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Jordan |title=Why Rangers are recruiting 'emerging talent' – after banking almost £10m |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3353107/2022/07/02/rangers-recruitment-emerging-talent-10m/ |access-date=23 January 2025 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=2 July 2022 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=25 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125194549/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3353107/2022/07/02/rangers-recruitment-emerging-talent-10m/ |url-status=live }}</ref> His deal was extended in January 2023 to last until June 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Irvine |first1=David |title=Five Rangers youngsters agree Ibrox contract extensions |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/23241223.five-rangers-youngsters-agree-ibrox-contract-extensions/ |access-date=23 January 2025 |work=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]] |date=10 January 2023}}</ref> On 1 May 2024 he scored a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]] to equalise as Rangers came from behind to win the [[Scottish Youth Cup]] against [[Aberdeen F.C. Reserves and Academy|Aberdeen]] at [[Hampden Park]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Idessane |first1=Kheredine |title=Rangers hit back against Aberdeen to win Youth Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c51n37x49rdo |access-date=23 January 2025 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=1 May 2024}}</ref> On 28 May 2024, Curtis signed a further extension until 2025.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://x.com/RFC_Youth/status/1795424785129947242|title=Rangers Academy can today announce Findlay Curtis has signed a contract extension until summer 2025.|work=Rangers FC|publisher=X.com|date=28 May 2024|archive-date=26 January 2025|access-date=26 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126223109/https://x.com/RFC_Youth/status/1795424785129947242|url-status=live}}</ref>

Curtis was part of the [[Rangers F.C. B Team and Academy|Rangers B Team]] in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]]. He scored twice in a 4–1 home win over [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] on 22 October 2024, in the fourth round of the cup.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kearney |first1=Ben |title=£10 million team too much for Stenhousemuir as Rangers B seal SPFL Trust Trophy quarter-final spot |url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/ps10-million-team-too-much-for-stenhousemuir-as-rangers-b-seal-spfl-trust-trophy-quarter-final-spot-4836911 |access-date=23 January 2025 |work=[[Falkirk Herald]] |date=23 October 2024 |archive-date=25 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125194622/https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/ps10-million-team-too-much-for-stenhousemuir-as-rangers-b-seal-spfl-trust-trophy-quarter-final-spot-4836911 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 19 January 2025, Curtis made his first-team debut in the fourth round of the [[Scottish Cup]], in a 5–0 win over [[Highland Football League]] club [[Fraserburgh F.C.|Fraserburgh]]. He came on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in the 62nd minute and assisted the last goal, completing [[Cyriel Dessers]]' hat-trick.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dessers hits hat-trick as Rangers beat Fraserburgh in David v Goliath tie |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/cyriel-dessers-hits-hat-trick-as-rangers-breeze-past-fraserburgh-in-david-v-goliath-scottish-cup-clash |access-date=23 January 2025 |agency=PA Sport |publisher=[[STV News]] |date=19 January 2025 |archive-date=19 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119164944/https://news.stv.tv/sport/cyriel-dessers-hits-hat-trick-as-rangers-breeze-past-fraserburgh-in-david-v-goliath-scottish-cup-clash |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Rangers 5–0 Fraserburgh |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3w8qwlv498t |access-date=23 January 2025 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=19 January 2025 |archive-date=20 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120105855/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3w8qwlv498t |url-status=live }}</ref> Four days later he made his European debut in the [[UEFA Europa League]] [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League league phase|league phase]], again from the bench for the final half-hour of a 2–1 loss away to [[Manchester United]]; according to Ewan Paton of ''[[The National (Scotland)|The National]]'', he gave a good performance in "difficult circumstances".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Paton |first1=Ewan |title=Rangers player ratings in Europa League loss vs Man Utd |url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/24881017.rangers-player-ratings-europa-league-loss-vs-man-utd/ |access-date=23 January 2025 |work=[[The National (Scotland)|The National]] |date=23 January 2025 |archive-date=24 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124085337/https://www.thenational.scot/sport/24881017.rangers-player-ratings-europa-league-loss-vs-man-utd/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 29 January 2025, Curtis signed a contract extension of undisclosed length.<ref>{{cite news |title='Proud day' as Curtis signs contract extension |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/ce3nx5kel55o |access-date=30 January 2025 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=29 January 2025}}</ref> Eighteen days later, he made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut in the last minute of a 3–1 win away to [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pattullo |first1=Alan |title=Philippe Clement spared Ibrox vitriol as Rangers agenda moves on with no need for Jose Mourinho's laundry basket |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/rangers/latest-rangers-news/philippe-clement-spared-ibrox-vitriol-as-rangers-agenda-moves-on-with-no-need-for-jose-mourinhos-laundry-basket-5002619 |access-date=23 February 2025 |work=The Scotsman |date=21 February 2025 |archive-date=23 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223052012/https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/rangers/latest-rangers-news/philippe-clement-spared-ibrox-vitriol-as-rangers-agenda-moves-on-with-no-need-for-jose-mourinhos-laundry-basket-5002619 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 22 July 2025, Curtis scored his first goal for Rangers in a [[UEFA Champions League]] qualifier against [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]].<ref name="Age"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Rangers 2-0 Panathinaikos|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cm2lgl1x1vpt|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 July 2025|archive-date=21 July 2025|access-date=22 July 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250721181742/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cm2lgl1x1vpt|url-status=live}}</ref> He started the game on the left side of the attack, in [[Russell Martin (footballer)|Russell Martin]]'s first game as manager.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McPheat |first1=Nick |title='Cool cat' Curtis ignites Martin's Rangers reign |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c0m8d11y24vo |access-date=27 July 2025 |publisher=BBC Sport |archive-date=22 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250722225744/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c0m8d11y24vo |url-status=live }}</ref> His first league goal came on 24 August as the equaliser in a 1–1 draw away to [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], as a substitute for [[Joe Rothwell]].<ref>{{cite news |title='I have to trust him': Martin queries Igamane injury claim after Rangers draw |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/aug/24/st-mirren-rangers-scottish-premiership-match-report |access-date=1 February 2026 |work=The Guardian |date=24 August 2025}}</ref>

On 30 January 2026, having achieved three goals and two assists in 21 Rangers appearances, Curtis joined fellow Scottish Premiership club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Killie sign striker Hugill & loan Rangers winger Curtis |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c3dm3k9kkxzo |access-date=1 February 2026 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=30 January 2026 |archive-date=17 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260517131008/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c3dm3k9kkxzo |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored five goals in 14 games, including four in the last five fixtures, as "Killie" avoided relegation in 10th place.<ref name=oneill/>

==International career==
Curtis made his first appearance for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] team on 5 September 2025, as a 77th-minute substitute for [[Daniel Kelly (footballer, born 2005)|Daniel Kelly]] in a 2–0 loss away to the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] in [[2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=248302&lid=5 |title=Findlay Curtis |website=Scottish FA |accessdate=16 March 2026 |archive-date=14 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260314082848/https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=248302&lid=5 |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Curtis was included in the full [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad for the first time in March 2026, for [[Exhibition game|friendly matches]] against [[Japan national football team|Japan]] and the [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cpd8w4xg991o |title=Scotland squad: Kilmarnock winger Findlay Curtis called up |website=BBC Sport |date=16 March 2026 |accessdate=16 March 2026 |archive-date=28 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260528155305/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cpd8w4xg991o |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his debut on 28 March against Japan at [[Hampden Park]], replacing [[Tommy Conway]] for the last nine minutes.<ref>{{cite news |last1=O'Neill |first1=George |title=What might Scotland change for Ivory Coast test? |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/ce84ml83x14o |access-date=29 March 2026 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=29 March 2026}}</ref> He was called up for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] in North America; manager [[Steve Clarke]] praised his decision to move on loan to Kilmarnock for regular playing time.<ref name=oneill>{{cite news |last1=O'Neill |first1=George |title= How Curtis timed run to perfection for World Cup place|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/ce8pn4jjjzko|access-date=19 May 2026 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=19 May 2026}}</ref> He scored his first Scotland goal on 30 May, equalising in a 4–1 friendly win against [[Curaçao national football team|Curaçao]] and winning a penalty that [[Ryan Christie]] scored.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Burke |first1=Andy |title=What we learned from Scotland's win over Curacao|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c2d2wxgnx4yo|access-date=14 June 2026 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=31 May 2026}}</ref> In Scotland's opening game of the tournament, a 1–0 win over [[Haiti national football team|Haiti]], he played the last seven minutes and took the record of teammate [[Ben Gannon-Doak]] as the team's youngest ever World Cup player.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Canavan |first1=Amy |title=The 20-year-old who stole the show on Scotland's World Cup return|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/clyrepwp0gno|access-date=14 June 2026 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=14 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Finlay Ian Pollock''' (born 27 June 2004) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], as a [[midfielder]]. Born in Edinburgh, he began his career as a youth with local side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], and represented the club with Hearts B in the Lowland league as well as the first team. 

He has also played for [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] and [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on loan and represented [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland]] at under 19 and under 21 level. 

==Club career==
Born in Edinburgh,<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title=Birth registers |url=https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/record-results/76800548669af44247c373 |website=Scotland's People |location=Edinburgh, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=9 March 2026}}</ref> Pollock grew up a fan of [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghlive.co.uk/sport/hearts-tie-down-finlay-pollock-25322013|title=Hearts tie down Finlay Pollock to long-term deal as Joe Savage lists key attributes
|work=edinburghlive.co.uk|publisher=Edinburgh Live |date=21 October 2022|accessdate=3 February 2025}}</ref> and attended [[Stewart's Melville College]];<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.erskinestewartmelville.com/news/smc-pupil-finlay-pollock-makes-heart-midlothian-fc-debut|title=SMC Pupil Finlay Pollock Makes Heart of Midlothian Debut|work=erskinestewartmelville.com|publisher=[[Stewart's Melville College]] |date=27 April 2021|accessdate=6 February 2025}}</ref> he simultaneously was part of the Hearts Academy<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/senior-hearts-players-to-look-after-teen-talent-3307408|title=Senior Hearts players to look after teenager Finlay Pollock as Andy Halliday takes lead role|work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com|publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=14 July 2021|accessdate=6 February 2025}}</ref> and latterly the B team in the [[Lowland League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsstandard.co.uk/news/24524592.interview-meet-exciting-player-hearts-right-now/|title=Meet the most exciting player at Hearts right now|work=heartsstandard.co.uk|publisher=Hearts Standard |date=28 August 2024|accessdate=7 February 2025}}</ref> He signed his first professional contract during the summer of 2021,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/top-teen-talent-signs-deal-with-hearts-3464414|title=Hearts sign promising teenager on professional deal |work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com|publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=19 November 2021|accessdate=7 February 2025}}</ref> having made his first team debut on 24 April 2021, against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/pages/finlay-pollock|title=Finlay Pollock Hearts Profile
|work=heartsfc.co.uk |publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] |accessdate=7 February 2025}}</ref> in a 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56782167|title=Hearts 3-0 Inverness CT: Highlanders' play-off hopes ended as champions win|work=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=24 April 2021|accessdate=7 February 2025}}</ref> With the season drawing to a close he made one more appearance,<ref>{{Soccerbase season|id=139074|season=2020|access-date=7 February 2025}}</ref> as Hearts won the [[Scottish Championship]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/56874215|title=Hearts lift the Scottish Championship trophy in a subdued fashion after beating Inverness|work=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=24 April 2021|accessdate=7 February 2025}}</ref>

The following season he scored his first goal for the club, scoring the winning goal against [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]]. In October 2022, Pollock signed a new three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/crg844j7320o|title=Hearts teenager Pollock signs three-year deal
|work=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=21 October 2022|accessdate=3 February 2025}}</ref> In all he made four appearances, before going on Loan to East Fife.<ref name="Fife">{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/pollock-leaves-hearts-on-loan-3590620|title=Hearts teen Finlay Pollock joins East Fife on loan|work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com|publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=28 February 2022|accessdate=3 February 2025}}</ref>

He made his next appearance for the first team in November 2022, as a substitute against [[Başakşehir]] in the [[UEFA Conference League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c9ep27mynygo|title='It's what you dream of as a Jambo'
|work=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=4 November  2022|accessdate=3 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c9ep27mynygo|title=Başakşehir İstanbul Başakşehir 3 Hearts 1|work=uefa.com |publisher=[[UEFA Conference League]] |date=3 November  2022|accessdate=7 February 2025}}</ref> Subsequently, a diagnosis of [[patellar tendonitis]]<ref name="Tendon">{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/finlay-pollocks-mysterious-hearts-absence-explained-after-a-year-out-of-the-tynecastle-first-team-4384482|title=Finlay Pollock's mysterious Hearts absence explained after a year out of the Tynecastle first team|work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com|publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=25 October 2023|accessdate=3 February 2025}}</ref> and ongoing rehabilitation led him to be absent from the first team for over a year.<ref name = "Tendon"/> His next appearance came in February 2024,<ref name = "Hibs"/> in a 1–1 draw in the [[Edinburgh Derby]] against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68355885|title=Lawrence Shankland penalty denies wasteful visitors rare Tynecastle win|work=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=28 February 2024|accessdate=3 February 2025}}</ref>

In September 2024, Pollock signed a new two-year contract,<ref name = "Raith"/> before going on loan to [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/5086200/neill-collins-raith-rovers-hearts-finlay-pollock/|title=Neill Collins 'delighted' as Raith Rovers snap up Hearts youngster Finlay Pollock on loan|work=thecourier.co.uk|publisher=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |date=19 September 2024|accessdate=3 February 2025}}</ref>

===East Fife===
On 28 February 2022, Pollock joined [[Scottish League One|League One]] side [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] for the remainder of the season.<ref name = "Fife"/> He made his debut on 12 March 2022, against [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]], in a 2–0 win. In all he made seven appearances for East Fife.<ref name = "Fifers"/>

===Raith Rovers===
On 9 September 2024, Pollock joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on a season long loan.<ref name="Raith">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c869w7legw2o|title=Pollock signs new deal & goes on loan to Raith
|work=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=19 September 2024|accessdate=6 February 2025}}</ref> He made his debut<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifetoday.co.uk/sport/football/raith-rovers-great-pedigree-hearts-kid-makes-goalscoring-start-at-starks-park-4792867 |title=Raith Rovers: 'Great pedigree' Hearts kid makes goalscoring start at Stark's Park|work=fifetoday.co.uk |publisher=[[Fife Today]] |date=23 September 2024|accessdate=6 February 2025}}</ref> on 21 September, against [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], scoring the second goal in a 3–3 draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c0m0zpwndgyt|title=Oli Shaw's overhead kick helped Hamilton Academical snatch a point against Raith Rovers in a six-goal thriller at Stark's Park.
|work=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=21 September 2024|accessdate=3 February 2025}}</ref>

'''Cláudio Rafael Soares Braga''' (born 28 October 1999) is a Portuguese professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].

==Career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Mafamude]] in [[Vila Nova de Gaia]], Braga played for several local clubs at youth level, later telling ''[[A Bola]]'' that he was not considered a significant prospect at any of them.<ref name=bola/>

Braga concluded his youth career at [[Rio Ave F.C.|Rio Ave]] and made his senior debut with its [[reserve team]] in the [[Porto Football Association]]'s district leagues in 2018. A year later, he signed for [[Valadares Gaia F.C.|Valadares Gaia]] of what was then the third-tier [[Campeonato de Portugal (league)|Campeonato de Portugal]]. He transferred mid-season in January 2020 to [[C.D. Fátima|Fátima]], where his good start was halted by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal|COVID-19 pandemic]]. He then moved on to [[S.C. Ideal|Sporting Ideal]] and [[AC Vila Meã|Vila Meã]], again in the same league.<ref name=bola/>

=== Norway ===
Ahead of the [[2022 Norwegian Second Division|2022 season]], Braga's agent convinced him to sign for [[Norwegian Second Division]] side [[Moss FK|Moss]]. He helped the club achieve promotion to the [[Norwegian First Division]], and was their top scorer and among the highest in the league in the [[2023 Norwegian First Division|2023 season]].<ref name=bola/>

Braga believed his performances in Norway's second tier would lead to a transfer to the top-flight [[Eliteserien]], but he instead joined [[Aalesunds FK|Aalesund]] in 2024, a team who had been relegated from it.<ref name=bola/>

=== Heart of Midlothian ===
On 15 June 2025, Braga joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] for an undisclosed fee, signing a three-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-15 |title=Claudio Braga: Hearts sign Portuguese striker from Norwegian side Aalesunds |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cwyjy87dk06o |access-date=2025-10-21 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Braga became a fan favourite at Heart of Midlothian with 14 goals and three assists in 33 games by April 2026,<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date=17 April 2026 |title=Premiership Team of the Year |url=https://pfascotland.co.uk/premiership-team-of-the-year/ |website=PFA Scotland |location=Glasgow, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=17 April 2026}}</ref> and was named in the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Premiership 12|PFA Scotland Team of the Year]] for [[2025-26 Scottish Premiership|the 2025–26 season]]<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date=17 April 2026 |title=Premiership Team of the Year |url=https://pfascotland.co.uk/premiership-team-of-the-year/ |website=PFA Scotland |location=Glasgow, Scotland |publisher= |access-date=17 April 2026}}</ref> having played a key role in [[2025-26 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|Hearts' title challenge]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Cohen |first=Charlotte |date= |title=How Braga became Hearts fan favourite |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c36r2633e7lo |work=BBC Sport Scotland |location=Glasgow, Scotland |publisher=BBC |access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref> Braga also won the 2025–26 [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year]] for his performances with the club, becoming the first Portuguese player to win the award.<ref name="PFA Scotland">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/crmpn0vn8ymo |title=Hearts trio pick up PFA Scotland prizes |website=BBC Sport |date=4 May 2026 |accessdate=4 May 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Braga plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] and is right-footed. Prior to signing for the club in July 2025, [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] newspaper ''Hearts Standard'' described him as a "versatile and multi-faceted forward who can play off the left or through the middle".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heartsstandard.co.uk/news/25222983.hearts-eye-portuguese-forward-make-top-target/|title=Hearts eye Portuguese forward and make him top target|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=Hearts Standard|date=8 June 2025|access-date=24 June 2025}}</ref>

'''Sabah Kerjota''' (born 14 August 2001) is an Albanian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{Soccerway}}</ref>

==Club career==
As a youth player, Kerjota joined the [[youth academy]] of Albanian side [[KF Vllaznia|Vllaznia]]. In 2018, he signed for Italian side [[ASD Narnese Calcio|Narnese]], before signing Clitunno in 2019, where he made twenty-two league appearances and scored fifteen goals. One year later, he signed for [[SSC Ancona ASD|Ancona]]. Subsequently, he signed for Montefano in 2021. 

Following his stint there, he signed for Vigor Senigallia in 2022, where he made sixty-nine league appearances and scored nineteen goals. Italian newspaper ''[[il Resto del Carlino]]'' wrote in 2025 that "in his first season [with the club], his play was eye-catching, so much so that he was named the Best Young Player in [[Serie D]] for the [[2022–23 Serie D|2022–23]] season, with nine goals and thirteen assists".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ilrestodelcarlino.it/ancona/cronaca/vigor-ce-lex-kerjota-sulla-306934ab|title=Vigor, c’è l’ex Kerjota sulla strada del riscatto|trans-title=Vigor, former Kerjota on the road to redemption|publisher=[[il Resto del Carlino]]|date=28 March 2025|access-date=24 July 2025}}</ref>

During the summer of 2024, he signed for [[AS Sambenedettese|Sambenedettese]], where he made thirty-six league appearances and scored ten goals and helped the club achieve [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] to [[Serie C]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.valleumbrasport.it/dalla-clitunno-alla-serie-a-scozzese-lincredibile-favola-di-sabah-kerjota/|title=Dalla Clitunno alla serie A scozzese, l’incredibile favola di Sabah Kerjota|trans-title=From Clitunno to the Scottish Serie A, the incredible tale of Sabah Kerjota|language=it|publisher=ValleUmbraSport|date=8 July 2025|access-date=24 July 2025}}</ref> 

Ahead of the [[2025–26 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2025–26 season]], he signed for Scottish side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/kerjota-joins-hearts|title=Kerjota Joins Hearts|work=heartsfc.co.uk|publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] |date=22 July 2025 |accessdate=22 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-transfer-done-as-six-figure-signing-completes-his-move-to-tynecastle-5235091|title=Hearts transfer done as six-figure signing completes his move to Tynecastle|work=edinburghnews.scotsman.com|publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=22 July 2025 |accessdate=22 July 2025}}</ref> Memorably, he set up a last minute winner over [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in his first [[Edinburgh derby]], having been on the pitch for only ten minutes.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coyle |first=Andy |date=2025-10-04 |title=Late Craig Halkett strike gives Hearts win over Hibs in Edinburgh derby |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/hearts-v-hibs-late-craig-halkett-goal-gives-premiership-leaders-1-0-win |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=STV News |language=en-GB}}</ref> He also contributed with two assists when Hearts came from behind to beat Hibs 2–1 at Easter Road.

==International career==
On 19 September 2026, [[Rolando Maran]] called Kerjota up to the senior [[Albania national football team|Albanian national team]] for a set of [[2026–27 UEFA Nations League]] matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fshf.org/sq/trajneri-maran-shpall-listen-me-29-lojtaret-e-grumbulluar-per-4-ndeshjet-e-uefa-nations-league/|title=Trajneri Maran shpall listën me 29 lojtarët e grumbulluar për 4 ndeshjet e UEFA Nations League|date=19 September 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kerjota was born on 14 August 2001 in [[Shkodër]], Albania.

'''Tómas Bent Magnússon''' (born 14 August 2002) is an Icelandic professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. He previously played for Icelandic sides [[ÍBV men's football|ÍBV]] and [[Valur (men's football)|Valur]] and was a youth player at [[Fylkir]].

==Early life==
Tómas was born on 14 August 2002 in [[Iceland]]. The cousin of Icelandic footballer [[Guðjón Ernir Hrafnkelsson]], he is a native of the [[Vestmannaeyjar]], Iceland.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fotbolti.net/news/29-04-2024/hin-hlidin-tomas-bent-magnusson-ibv|title=Hin hliðin - Tómas Bent Magnússon (ÍBV)|trans-title=The Other Side - Tómas Bent Magnússon (ÍBV)|language=is|publisher=[[Fótbolti.net]]|date=29 April 2024|access-date=6 August 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
As a youth player, Tómas joined the [[youth academy]] of [[Fylkir]]. In 2012, he joined the youth academy of [[ÍBV men's football|ÍBV]] and was promoted to the club's senior team in 2019, where he made eighty-one league appearances and scored nine goals and helped them achieve [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] from the [[1. deild karla (football)|second tier]] to the [[Besta deild karla|top flight]].  The same year, he was sent on loan to KFS, where he made nine league appearances and scored two goals. 

Following his stint there, he signed for [[Valur (men's football)|Valur]] ahead of the [[2025 Besta deild karla|2025 season]], where he made ten league appearances and scored two goals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/t-mas-magn-sson/553885/|title=Tómas Bent Magnússon|access-date=19 August 2025}}</ref>  Icelandic newspaper ''[[Morgunblaðið]]'' wrote in 2025 that he "played a key role for Valur" while playing for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mbl.is/sport/efstadeild/2025/08/04/engin_oskastada_fyrir_val/|title="Engin óskastaða" fyrir Val|trans-title="No preference" for Val|language=is|publisher=[[Morgunblaðið]]|date=4 August 2025|access-date=6 August 2025}}</ref> 

During the summer of 2025, he signed for Scottish side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c98l4q84693o |title=Magnusson will bring 'height & aggression' to Hearts |website=BBC Sport |date=4 August 2025 |accessdate=4 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/magnusson-is-maroon|title=Magnússon is Maroon|work=heartsfc.co.uk|publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] |date=4 August 2025 |accessdate=4 August 2025}}</ref> On 10 February 2026, he scored the winning goal in a 1-0 derby victory over Hearts' [[Edinburgh derby|city rivals]] Hibernian.

'''Pierre Landry Kaboré''' (born 5 July 2001) is a Burkinabé professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] or [[Forward (association football)|forward]]. He has also represented [[Burkina Faso national football team|Burkina Faso]] at international level.

Kaboré previously played for [[ASF Bobo Dioulasso|ASF Bobo]], [[Salitas FC|Salitas]], [[AS SONABEL]], SOL and [[JK Narva Trans|Narva Trans]].

==Club career==
Kaboré started his career with Burkinabé side [[ASF Bobo Dioulasso|ASF Bobo]]. Following his stint there, he signed for [[Salitas FC|Salitas]] in 2021. One year later, he signed for [[AS SONABEL]]. Subsequently, he signed for Ivorian side SOL in 2022.

Ahead of the [[2024 Meistriliiga|2024 season]], he signed for Estonian side [[JK Narva Trans|Narva Trans]]. Burkinabé news website ''226foot.com'' wrote in 2025 that he was a "has been a key figure for his side" while playing for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://226foot.com/les-chiffres-impressionnants-de-pierre-landry-Kaboré-au-jk-trans-narva-cette-saison/|title=Les chiffres impressionnants de Pierre Landry Kaboré au JK Trans Narva cette saison|trans-title=Pierre Landry Kaboré's impressive numbers at JK Trans Narva this season|language=fr|publisher=226foot.com|date=21 May 2025|access-date=7 August 2025}}</ref>

In August 2025, he signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c620jerndwdo |title='Versatile' Kabore's prolonged Hearts move complete |website=BBC Sport |date=6 August 2025 |accessdate=6 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/Kabore-is-a-jambo|title=Kabore is a Jambo|work=heartsfc.co.uk|publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] |date=6 August 2025 |accessdate=6 August 2025}}</ref> He scored his first two goals for Hearts in a 4-0 victory over Dundee.

==International career==
Kaboré is a Burkina Faso international. On 2 June 2025, he debuted for the [[Burkina Faso national football team]] during a 0–2 away [[Exhibition match|friendly]] loss to the [[Tunisia national football team]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fasozine.com/5-choses-a-savoir-sur-pierre-landry-Kaboré/|title=5 Choses à savoir sur Pierre Landry Kaboré|trans-title=5 Things to Know About Pierre Landry Kaboré|language=fr|publisher={{ill|FasoZine|fr}}|date=23 May 2025|access-date=7 August 2025}}</ref> On 12 October 2025, he scored his first international goals by netting a hat-trick in a 3–1 win over [[Ethiopia national football team|Ethiopia]] during the [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (CAF)|2026 FIFA World Cup qualification]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/687130/ethiopia-burkina-faso |title=Burkina Faso 3–1 Ethiopia |publisher=ESPN |date=12 October 2025 }}</ref>

'''Eduardo Ageu Almeida Santos''' (born 20 February 2002), commonly known as '''Eduardo Ageu''' or simply '''Ageu''', is a Brazilian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] as a [[midfielder]].

Ageu started his career as a youth for [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]], before transferring to [[C.D. Santa Clara|Santa Clara]] and subsequently joining [[F.C. Alverca|Alverca]] on loan. At the time of his transfer to [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], his transfer fee broke a club record.

==Career==
Ageu began his senior career with [[C.D. Santa Clara|Santa Clara]] in Portugal in 2023, having previously been part of the youth system at Brazilian club [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]]. In 2024, he was loaned to Portuguese second-tier club [[F.C. Alverca|Alverca]], where he impressed with 11 goal contributions across the season and helped the team achieve promotion.<ref name="BBC-Hearts-signing">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cj6yjkl7ngko|title=Ageu: Hearts sign Brazilian midfielder from Santa Clara|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 August 2025|access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref>

On 29 August 2025, Ageu signed for Scottish Premiership side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on a four-year contract, in a move reported to be a club-record transfer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-transfer-news-ageu-brazilian-midfielder-santa-clara-portugal-5294005|title=Hearts sign Ageu from Santa Clara in record deal|publisher=Edinburgh Evening News|date=29 August 2025|access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref> He made his debut a day later, as a substitute in a 1–2 away victory against [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] at [[Almondvale Stadium|Almondvale]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Cohen |first=Charlotte |date=30 August 2025 |title=Livingston 1-2 Hearts |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c1le1nnel1jt |work=BBC Sport Scotland |location=Glasgow, Scotland |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=4 September 2025}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Ageu primarily plays as a central midfielder but can also operate as an attacking midfielder or from the left. He is known for his vision, creativity, and ability to break defensive lines with incisive passing. His performances at Alverca were widely praised for their consistency and flair.<ref name="BBC-Hearts-signing" />

'''Jordi Altena''' (born 4 December 2003) is a Dutch professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]], [[midfielder]] or [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].

==Early life==
Altena was born on 4 December 2003. Born in the [[Netherlands]], he is a native of [[Sleeuwijk]] in [[North Brabant]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ad.nl/altena/een-jaar-knallen-dan-breng-ik-je-terug-naar-betaald-voetbal-hoe-zijn-de-treffers-coach-bijdroeg-aan-de-carriere-van-jordi-altena~a2eb999c/|title='Eén jaar knallen, dan breng ik je terug naar betaald voetbal': hoe zijn De Treffers-coach bijdroeg aan de carrière van Jordi Altena|trans-title='One year of hard work, then I'll bring you back to professional football': how his De Treffers coach contributed to Jordi Altena's career|language=nl|publisher=[[Algemeen Dagblad]]|date=30 December 2025|access-date=5 January 2026}}</ref>

==Career==
As a youth player, Nieling joined the [[youth academy]] of Dutch side {{ill|VV Sleeuwijk|nl}}. Following his stint there, he joined the youth academy of Dutch side [[FC Dordrecht]] in 2014. Four years later, he joined the youth academy of Dutch side [[SBV Vitesse]] and was promoted to the club's senior team in 2023, where he made two league appearances and scored zero goals.<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|jordi-altena}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2024–25 Tweede Divisie|2024–25 season]], he signed for Dutch side [[De Treffers]], where he made twenty-seven league appearances and scored three goals. During the summer of 2025, he signed for Dutch side [[RKC Waalwijk]], where he made twenty-one league appearances and scored two goals. Six months later, he signed for Scottish side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] after receiving interest from American side [[D.C. United]] and Spanish side [[Real Valladolid]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/jordi-altena-transfer-interest-ignored-beautiful-hearts-a-crazy-journey-and-derek-mcinnes-message-5461687|title=Jordi Altena: Transfer interest ignored, beautiful Hearts, a crazy journey and Derek McInnes' message|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]]|date=4 January 2026|access-date=5 January 2026}}</ref>

'''Alexander Briedl''' (born 21 April 2002) is an Austrian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]. 

==Club career==
As a youth player, Briedl joined the [[youth academy]] of Austrian side [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]] and was promoted to the club's senior team in 2020, where he made zero league appearances and scored zero goals. The same year, he was sent on loan to Austrian side [[USK Anif]]. Following his stint there, he signed for Austrian side [[SV Horn]] in 2021, where he made thirty-three league appearances and scored zero goals. 

One year later, he signed for Austrian side [[FC Blau-Weiß Linz]], where he made ninety-three league appearances and scored three goals and helped the club achieve [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] from the [[2. Liga (Austria)|second tier]] to the [[Austrian Football Bundesliga|top flight]]. Austrian news website ''[[Laola1]]'' wrote in 2024 that he "made an immediate impact in the Bundesliga and has been a regular starter" while playing for them.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.laola1.at/de/red/fussball/bundesliga/diashows/das-sind-die-gewinner-der-bundesliga-saison-2023-24/?page=27|title=Das sind die Gewinner der Bundesliga-Saison 2023/24|trans-title=Das sind die Gewinner der Bundesliga-Saison 2023/24|language=de|publisher=[[Laola1]]|date=29 May 2024|access-date=1 June 2026}}</ref> During the summer of 2023, he was sent on loan to Austrian side [[SV Wallern]], where he made five league ppearances and scored zero goals. Ahead of the [[2026–27 Scottish Premiership|2026–27 season]], he signed for Scottish side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|alexander-briedl}}</ref>

==International career==
Briedl is an Austria youth international. On 7 June 2024, he debuted for the [[Austria national under-21 football team]] during a 5–0 [[Home (sports)|home]] [[Exhibition match|friendly]] win over the [[Scotland national under-21 football team]].

==Style of play==
Briedl plays as a [[midfielder]]. Left-footed, he is known for his pressing ability.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/7029224/aberdeen-fc-new-signing-alexander-briedl-target/|title=New Aberdeen signing Alexander Briedl reveals key career target after moving to Pittodrie|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[The Press and Journal]]|date=29 May 2026|access-date=1 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Severin Sabri Guendouz''' (born 9 February 2000) is a French professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], as a [[midfielder]], [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] or [[Forward (association football)|forward]].

==Career==
As a youth player, Guendouz joined the [[youth academy]] of French side [[Valenciennes FC]] and was promoted to the club's [[reserve team]] in 2019, where he made sixteen league appearances and scored two goals. Following his stint there, he signed for the reserve team of French side [[En Avant Guingamp]] in 2020 and was promoted to the club's senior team in 2024, where he made twenty league appearances and scored zero goals. 

During the summer of 2025, he signed for Belgian side [[K Beerschot VA]], where he made thirty-one league appearances and scored three goals. Ahead of the [[2026–27 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2026–27 season]], he signed for Scottish side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/sabri-signs|title=Sabri Signs|work=heartsfc.co.uk|publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] |date=24 June 2026|accessdate=24 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cn4rl8edlreo|title=Hearts buy 'direct' forward Guendouz from Beerschot|work=bbc.co.uk|publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=24 June 2026 |accessdate=28 June 2026}}</ref>
==Style of play==
Guendouz plays as a [[midfielder]], [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] or [[Forward (association football)|forward]]. Two-footed, he is known for his speed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/ea-guingamp/ea-guingamp-sabri-guendouz-a-letroit-en-n2-e8b4069e-f348-11ee-9bee-6b4d91ded6b2|title=Sabri Guendouz, à l’étroit en N2?|trans-title=Is Sabri Guendouz feeling out of place in N2?|language=fr|publisher=[[Ouest-France]]|date=5 April 2024|access-date=26 June 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Guendouz was born on 9 February 2000. Born in Cambrai [[France]], he has been married.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c8j2m27pp91o|title=Guendouz targets title and Champions League on joining Hearts|trans-title=|language=en|work=bbc.co.uk|publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=24 June 2026|access-date=26 June 2026}}</ref>
