'''Tom Renaud ''' (born 19 November 2000) is a French professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|HeartofM}} side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. Renaud began his career as youth with [[FC Lorient]] and subsequently played for [[SO Cholet|Cholet]] and [[FC Versailles 78|FC Versailles]].

==Early life==
Renaud was born on 19 November 2000 in [[Ploemeur]], France. Growing up, he started playing football at the age of five.<ref name="fr">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/morbihan/tom-renaud-creuse-son-sillon-au-fcl-5683168|title=Tom Renaud creuse son sillon au FCL|trans-title=Tom Renaud is making his mark at FCL|language=fr|publisher=[[Ouest-France]]|date=7 April 2018|access-date=26 June 2026}}</ref>

==Career==
As a youth player, Renaud joined the [[youth academy]] of French side [[FC Lorient|Lorient]] and was promoted to the club's [[reserve team]] in 2016, where he made thirty-eight league appearances and scored one goal. Following his stint there, he signed for French side [[SO Cholet|Cholet]] in 2020, where he made sixty league appearances and scored five goals. 

During the summer of 2024, Renaud signed for French side [[FC Versailles 78|Versailles]], where he made fifty-four league appearances and scored zero goals and helped the club achieve fifth place in the [[Ligue 3|league]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/clyr1p755l1o|title='Maestro of Versailles' Renaud pulls into Hearts|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=24 June 2026|access-date=26 June 2026}}</ref> 

Ahead of the [[2026–27 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2026–27 season]], Renaud signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] on a four year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/renaud-joins-the-jambos|title=Renaud Joins the Jambos|work=heartsfc.co.uk|publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]|date=24 June 2026|accessdate=24 June 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828114414/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/renaud-joins-the-jambos|archive-date=28 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> He made his debut for the club, coming on as a 75th-minute substitute, in a 4-0 loss against [[SK Sturm Graz|Sturm Graz]] in the first leg of the [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League qualifying#Second_qualifying_round|UEFA Champions League's second qualifying round]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-sturm-graz-4-0-heart-of-midlothian|title=Match Report: Sturm Graz 4-0 Heart of Midlothian|website=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=21 July 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828071745/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-sturm-graz-4-0-heart-of-midlothian|archive-date=28 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Renaud scored his first goal for Hearts when he "latched on to possession before expertly sending a low drive into [[Samuel Soares]]’ bottom right corner to pull one back, in a 6-1 loss against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in [[2026–27_UEFA_Europa_League_qualifying#Third_qualifying_round|the first leg of the UEFA Europa League third qualifying round]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-benfica-6-1-hearts|title=Match Report: Benfica 6-1 Hearts|website=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=6 August 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828073316/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-benfica-6-1-hearts|archive-date=28 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Renaud scored his first league goal for the club, in a 4-0 win against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on 8 August 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-hearts-4-0-dundee-utd|title=Match Report: Hearts 4-0 Dundee Utd|website=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=9 August 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828073223/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-hearts-4-0-dundee-utd|archive-date=28 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> However, in the return leg against [[SK Rapid Wien|Rapid Wien]] in the [[2026–27 UEFA_Conference League#Play-off_round|play-off round of UEFA Conference League]], he suffered ankle injury and substituted in the 15th minute, as Hearts went on to win 4-3 on penalties following a 2-2 draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-sk-rapid-2-2-hearts-3-4p|title=Match Report: SK Rapid 2-2 Hearts (3-4p)|website=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=26 August 2026|access-date=28 August 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828073436/https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/blogs/news/match-report-sk-rapid-2-2-hearts-3-4p|archive-date=28 August 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Renaud plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] or [[midfielder]]. French newspaper ''[[Ouest-France]]'' wrote in 2018 "initially a striker, then a central defender, he ultimately found his niche as a defensive midfielder".<ref name="fr"/>

'''Ayoub Mouloua''' ({{langx|ar|أيوب مولوع}}; born 30 September 2002) is a Moroccan professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]. 

==Early life==
Mouloua was born on 30 September 2002. Born in [[Morocco]], he is a native of [[Oujda]], Morocco.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sport.le360.ma/football/ayoub-mouloua-une-etoile-est-nee-parmi-les-lionceaux-83562/|title=Ayoub Mouloua: une étoile est née parmi les Lionceaux|trans-title=Ayoub Mouloua: a star is born among the Lion Cubs|language=fr|publisher=[[Le360]]|date=23 February 2023|access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref>

==Club career==
As a youth player, Mouloua joined the [[youth academy]] of Moroccan side [[Fath Union Sport|FUS]] and was promoted to the club's senior team in 2021, where he made fifty league appearances and scored seventeen goals. Following his stint there, he signed for Scottish side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] ahead of the [[2026–27 Aberdeen F.C. season|2026–27 season]].<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|ayoub-mouloua}}</ref> 

==International career==
Mouloua is a Morocco A' international. During the summer of 2025, he played for the [[Morocco A' national football team]] at the [[2024 African Nations Championship]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/7049282/aberdeen-fc-ayoub-mouloua-long-term-deal/|title=Ayoub Mouloua joins Aberdeen on long-term deal: Stephen Robinson gives lowdown on new striker|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[The Press and Journal]]|date=28 June 2026|access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Aron Benjaminsen''' (born 2 November 2007) is a [[Faroese people|Faroese]] professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] and the [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands national team]].

Benjaminsen began his career as a youth at local side [[Skála ÍF]] and Norwegian side [[Kristiansund BK|Kristiansund 2]], before returning to the Faroe Islands to sign for [[Víkingur Gøta|Víkingur]]. He has previously represented the [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]] at [[Faroe Islands national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[Faroe Islands national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Faroe Islands national under-21 football team|under-21]] level.

==Early life==
Benjaminsen was born on 2 November 2007 in the [[Faroe Islands]]. He is the son of [[Fróði Benjaminsen]] and the cousin of [[Árni Frederiksberg]], themselves both [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]] national footballers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bolt.fo/news/details?title=Systkinab%C3%B8rn%20bresta%20saman:%20%C3%81rni%20Frederiksberg%20m%C3%B3ti%20Aroni%20Benjaminsen&id=10822|title=Systkinabørn bresta saman: Árni Frederiksberg móti Aroni Benjaminsen|trans-title=|language=fo|publisher=Bolt.fo|date=18 June 2026|access-date=4 September 2026}}</ref>

==Club career==
As a youth player, Benjaminsen joined the [[youth academy]] of [[Skála ÍF|Skála]]. Following his stint there, he signed for Norwegian side [[Kristiansund BK|Kristiansund]] at the age of sixteen and played for the club's [[reserve team]], where he made forty-two league appearances and scored five goals. 

Ahead of the 2026 Faroese season, he signed for [[Víkingur Gøta|Víkingur]], where he played in the [[UEFA Conference League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://in.fo/news-detail/hetta-er-elddopurin-hja-aroni-og-josefi|title=Hetta er elddópurin hjá Aroni og Jósefi|trans-title=This is the baptism of fire with Aron and Josef|language=fo|publisher=[[Sosialurin]]|date=9 July 2026|access-date=4 September 2026}}</ref> On 13 March 2026, he first started for the club during a 0–0 [[Home (sports)|home]] draw with [[B36 Tórshavn|B36]] in the [[Faroe Islands Premier League|league]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dimma.fo/grein/aron-droymir-framvegis-um-at-spaela-uttanlands|title=Aron droymir framvegis um at spæla uttanlands|trans-title=
Aron still dreams of playing abroad|language=fo|publisher=[[Dimmalætting]]|date=|access-date=4 September 2026}}</ref> and went on to make twenty league appearances and score seven goals while playing for them. In September 2026, he signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref name="world">{{WorldFootball.net|new_id=pe883552}}</ref>

==International career==
Benjaminsen is a Faroe Islands international and has represented his country at youth level. Altogether, he made eighteen appearances and scored four goals while playing for the [[Faroe Islands national under-17 football team]] and eight appearances and scored two goals while playing for the [[Faroe Islands national under-19 football team]]. 

At the age of seventeen, he debuted for the [[Faroe Islands national under-21 football team]]. During June, September and October 2025 and March 2026, he played for the [[Faroe Islands national under-21 football team]] for [[2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]].<ref name="world"/>

On 29 September 2026, Benjaminsen made his debut for the [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands national team]] in a [[2026–27 UEFA Nations League C]] game against Moldova.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=ESPN|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/401861090/faroe-islands-moldova|title=Moldova 1-1 Faroe Islands (29 Sep, 2026) Final Score - ESPN (UK)|date=29 September 2026|access-date=12 October 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Benjaminsen plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]]. Left-footed, he is known for his dribbling ability<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bolt.fo/news/details?title=Scouting-%20og%20rekrutteringarlei%C3%B0arin%20hj%C3%A1%20Viborg%20s%C3%A1%20Aron%20v%C3%ADsa%20st%C3%B3rsp%C3%A6l&id=10735|title=Scouting- og rekrutteringarleiðarin hjá Viborg sá Aron vísa stórspæl|trans-title=Viborg's scouting and recruitment manager saw Aron show great play|language=fo|publisher=Bolt.fo|date=22 May 2026|access-date=4 September 2026}}</ref> and  received comparisons to [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] international [[Xherdan Shaqiri]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heartsstandard.co.uk/news/26511388.hearts-new-boy-son-legend-possesses-x-factor/|title=Hearts new boy is the son of a legend and why he possesses an X-factor|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=Hearts Standard|date=2 September 2026|access-date=4 September 2026}}</ref>

Scottish newspaper ''[[Edinburgh Evening News]]'' wrote in 2026 that he "[was] regarded as one of his country's most promising emerging talents. He is predominantly a right-sided wide player but can also operate on the left. He is known for drifting into the penalty area to get on the end of crosses and his finishing prowess earned him a big reputation in his homeland".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-sign-aron-benjaminsen-on-a-huge-contract-with-more-transfers-to-come-8951639|title=Hearts sign Aron Benjaminsen on a huge contract with more transfers to come|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]]|date=2 September 2026|access-date=4 September 2026}}</ref>
